1.1.s: Evaṁ me sutaṁ— ekaṁ samayaṁ bhagavā sāvatthiyaṁ viharati jetavane anāthapiṇḍikassa ārāme.
1.1.e: So I have heard. At one time the Buddha was staying near Sāvatthī in Jeta’s Grove, Anāthapiṇḍika’s monastery.

1.1.s: Atha kho aññatarā devatā abhikkantāya rattiyā abhikkantavaṇṇā kevalakappaṁ jetavanaṁ obhāsetvā yena bhagavā tenupasaṅkami; upasaṅkamitvā bhagavantaṁ abhivādetvā ekamantaṁ aṭṭhāsi. Ekamantaṁ ṭhitā kho sā devatā bhagavantaṁ etadavoca: “kathaṁ nu tvaṁ, mārisa, oghamatarī”ti?
1.1.e: Then, late at night, a glorious deity, lighting up the entire Jeta’s Grove, went up to the Buddha, bowed, stood to one side, and said to him, “Good fellow, how did you cross the flood?”
“Neither standing nor swimming, respectable sir, I crossed the flood.”

1.1.s: “Yathākathaṁ pana tvaṁ, mārisa, appatiṭṭhaṁ anāyūhaṁ oghamatarī”ti?
1.1.e: “But in what way did you cross the flood neither standing nor swimming?”

1.1.s: “Yadāsvāhaṁ, āvuso, santiṭṭhāmi tadāssu saṁsīdāmi; yadāsvāhaṁ, āvuso, āyūhāmi tadāssu nibbuyhāmi. Evaṁ khvāhaṁ, āvuso, appatiṭṭhaṁ anāyūhaṁ oghamatarin”ti.
1.1.e: “When I stood, I sank under. When I swam, I was swept away. That’s how I crossed the flood neither standing nor swimming.”

1.1.s:
“Cirassaṁ vata passāmi,
brāhmaṇaṁ parinibbutaṁ;
Appatiṭṭhaṁ anāyūhaṁ,
tiṇṇaṁ loke visattikan”ti.
1.1.e:
“After a long time I see
a brahmin fully quenched.
Neither standing nor swimming,
he’s crossed over clinging to the world.”

1.1.s: Idamavoca sā devatā. Samanuñño satthā ahosi. Atha kho sā devatā: “samanuñño me satthā”ti bhagavantaṁ abhivādetvā padakkhiṇaṁ katvā tatthevantaradhāyīti.
1.1.e: That is what that deity said, and the Teacher concurred. Then that deity, knowing that the Teacher concurred, bowed and respectfully circled the Buddha, keeping him on his right, before vanishing right there.

1.2.s: Atha kho aññatarā devatā abhikkantāya rattiyā abhikkantavaṇṇā kevalakappaṁ jetavanaṁ obhāsetvā yena bhagavā tenupasaṅkami; upasaṅkamitvā bhagavantaṁ abhivādetvā ekamantaṁ aṭṭhāsi. Ekamantaṁ ṭhitā kho sā devatā bhagavantaṁ etadavoca: “Jānāsi no tvaṁ, mārisa, sattānaṁ nimokkhaṁ pamokkhaṁ vivekan”ti?
1.2.e: Then, late at night, a glorious deity, lighting up the entire Jeta’s Grove, went up to the Buddha, bowed, stood to one side, and said to him, “Good fellow, do you know the liberation, emancipation, and seclusion of sentient beings?”

1.2.s: “Jānāmi khvāhaṁ, āvuso, sattānaṁ nimokkhaṁ pamokkhaṁ vivekan”ti.
“Yathākathaṁ pana tvaṁ, mārisa, jānāsi sattānaṁ nimokkhaṁ pamokkhaṁ vivekan”ti?
1.2.e: “But how is it that you know the liberation, emancipation, and seclusion of sentient beings?”

1.2.s: “Nandībhavaparikkhayā, Saññāviññāṇasaṅkhayā; Vedanānaṁ nirodhā upasamā, Evaṁ khvāhaṁ āvuso jānāmi; Sattānaṁ nimokkhaṁ pamokkhaṁ vivekan”ti.
1.2.e: “Due to the ending of relish for rebirth; due to the finishing of perception and consciousness; due to the cessation and stilling of feelings— that, respectable sir, is how I know the liberation, emancipation, and seclusion of sentient beings.”

1.3.s: Ekamantaṁ ṭhitā kho sā devatā bhagavato santike imaṁ gāthaṁ abhāsi:
1.3.e: Standing to one side, that deity spoke this verse in the Buddha’s presence:

1.3.s:
“Upanīyati jīvitamappamāyu,
Jarūpanītassa na santi tāṇā;
Etaṁ bhayaṁ maraṇe pekkhamāno,
Puññāni kayirātha sukhāvahānī”ti.
1.3.e:
“This life, so very short, is led onward.
One led on to old age has no shelter.
Seeing this peril in death,
do good deeds that bring you joy.”

1.3.s:
“Upanīyati jīvitamappamāyu,
Jarūpanītassa na santi tāṇā;
Etaṁ bhayaṁ maraṇe pekkhamāno,
Lokāmisaṁ pajahe santipekkho”ti.
1.3.e:
“This life, so very short, is led onward.
One led on to old age has no shelter.
Seeing this peril in death,
a seeker of peace would drop the world’s bait.”

1.4.s: Ekamantaṁ ṭhitā kho sā devatā bhagavato santike imaṁ gāthaṁ abhāsi:
1.4.e: Standing to one side, that deity spoke this verse in the Buddha’s presence:

1.4.s:
“Accenti kālā tarayanti rattiyo,
Vayoguṇā anupubbaṁ jahanti;
Etaṁ bhayaṁ maraṇe pekkhamāno,
Puññāni kayirātha sukhāvahānī”ti.
1.4.e:
“Time flies, nights pass by,
the stages of life leave us one by one.
Seeing this peril in death,
do good deeds that bring you joy.”

1.4.s:
“Accenti kālā tarayanti rattiyo,
Vayoguṇā anupubbaṁ jahanti;
Etaṁ bhayaṁ maraṇe pekkhamāno,
Lokāmisaṁ pajahe santipekkho”ti.
1.4.e:
“Time flies, nights pass by,
the stages of life leave us one by one.
Seeing this peril in death,
a seeker of peace would drop the world’s bait.”

1.5.s: Ekamantaṁ ṭhitā kho sā devatā bhagavato santike imaṁ gāthaṁ abhāsi:
1.5.e: Standing to one side, that deity spoke this verse in the Buddha’s presence:

1.5.s:
“Kati chinde kati jahe,
kati cuttari bhāvaye;
Kati saṅgātigo bhikkhu,
oghatiṇṇoti vuccatī”ti.
1.5.e:
“Cut how many? Drop how many?
Develop how many more?
When a mendicant slips how many chains
are they said to have crossed the flood?”

1.5.s:
“Pañca chinde pañca jahe,
pañca cuttari bhāvaye;
Pañca saṅgātigo bhikkhu,
oghatiṇṇoti vuccatī”ti.
1.5.e:
“Five to cut, five to drop,
and five more to develop.
When a mendicant slips five chains
they’re said to have crossed the flood.”

1.6.s: Ekamantaṁ ṭhitā kho sā devatā bhagavato santike imaṁ gāthaṁ abhāsi:
1.6.e: Standing to one side, that deity spoke this verse in the Buddha’s presence:

1.6.s:
“Kati jāgarataṁ suttā,
kati suttesu jāgarā;
Katibhi rajamādeti,
katibhi parisujjhatī”ti.
1.6.e:
“How many sleep among the waking?
How many wake among the sleeping?
By how many do you gather dust?
By how many are you cleansed?”

1.6.s:
“Pañca jāgarataṁ suttā,
pañca suttesu jāgarā;
Pañcabhi rajamādeti,
pañcabhi parisujjhatī”ti.
1.6.e:
“Five sleep among the waking.
Five wake among the sleeping.
By five you gather dust.
By five you’re cleansed.”

1.7.s: Ekamantaṁ ṭhitā kho sā devatā bhagavato santike imaṁ gāthaṁ abhāsi:
1.7.e: Standing to one side, that deity spoke this verse in the Buddha’s presence:

1.7.s:
“Yesaṁ dhammā appaṭividitā,
Paravādesu nīyare;
Suttā te nappabujjhanti,
Kālo tesaṁ pabujjhitun”ti.
1.7.e:
“Those have not deciphered the teachings
may be led astray by the doctrines of others.
Asleep, they have not woken up:
it is time for them to wake!”

1.7.s:
“Yesaṁ dhammā suppaṭividitā,
Paravādesu na nīyare;
Te sambuddhā sammadaññā,
Caranti visame saman”ti.
1.7.e:
“Those who have well deciphered the teachings
won’t be led astray by the doctrines of others.
They have woken up, they rightly know,
smoothly they walk in the rough.”

1.8.s: Ekamantaṁ ṭhitā kho sā devatā bhagavato santike imaṁ gāthaṁ abhāsi:
1.8.e: Standing to one side, that deity spoke this verse in the Buddha’s presence:

1.8.s:
“Yesaṁ dhammā susammuṭṭhā,
paravādesu nīyare;
Suttā te nappabujjhanti,
kālo tesaṁ pabujjhitun”ti.
1.8.e:
“Those who are very confused about the teachings
may be led astray by the doctrines of others.
Asleep, they have not woken up:
it is time for them to wake!”

1.8.s:
“Yesaṁ dhammā asammuṭṭhā,
paravādesu na nīyare;
Te sambuddhā sammadaññā,
caranti visame saman”ti.
1.8.e:
“Those who are unconfused about the teachings,
won’t be led astray by the doctrines of others.
They have woken up, they rightly know,
smoothly they walk in the rough.”

1.9.s: Ekamantaṁ ṭhitā kho sā devatā bhagavato santike imaṁ gāthaṁ abhāsi:
1.9.e: Standing to one side, that deity spoke this verse in the Buddha’s presence:

1.9.s:
“Na mānakāmassa damo idhatthi,
Na monamatthi asamāhitassa;
Eko araññe viharaṁ pamatto,
Na maccudheyyassa tareyya pāran”ti.
1.9.e:
“One fond of conceit can’t be tamed,
no sage is lacking immersion.
Living negligent alone in the wilderness,
they can’t cross beyond Death’s dominion.”

1.9.s:
“Mānaṁ pahāya susamāhitatto,
Sucetaso sabbadhi vippamutto;
Eko araññe viharaṁ appamatto,
Sa maccudheyyassa tareyya pāran”ti.
1.9.e:
“Having given up conceit, serene within oneself,
with a good heart, everywhere free;
living diligent alone in the wilderness,
they cross beyond Death’s dominion.”

1.10.s: Ekamantaṁ ṭhitā kho sā devatā bhagavantaṁ gāthāya ajjhabhāsi:
1.10.e: Standing to one side, that deity addressed the Buddha in verse:

1.10.s:
“Araññe viharantānaṁ,
santānaṁ brahmacārinaṁ;
Ekabhattaṁ bhuñjamānānaṁ,
kena vaṇṇo pasīdatī”ti.
1.10.e:
“Living in the wilderness,
peaceful spiritual practitioners
eat just one meal a day:
so why is their complexion so clear?”

1.10.s:
“Atītaṁ nānusocanti,
nappajappanti nāgataṁ;
Paccuppannena yāpenti,
tena vaṇṇo pasīdati.
1.10.e:
“They don’t grieve for the past,
nor do they pray for the future;
they feed on whatever comes that day,
that’s why their complexion’s so clear.

1.10.s:
Anāgatappajappāya,
atītassānusocanā;
Etena bālā sussanti,
naḷova harito luto”ti.
1.10.e:
Because they pray for the future,
and grieve for the past,
fools wither away,
like a green reed mowed down.”

1.11.s: Evaṁ me sutaṁ— ekaṁ samayaṁ bhagavā sāvatthiyaṁ viharati jetavane anāthapiṇḍikassa ārāme. Tatra kho bhagavā bhikkhū āmantesi: “bhikkhavo”ti.
1.11.e: So I have heard. At one time the Buddha was staying near Sāvatthī in Jeta’s Grove, Anāthapiṇḍika’s monastery. There the Buddha addressed the mendicants, “Mendicants!”

1.11.s: “Bhadante”ti te bhikkhū bhagavato paccassosuṁ. Bhagavā etadavoca:
1.11.e: “Venerable sir,” they replied. The Buddha said this:

1.11.s: “Bhūtapubbaṁ, bhikkhave, aññatarā tāvatiṁsakāyikā devatā nandane vane accharāsaṅghaparivutā dibbehi pañcahi kāmaguṇehi samappitā samaṅgībhūtā paricārayamānā tāyaṁ velāyaṁ imaṁ gāthaṁ abhāsi:
1.11.e: “Once upon a time, mendicants, a certain deity of the company of the thirty-three was amusing themselves in the Garden of Delight, escorted by a band of nymphs, and supplied and provided with the five kinds of heavenly sensual stimulation. On that occasion she spoke this verse:

1.11.s:
‘Na te sukhaṁ pajānanti,
ye na passanti nandanaṁ;
Āvāsaṁ naradevānaṁ,
tidasānaṁ yasassinan’ti.
1.11.e:
‘They don’t know pleasure
who don’t see the Garden of Delight!
It’s the abode of lordly gods,
the glorious host of Thirty!’

1.11.s: Evaṁ vutte, bhikkhave, aññatarā devatā taṁ devataṁ gāthāya paccabhāsi:
1.11.e: When they had spoken, another deity replied with this verse:

1.12.s: Ekamantaṁ ṭhitā kho sā devatā bhagavato santike imaṁ gāthaṁ abhāsi:
1.12.e: Standing to one side, that deity spoke this verse in the Buddha’s presence:

1.12.s:
“Nandati puttehi puttimā,
Gomā gohi tatheva nandati;
Upadhīhi narassa nandanā,
Na hi so nandati yo nirūpadhī”ti.
1.12.e:
“Children bring you delight!
Cattle also bring you delight!
For attachments are a man’s delight;
without attachments there’s no delight.”

1.12.s:
“Socati puttehi puttimā,
Gomā gohi tatheva socati;
Upadhīhi narassa socanā,
Na hi so socati yo nirūpadhī”ti.
1.12.e:
“Children bring you sorrow.
Cattle also bring you sorrow.
For attachments are a man’s sorrow;
without attachments there are no sorrows.”

1.13.s: Ekamantaṁ ṭhitā kho sā devatā bhagavato santike imaṁ gāthaṁ abhāsi:
1.13.e: Standing to one side, that deity spoke this verse in the Buddha’s presence:

1.13.s:
“Natthi puttasamaṁ pemaṁ,
natthi gosamitaṁ dhanaṁ;
Natthi sūriyasamā ābhā,
samuddaparamā sarā”ti.
1.13.e:
“There’s no fondness like that for a child,
no wealth equal to cattle,
no light like that of the sun,
and of streams the ocean is paramount.”

1.13.s:
“Natthi attasamaṁ pemaṁ,
natthi dhaññasamaṁ dhanaṁ;
Natthi paññāsamā ābhā,
vuṭṭhi ve paramā sarā”ti.
1.13.e:
“There’s no fondness like that for oneself,
no wealth equal to grain,
no light like that of wisdom,
and of streams the rain is paramount.”

1.14.s:
“Khattiyo dvipadaṁ seṭṭho,
balībaddo catuppadaṁ;
Komārī seṭṭhā bhariyānaṁ,
yo ca puttāna pubbajo”ti.
1.14.e:
“An aristocrat is the best of bipeds,
an ox is the best of quadrupeds,
a maiden is the best of wives,
and a first-born the best of sons.”

1.14.s:
“Sambuddho dvipadaṁ seṭṭho,
ājānīyo catuppadaṁ;
Sussūsā seṭṭhā bhariyānaṁ,
yo ca puttānamassavo”ti.
1.14.e:
“A Buddha is the best of bipeds,
a thoroughbred, the best of quadrupeds,
a good listener is the best of wives,
and the best of sons is loyal.”

1.15.s:
“Ṭhite majjhanhike kāle,
sannisīvesu pakkhisu;
Saṇateva brahāraññaṁ,
taṁ bhayaṁ paṭibhāti man”ti.
1.15.e:
“In the still of high noon,
when the birds have settled down,
the mighty forest itself resounds—
that strikes me as so scary!”

1.15.s:
“Ṭhite majjhanhike kāle,
sannisīvesu pakkhisu;
Saṇateva brahāraññaṁ,
sā rati paṭibhāti man”ti.
1.15.e:
“In the still of high noon,
when the birds have settled down,
the mighty forest itself resounds—
that strikes me as so delightful!”

1.16.s:
“Niddā tandī vijambhitā,
Aratī bhattasammado;
Etena nappakāsati,
Ariyamaggo idha pāṇinan”ti.
1.16.e:
“Sleepiness, sloth, and yawning,
discontent, and grogginess after eating:
because of this the noble path
doesn’t shine for creatures here.”

1.16.s:
“Niddaṁ tandiṁ vijambhitaṁ,
Aratiṁ bhattasammadaṁ;
Vīriyena naṁ paṇāmetvā,
Ariyamaggo visujjhatī”ti.
1.16.e:
“Sleepiness, sloth, and yawning,
discontent, and grogginess after eating:
when this is energetically fended off,
the noble path is purified.”

1.17.s:
“Dukkaraṁ duttitikkhañca,
abyattena ca sāmaññaṁ;
Bahūhi tattha sambādhā,
yattha bālo visīdatī”ti.
1.17.e:
“Hard to do, hard to endure,
is the ascetic life for the inept,
for it has many narrow passes
where the fool founders.”

1.17.s:
“Katihaṁ careyya sāmaññaṁ,
cittañce na nivāraye;
Pade pade visīdeyya,
saṅkappānaṁ vasānugoti.
1.17.e:
“How many days could an ascetic live
without controlling the mind?
They’d founder with each step,
under the sway of thoughts.

1.17.s:
Kummova aṅgāni sake kapāle,
Samodahaṁ bhikkhu manovitakke;
Anissito aññamaheṭhayāno,
Parinibbuto nūpavadeyya kañcī”ti.
1.17.e:
A mendicant should collect their thoughts
as a tortoise draws its limbs into its shell.
Independent, not disturbing others,
quenched: they wouldn’t blame anyone.”

1.18.s:
“Hirīnisedho puriso,
koci lokasmiṁ vijjati;
Yo nindaṁ apabodhati,
asso bhadro kasāmivā”ti.
1.18.e:
“Can a person constrained by conscience
be found in the world,
who is cognizant of blame,
like a fine horse of the whip?”

1.18.s:
“Hirīnisedhā tanuyā,
ye caranti sadā satā;
Antaṁ dukkhassa pappuyya,
caranti visame saman”ti.
1.18.e:
“Few are those constrained by conscience,
who live always mindful.
Having reached the end of suffering,
smoothly they walk in the rough.”

1.19.s:
“Kacci te kuṭikā natthi,
kacci natthi kulāvakā;
Kacci santānakā natthi,
kacci muttosi bandhanā”ti.
1.19.e:
“Don’t you have a little hut?
Don’t you have a little nest?
Don’t you have any networks?
Aren’t you free of shackles?”

1.19.s:
“Taggha me kuṭikā natthi,
taggha natthi kulāvakā;
Taggha santānakā natthi,
taggha muttomhi bandhanā”ti.
1.19.e:
“Indeed I have no little hut.
Indeed I have no little nest.
Indeed I have no networks.
Indeed I’m free from shackles.”

1.19.s:
“Kintāhaṁ kuṭikaṁ brūmi,
kiṁ te brūmi kulāvakaṁ;
Kiṁ te santānakaṁ brūmi,
kintāhaṁ brūmi bandhanan”ti.
1.19.e:
“What do you think I call your little hut?
What do I call your little nest?
What do I call your network?
And what do I call your shackle?”

1.19.s:
“Mātaraṁ kuṭikaṁ brūsi,
bhariyaṁ brūsi kulāvakaṁ;
Putte santānake brūsi,
taṇhaṁ me brūsi bandhanan”ti.
1.19.e:
“You call mother a little hut;
and wife a little nest.
You call children a network,
and you call my craving a shackle.”

1.19.s:
“Sāhu te kuṭikā natthi,
sāhu natthi kulāvakā;
Sāhu santānakā natthi,
sāhu muttosi bandhanā”ti.
1.19.e:
“It’s good you have no little hut!
It’s good you have no little nest!
It’s good you have no networks!
And good that you’re free from shackles.”

1.20.s: Evaṁ me sutaṁ— ekaṁ samayaṁ bhagavā rājagahe viharati tapodārāme.
1.20.e: So I have heard. At one time the Buddha was staying near Rājagaha in the Hot Springs Monastery.

1.20.s: Atha kho āyasmā samiddhi rattiyā paccūsasamayaṁ paccuṭṭhāya yena tapodā tenupasaṅkami gattāni parisiñcituṁ. Tapode gattāni parisiñcitvā paccuttaritvā ekacīvaro aṭṭhāsi gattāni pubbāpayamāno.
1.20.e: Then Venerable Samiddhi rose at the crack of dawn and went to the hot springs to bathe. When he had bathed and emerged from the water he stood in one robe drying his limbs.

1.20.s: Atha kho aññatarā devatā abhikkantāya rattiyā abhikkantavaṇṇā kevalakappaṁ tapodaṁ obhāsetvā yena āyasmā samiddhi tenupasaṅkami; upasaṅkamitvā vehāsaṁ ṭhitā āyasmantaṁ samiddhiṁ gāthāya ajjhabhāsi:
1.20.e: Then, late at night, a glorious deity, lighting up the entire hot springs, went up to Samiddhi, and, standing in the air, addressed him in verse:

1.20.s:
“Abhutvā bhikkhasi bhikkhu,
na hi bhutvāna bhikkhasi;
Bhutvāna bhikkhu bhikkhassu,
mā taṁ kālo upaccagā”ti.
1.20.e:
“Mendicant, you seek alms before you eat;
you don’t seek alms after eating.
But you should eat first, then seek alms:
don’t let the time pass you by.”

1.20.s:
“Kālaṁ vohaṁ na jānāmi,
channo kālo na dissati;
Tasmā abhutvā bhikkhāmi,
mā maṁ kālo upaccagā”ti.
1.20.e:
“I actually don’t know the time;
it’s hidden and unseen.
That’s why I seek alms before eating,
so that the time may not pass me by!”

1.20.s: Atha kho sā devatā pathaviyaṁ patiṭṭhahitvā āyasmantaṁ samiddhiṁ etadavoca: “daharo tvaṁ, bhikkhu, pabbajito susu kāḷakeso, bhadrena yobbanena samannāgato, paṭhamena vayasā, anikkīḷitāvī kāmesu. Bhuñja, bhikkhu, mānusake kāme; mā sandiṭṭhikaṁ hitvā kālikaṁ anudhāvī”ti.
1.20.e: Then that deity landed on the ground and said to Samiddhi, “You’ve gone forth while young, mendicant. With pristine black hair, you’re blessed with youth, in the prime of life, and you’ve never flirted with sensual pleasures. Enjoy human sensual pleasures! Don’t give up what is apparent in the present to chase after what takes effect over time.”

1.20.s: “Na khvāhaṁ, āvuso, sandiṭṭhikaṁ hitvā kālikaṁ anudhāvāmi. Kālikañca khvāhaṁ, āvuso, hitvā sandiṭṭhikaṁ anudhāvāmi. Kālikā hi, āvuso, kāmā vuttā bhagavatā bahudukkhā bahupāyāsā; ādīnavo ettha bhiyyo. Sandiṭṭhiko ayaṁ dhammo akāliko ehipassiko opaneyyiko paccattaṁ veditabbo viññūhī”ti.
1.20.e: “I’m not, respectable sir. I’m giving up what takes effect over time to chase after what is apparent in the present. For the Buddha has said that sensual pleasures take effect over time, with much suffering and distress, and they’re all the more full of drawbacks. But this teaching is apparent in the present life, immediately effective, inviting inspection, relevant, so that sensible people can know it for themselves.”

1.20.s: “Kathañca, bhikkhu, kālikā kāmā vuttā bhagavatā bahudukkhā bahupāyāsā, ādīnavo ettha bhiyyo? Kathaṁ sandiṭṭhiko ayaṁ dhammo akāliko ehipassiko opaneyyiko paccattaṁ veditabbo viññūhī”ti?
1.20.e: “But in what way, mendicant, has the Buddha said that sensual pleasures take effect over time, with much suffering and distress, and they’re all the more full of drawbacks? And how is this teaching apparent in the present life, immediately effective, inviting inspection, relevant, so that sensible people can know it for themselves?”

1.20.s: “Ahaṁ kho, āvuso, navo acirapabbajito adhunāgato imaṁ dhammavinayaṁ. Na tāhaṁ sakkomi vitthārena ācikkhituṁ. Ayaṁ so bhagavā arahaṁ sammāsambuddho rājagahe viharati tapodārāme. Taṁ bhagavantaṁ upasaṅkamitvā etamatthaṁ puccha. Yathā te bhagavā byākaroti tathā naṁ dhāreyyāsī”ti.
1.20.e: “I’m junior, respectable sir, recently gone forth, newly come to this teaching and training. I’m not able to explain this in detail. But he, that Blessed One, the perfected one, the fully awakened Buddha, is staying near Rājagaha in the Hot Springs Monastery. You should approach him and ask about this matter. And you should remember it in line with the Buddha’s answer.”

1.20.s: “Na kho, bhikkhu, sukaro so bhagavā amhehi upasaṅkamituṁ, aññāhi mahesakkhāhi devatāhi parivuto. Sace kho tvaṁ, bhikkhu, taṁ bhagavantaṁ upasaṅkamitvā etamatthaṁ puccheyyāsi, mayampi āgaccheyyāma dhammassavanāyā”ti.
1.20.e: “It’s not easy for us to approach the Buddha, as he is surrounded by other illustrious deities. If you go to the Buddha and ask him about this matter, we’ll come along and listen to the teaching.”

1.20.s: “Evamāvuso”ti kho āyasmā samiddhi tassā devatāya paṭissutvā yena bhagavā tenupasaṅkami; upasaṅkamitvā bhagavantaṁ abhivādetvā ekamantaṁ nisīdi. Ekamantaṁ nisinno kho āyasmā samiddhi bhagavantaṁ etadavoca:
1.20.e: “Yes, reverend,” Venerable Samiddhi replied. He went to the Buddha, bowed, sat down to one side, and told him what had happened. Then he added:

1.20.s: “Idhāhaṁ, bhante, rattiyā paccūsasamayaṁ paccuṭṭhāya yena tapodā tenupasaṅkamiṁ gattāni parisiñcituṁ. Tapode gattāni parisiñcitvā paccuttaritvā ekacīvaro aṭṭhāsiṁ gattāni pubbāpayamāno. Atha kho, bhante, aññatarā devatā abhikkantāya rattiyā abhikkantavaṇṇā kevalakappaṁ tapodaṁ obhāsetvā yenāhaṁ tenupasaṅkami; upasaṅkamitvā vehāsaṁ ṭhitā imāya gāthāya ajjhabhāsi:

‘Abhutvā bhikkhasi bhikkhu,
na hi bhutvāna bhikkhasi;
Bhutvāna bhikkhu bhikkhassu,
mā taṁ kālo upaccagā’ti.
Evaṁ vutte, ahaṁ, bhante, taṁ devataṁ gāthāya paccabhāsiṁ:

‘Kālaṁ vohaṁ na jānāmi,
channo kālo na dissati;
Tasmā abhutvā bhikkhāmi,
mā maṁ kālo upaccagā’ti.

Atha kho, bhante, sā devatā pathaviyaṁ patiṭṭhahitvā maṁ etadavoca: ‘daharo tvaṁ, bhikkhu, pabbajito susu kāḷakeso, bhadrena yobbanena samannāgato, paṭhamena vayasā, anikkīḷitāvī kāmesu. Bhuñja, bhikkhu, mānusake kāme; mā sandiṭṭhikaṁ hitvā kālikaṁ anudhāvī’ti.

Evaṁ vuttāhaṁ, bhante, taṁ devataṁ etadavocaṁ: ‘na khvāhaṁ, āvuso, sandiṭṭhikaṁ hitvā kālikaṁ anudhāvāmi; kālikañca khvāhaṁ, āvuso, hitvā sandiṭṭhikaṁ anudhāvāmi. Kālikā hi, āvuso, kāmā vuttā bhagavatā bahudukkhā bahupāyāsā; ādīnavo ettha bhiyyo. Sandiṭṭhiko ayaṁ dhammo akāliko ehipassiko opaneyyiko paccattaṁ veditabbo viññūhī’ti.

Evaṁ vutte, bhante, sā devatā maṁ etadavoca: ‘kathañca, bhikkhu, kālikā kāmā vuttā bhagavatā bahudukkhā bahupāyāsā; ādīnavo ettha bhiyyo? Kathaṁ sandiṭṭhiko ayaṁ dhammo akāliko ehipassiko opaneyyiko paccattaṁ veditabbo viññūhī’ti?

Evaṁ vuttāhaṁ, bhante, taṁ devataṁ etadavocaṁ: ‘ahaṁ kho, āvuso, navo acirapabbajito adhunāgato imaṁ dhammavinayaṁ, na tāhaṁ sakkomi vitthārena ācikkhituṁ. Ayaṁ so bhagavā arahaṁ sammāsambuddho rājagahe viharati tapodārāme. Taṁ bhagavantaṁ upasaṅkamitvā etamatthaṁ puccha. Yathā te bhagavā byākaroti tathā naṁ dhāreyyāsī’ti.

Evaṁ vutte, bhante, sā devatā maṁ etadavoca: ‘na kho, bhikkhu, sukaro so bhagavā amhehi upasaṅkamituṁ, aññāhi mahesakkhāhi devatāhi parivuto. Sace kho tvaṁ, bhikkhu, taṁ bhagavantaṁ upasaṅkamitvā etamatthaṁ puccheyyāsi, mayampi āgaccheyyāma dhammassavanāyā’ti. Sace, bhante, tassā devatāya saccaṁ vacanaṁ, idheva sā devatā avidūre”ti.
1.20.e: “Sir, if that deity spoke the truth, he’ll be close by.”

1.20.s: Evaṁ vutte, sā devatā āyasmantaṁ samiddhiṁ etadavoca: “puccha, bhikkhu, puccha, bhikkhu, yamahaṁ anuppattā”ti.
1.20.e: When he had spoken, that deity said to Samiddhi, “Ask, mendicant, ask! For I have arrived.”

1.20.s: Atha kho bhagavā taṁ devataṁ gāthāhi ajjhabhāsi:
1.20.e: Then the Buddha addressed the deity in verse:

1.20.s:
“Akkheyyasaññino sattā,
akkheyyasmiṁ patiṭṭhitā;
Akkheyyaṁ apariññāya,
yogamāyanti maccuno.
1.20.e:
“Sentient beings who perceive the communicable,
become established in the communicable.
Not understanding the communicable,
they fall under the yoke of Death.

But having fully understood the communicable,
they don’t conceive a communicator,
for they have nothing
by which they might be described.

1.20.s: Sace vijānāsi vadehi yakkhā”ti.
1.20.e: Tell me if you understand, spirit.”

1.20.s: “Na khvāhaṁ, bhante, imassa bhagavatā saṅkhittena bhāsitassa vitthārena atthaṁ ājānāmi. Sādhu me, bhante, bhagavā tathā bhāsatu yathāhaṁ imassa bhagavatā saṅkhittena bhāsitassa vitthārena atthaṁ jāneyyan”ti.
1.20.e: “I don’t understand the detailed meaning of the Buddha’s brief statement. Please teach me this matter so I can understand the detailed meaning.”

“If you think that ‘I’m equal,
special, or worse’, you’ll dispute about that.
Unwavering in the face of the three discriminations,
they have no thought, ‘I’m equal or special’.

1.20.s: Sace vijānāsi vadehi yakkhā”ti.
1.20.e: Tell me if you understand, spirit.”

1.20.s: “Imassapi khvāhaṁ, bhante, bhagavatā saṅkhittena bhāsitassa na vitthārena atthaṁ ājānāmi. Sādhu me, bhante, bhagavā tathā bhāsatu yathāhaṁ imassa bhagavatā saṅkhittena bhāsitassa vitthārena atthaṁ jāneyyan”ti.
1.20.e: “I don’t understand the detailed meaning of the Buddha’s brief statement. Please teach me this matter so I can understand the detailed meaning.”

“They gave up judgment without falling into conceit;
craving for name and form was cut off right here.
They cut the ties, untroubled, <j>with no need for hope.
Though gods and humans search for them
in this life or the next, they never find them,
not in heaven nor in any abode.

1.20.s: Sace vijānāsi vadehi yakkhā”ti.
1.20.e: Tell me if you understand, spirit.”

1.20.s: “Imassa khvāhaṁ, bhante, bhagavatā saṅkhittena bhāsitassa evaṁ vitthārena atthaṁ ājānāmi—
1.20.e: “This is how I understand the detailed meaning of the Buddha’s brief statement:

1.20.s:
Pāpaṁ na kayirā vacasā manasā,
Kāyena vā kiñcana sabbaloke;
Kāme pahāya satimā sampajāno,
Dukkhaṁ na sevetha anatthasaṁhitan”ti.
1.20.e:
You should never do anything bad
by speech or mind or body in all the world.
Having given up sensual pleasures, <j>mindful and aware,
you shouldn’t keep doing <j>what’s painful and pointless.”

1.21.s: Ekamantaṁ ṭhitā kho sā devatā bhagavato santike imaṁ gāthaṁ abhāsi:
1.21.e: Standing to one side, that deity spoke this verse in the Buddha’s presence:

1.21.s:
“Sattiyā viya omaṭṭho,
ḍayhamānova matthake;
Kāmarāgappahānāya,
sato bhikkhu paribbaje”ti.
1.21.e:
“Like they’re struck by a sword,
like their head was on fire,
a mendicant, mindful, should go forth,
to give up sensual desire.”

1.21.s:
“Sattiyā viya omaṭṭho,
ḍayhamānova matthake;
Sakkāyadiṭṭhippahānāya,
sato bhikkhu paribbaje”ti.
1.21.e:
“Like they’re struck by a sword,
like their head was on fire,
a mendicant, mindful, should go forth,
to give up substantialist view.”

1.22.s:
“Nāphusantaṁ phusati ca,
phusantañca tato phuse;
Tasmā phusantaṁ phusati,
appaduṭṭhapadosinan”ti.
1.22.e:
“It doesn’t impact one who doesn’t impact others.
It impacts one because they impact others.
That’s why it impacts one who impacts,
who wrongs one who’s done no wrong.”

1.22.s:
“Yo appaduṭṭhassa narassa dussati,
Suddhassa posassa anaṅgaṇassa;
Tameva bālaṁ pacceti pāpaṁ,
Sukhumo rajo paṭivātaṁva khitto”ti.
1.22.e:
“Whoever wrongs a man who has done no wrong,
a pure man who has not a blemish,
the evil backfires on the fool,
like fine dust thrown upwind.”

1.23.s:
“Antojaṭā bahijaṭā,
Jaṭāya jaṭitā pajā;
Taṁ taṁ gotama pucchāmi,
Ko imaṁ vijaṭaye jaṭan”ti.
1.23.e:
“Tangled within, tangled without:
these people are tangled in tangles.
I ask you this, Gotama:
who can untangle this tangle?”

1.23.s:
“Sīle patiṭṭhāya naro sapañño,
Cittaṁ paññañca bhāvayaṁ;
Ātāpī nipako bhikkhu,
So imaṁ vijaṭaye jaṭaṁ.
1.23.e:
“A wise person grounded in ethics,
developing the mind and wisdom,
a keen and alert mendicant—
they can untangle this tangle.

1.23.s:
Yesaṁ rāgo ca doso ca,
avijjā ca virājitā;
Khīṇāsavā arahanto,
tesaṁ vijaṭitā jaṭā.
1.23.e:
Those in whom greed, hate, and ignorance
have faded away;
the perfected ones with defilements ended—
they have untangled the tangle.

1.23.s:
Yattha nāmañca rūpañca,
asesaṁ uparujjhati;
Paṭighaṁ rūpasaññā ca,
etthesā chijjate jaṭā”ti.
1.23.e:
And where name and form
cease with no residue left behind;
and impingement and perception of form:
it’s here this tangle is cut.”

1.24.s:
“Yato yato mano nivāraye,
Na dukkhameti naṁ tato tato;
Sa sabbato mano nivāraye,
Sa sabbato dukkhā pamuccatī”ti.
1.24.e:
“Whatever you’ve shielded the mind from
can’t cause you suffering.
So you should shield the mind from everything,
then you’re freed from all suffering.”

1.24.s:
“Na sabbato mano nivāraye,
Na mano saṁyatattamāgataṁ;
Yato yato ca pāpakaṁ,
Tato tato mano nivāraye”ti.
1.24.e:
“You need not shield the mind from everything,
nor has the mind gained self-control.
The mind need only be shielded
from where the bad things come.”

1.25.s:
“Yo hoti bhikkhu arahaṁ katāvī,
Khīṇāsavo antimadehadhārī;
Ahaṁ vadāmītipi so vadeyya,
Mamaṁ vadantītipi so vadeyyā”ti.
1.25.e:
“When a mendicant is perfected, well-versed,
with defilements ended, bearing the final body:
would they say, ‘I speak’,
or even ‘they speak to me’?”

“When a mendicant is perfected, well-versed,
with defilements ended, bearing the final body:
they would say, ‘I speak’,
and also ‘they speak to me’.
Skillful, understanding the world’s labels,
they’d use these terms as mere expressions.”

“When a mendicant is perfected, well-versed,
with defilements ended, bearing the final body:
is such a mendicant drawing close to conceit
if they’d say, ‘I speak’,
or even ‘they speak to me’?”

1.25.s:
“Pahīnamānassa na santi ganthā,
Vidhūpitā mānaganthassa sabbe;
Sa vītivatto maññataṁ sumedho,
Ahaṁ vadāmītipi so vadeyya.
1.25.e:
“Someone who has given up conceit has no ties,
the ties of conceit are all dissipated.
Though that intelligent person <j>has passed beyond conceiving,
they’d still say, ‘I speak’,

and also ‘they speak to me’.
Skillful, understanding the world’s labels,
they’d use these terms as mere expressions.”

1.26.s:
“Kati lokasmiṁ pajjotā,
Tehi loko pakāsati;
Bhagavantaṁ puṭṭhumāgamma,
Kathaṁ jānemu taṁ mayan”ti.
1.26.e:
“How many lamps are there
that light up the world?
We’ve come to ask the worthy sir:
how are we to understand this?”

1.26.s:
“Cattāro loke pajjotā,
pañcamettha na vijjati;
Divā tapati ādicco,
rattimābhāti candimā.
1.26.e:
“There are four lamps in the world,
a fifth is not found.
The sun blazes by day,
the moon radiates at night,

1.26.s:
Atha aggi divārattiṁ,
tattha tattha pakāsati;
Sambuddho tapataṁ seṭṭho,
esā ābhā anuttarā”ti.
1.26.e:
while a fire illuminates both
by day and by night.
But a Buddha is the best of blazes:
this is the supreme radiance.”

1.27.s:
“Kuto sarā nivattanti,
kattha vaṭṭaṁ na vattati;
Kattha nāmañca rūpañca,
asesaṁ uparujjhatī”ti.
1.27.e:
“From where do streams recoil?
Where does the cycle spin no more?
Where does name and form
cease with no residue left behind?”

1.27.s:
“Yattha āpo ca pathavī,
tejo vāyo na gādhati;
1.27.e:
“Where water and earth,
fire and air have no footing—

1.27.s:
Ato sarā nivattanti,
ettha vaṭṭaṁ na vattati;
Ettha nāmañca rūpañca,
asesaṁ uparujjhatī”ti.

1.28.s:
“Mahaddhanā mahābhogā,
raṭṭhavantopi khattiyā;
Aññamaññābhigijjhanti,
kāmesu analaṅkatā.
1.28.e:
“The affluent and the wealthy,
even the aristocrats who rule the land,
are jealous of each other,
insatiable in sensual pleasures.

1.28.s:
Tesu ussukkajātesu,
bhavasotānusārisu;
Kedha taṇhaṁ pajahiṁsu,
ke lokasmiṁ anussukā”ti.
1.28.e:
Among those of such an avid nature,
flowing along the stream of lives,
who here has given up craving?
Who in the world is not avid?”

“Having given up their home, their child, their cattle,
and all that they love, they went forth.
Having given up desire and hate,
having dispelled ignorance,
the perfected ones with defilements ended—
they in the world are not avid.”

1.29.s:
“Catucakkaṁ navadvāraṁ,
puṇṇaṁ lobhena saṁyutaṁ;
Paṅkajātaṁ mahāvīra,
kathaṁ yātrā bhavissatī”ti.
1.29.e:
“Four are its wheels, and nine its doors;
it’s stuffed full, bound with greed,
and born from a bog.
Great hero, how will I keep going?”

1.29.s:
“Chetvā naddhiṁ varattañca,
icchā lobhañca pāpakaṁ;
Samūlaṁ taṇhamabbuyha,
evaṁ yātrā bhavissatī”ti.
1.29.e:
“Having cut the strap and harness—
the wicked desire and greed—
and having plucked out craving, root and all:
that’s how you will keep going.”

1.30.e:
“O hero so lean, with antelope calves,
not greedy, eating little,
a giant, wandering alone like a lion,
you’re not concerned for sensual pleasures.
We’ve come to ask a question:
How is one released from all suffering?”

1.30.s:
“Pañca kāmaguṇā loke,
manochaṭṭhā paveditā;
Ettha chandaṁ virājetvā,
evaṁ dukkhā pamuccatī”ti.
1.30.e:
“The world has five kinds of sensual stimulation,
and the mind is said to be the sixth.
When you’ve discarded desire for these,
you’re released from all suffering.”

1.31.s: Evaṁ me sutaṁ— ekaṁ samayaṁ bhagavā sāvatthiyaṁ viharati jetavane anāthapiṇḍikassa ārāme.
1.31.e: So I have heard. At one time the Buddha was staying near Sāvatthī in Jeta’s Grove, Anāthapiṇḍika’s monastery.

1.31.s: Atha kho sambahulā satullapakāyikā devatāyo abhikkantāya rattiyā abhikkantavaṇṇā kevalakappaṁ jetavanaṁ obhāsetvā yena bhagavā tenupasaṅkamiṁsu; upasaṅkamitvā bhagavantaṁ abhivādetvā ekamantaṁ aṭṭhaṁsu. Ekamantaṁ ṭhitā kho ekā devatā bhagavato santike imaṁ gāthaṁ abhāsi:
1.31.e: Then, late at night, several glorious deities of the host of a hundred felicities, lighting up the entire Jeta’s Grove, went up to the Buddha, bowed, and stood to one side. Standing to one side, one deity spoke this verse in the Buddha’s presence:

1.31.s:
“Sabbhireva samāsetha,
sabbhi kubbetha santhavaṁ;
Sataṁ saddhammamaññāya,
seyyo hoti na pāpiyo”ti.
1.31.e:
“Associate only with the virtuous!
Try to get close to the virtuous!
Understanding the true teaching of the good,
things get better, not worse.”

1.31.s: Atha kho aparā devatā bhagavato santike imaṁ gāthaṁ abhāsi:
1.31.e: Then another deity spoke this verse in the Buddha’s presence:

1.31.s:
“Sabbhireva samāsetha,
sabbhi kubbetha santhavaṁ;
Sataṁ saddhammamaññāya,
paññā labbhati nāññato”ti.
1.31.e:
“Associate only with the virtuous!
Try to get close to the virtuous!
Understanding the true teaching of the good,
wisdom is gained—but not from anyone else.”

1.31.s: Atha kho aparā devatā bhagavato santike imaṁ gāthaṁ abhāsi:
1.31.e: Then another deity spoke this verse in the Buddha’s presence:

1.31.s:
“Sabbhireva samāsetha,
sabbhi kubbetha santhavaṁ;
Sataṁ saddhammamaññāya,
sokamajjhe na socatī”ti.
1.31.e:
“Associate only with the virtuous!
Try to get close to the virtuous!
Understanding the true teaching of the good,
you grieve not among the grieving.”

1.31.s: Atha kho aparā devatā bhagavato santike imaṁ gāthaṁ abhāsi:
1.31.e: Then another deity spoke this verse in the Buddha’s presence:

1.31.s:
“Sabbhireva samāsetha,
sabbhi kubbetha santhavaṁ;
Sataṁ saddhammamaññāya,
ñātimajjhe virocatī”ti.
1.31.e:
“Associate only with the virtuous!
Try to get close to the virtuous!
Understanding the true teaching of the good,
you dazzle among your relatives.”

1.31.s: Atha kho aparā devatā bhagavato santike imaṁ gāthaṁ abhāsi:
1.31.e: Then another deity spoke this verse in the Buddha’s presence:

1.31.s:
“Sabbhireva samāsetha,
sabbhi kubbetha santhavaṁ;
Sataṁ saddhammamaññāya,
sattā gacchanti suggatin”ti.
1.31.e:
“Associate only with the virtuous!
Try to get close to the virtuous!
Understanding the true teaching of the good,
sentient beings go to a good place.”

1.31.s: Atha kho aparā devatā bhagavato santike imaṁ gāthaṁ abhāsi:
1.31.e: Then another deity spoke this verse in the Buddha’s presence:

1.31.s:
“Sabbhireva samāsetha,
sabbhi kubbetha santhavaṁ;
Sataṁ saddhammamaññāya,
sattā tiṭṭhanti sātatan”ti.
1.31.e:
“Associate only with the virtuous!
Try to get close to the virtuous!
Understanding the true teaching of the good,
sentient beings live happily.”

1.31.s: Atha kho aparā devatā bhagavantaṁ etadavoca: “kassa nu kho, bhagavā, subhāsitan”ti?
1.31.e: Then another deity said to the Buddha, “Sir, who has spoken well?”

1.31.s: “Sabbāsaṁ vo subhāsitaṁ pariyāyena, api ca mamapi suṇātha—
1.31.e: “You’ve all spoken well in your own way. However, listen to me also:

1.31.s:
Sabbhireva samāsetha,
sabbhi kubbetha santhavaṁ;
Sataṁ saddhammamaññāya,
sabbadukkhā pamuccatī”ti.
1.31.e:
Associate only with the virtuous!
Try to get close to the virtuous!
Understanding the true teaching of the good,
you’re released from all suffering.”

1.31.s: Idamavoca bhagavā. Attamanā tā devatāyo bhagavantaṁ abhivādetvā padakkhiṇaṁ katvā tatthevantaradhāyiṁsūti.
1.31.e: That is what the Buddha said. Delighted, those deities bowed and respectfully circled the Buddha, keeping him on their right, before vanishing right there.

1.32.s: Ekaṁ samayaṁ bhagavā sāvatthiyaṁ viharati jetavane anāthapiṇḍikassa ārāme.
1.32.e: At one time the Buddha was staying near Sāvatthī in Jeta’s Grove, Anāthapiṇḍika’s monastery.

1.32.s: Atha kho sambahulā satullapakāyikā devatāyo abhikkantāya rattiyā abhikkantavaṇṇā kevalakappaṁ jetavanaṁ obhāsetvā yena bhagavā tenupasaṅkamiṁsu; upasaṅkamitvā bhagavantaṁ abhivādetvā ekamantaṁ aṭṭhaṁsu. Ekamantaṁ ṭhitā kho ekā devatā bhagavato santike imaṁ gāthaṁ abhāsi:
1.32.e: Then, late at night, several glorious deities of the host of a hundred felicities, lighting up the entire Jeta’s Grove, went up to the Buddha, bowed, and stood to one side. Standing to one side, one deity spoke this verse in the Buddha’s presence:

1.32.s:
“Maccherā ca pamādā ca,
evaṁ dānaṁ na dīyati;
Puññaṁ ākaṅkhamānena,
deyyaṁ hoti vijānatā”ti.
1.32.e:
“Because of stinginess and negligence
a gift is not given.
Wanting merit,
a smart person would give.”

1.32.s: Atha kho aparā devatā bhagavato santike imā gāthāyo abhāsi:
1.32.e: Then another deity recited these verses in the Buddha’s presence:

“When a miser fails to give because of fear,
the very thing they’re afraid of comes to pass.
The hunger and thirst
that a miser fears
hurt the fool
in this world and the next.

1.32.s:
Tasmā vineyya maccheraṁ,
dajjā dānaṁ malābhibhū;
Puññāni paralokasmiṁ,
patiṭṭhā honti pāṇinan”ti.
1.32.e:
So you should dispel stinginess,
overcoming that stain, and give a gift.
The good deeds of sentient beings
support them in the next world.”

1.32.s: Atha kho aparā devatā bhagavato santike imā gāthāyo abhāsi:
1.32.e: Then another deity recited these verses in the Buddha’s presence:

1.32.s:
“Te matesu na mīyanti,
panthānaṁva sahabbajaṁ;
Appasmiṁ ye pavecchanti,
esa dhammo sanantano.
1.32.e:
“Among the dead they do not die,
those who, like fellow travelers on the road,
are happy to provide, though they have but little.
This is an ancient teaching.

1.32.s:
Appasmeke pavecchanti,
bahuneke na dicchare;
Appasmā dakkhiṇā dinnā,
sahassena samaṁ mitā”ti.
1.32.e:
Some who have little are happy to provide,
while some who have much don’t wish to give.
An offering given from little
is multiplied a thousand times.”

1.32.s: Atha kho aparā devatā bhagavato santike imā gāthāyo abhāsi:
1.32.e: Then another deity recited these verses in the Buddha’s presence:

1.32.s:
“Duddadaṁ dadamānānaṁ,
dukkaraṁ kamma kubbataṁ;
Asanto nānukubbanti,
sataṁ dhammo duranvayo.
1.32.e:
“Giving what’s hard to give,
doing what’s hard to do;
the wicked don’t act like this,
for the teaching of the good is hard to follow.

1.32.s:
Tasmā satañca asataṁ,
nānā hoti ito gati;
Asanto nirayaṁ yanti,
santo saggaparāyanā”ti.
1.32.e:
That’s why the virtuous and the wicked
have different destinations after here.
The wicked go to hell,
while the virtuous are bound for heaven.”

1.32.s: Atha kho aparā devatā bhagavato santike etadavoca: “kassa nu kho, bhagavā, subhāsitan”ti?
1.32.e: Then another deity said to the Buddha, “Sir, who has spoken well?”

1.32.s: “Sabbāsaṁ vo subhāsitaṁ pariyāyena; api ca mamapi suṇātha—
1.32.e: “You’ve all spoken well in your own way. However, listen to me also:

1.32.s:
Dhammaṁ care yopi samuñjakaṁ care,
Dārañca posaṁ dadamappakasmiṁ;
Sataṁ sahassānaṁ sahassayāginaṁ,
Kalampi nāgghanti tathāvidhassa te”ti.
1.32.e:
A hundred thousand people <j>making a thousand sacrifices
isn’t worth a fraction of that sort,
who lives rightly, wandering for gleanings,
or one who supports their partner <j>with what little they have.”

1.32.s: Atha kho aparā devatā bhagavantaṁ gāthāya ajjhabhāsi:
1.32.e: Then another deity addressed the Buddha in verse:

1.32.s:
“Kenesa yañño vipulo mahaggato,
Samena dinnassa na agghameti;
Kathaṁ sataṁ sahassānaṁ sahassayāginaṁ,
Kalampi nāgghanti tathāvidhassa te”ti.
1.32.e:
“Why doesn’t that sacrifice of theirs, <j>so abundant and magnificent,
equal the value of a moral person’s gift?
How is it that a hundred thousand people <j>making a thousand sacrifices
isn’t worth a fraction of what’s offered by that sort?”

1.32.s:
“Dadanti heke visame niviṭṭhā,
Chetvā vadhitvā atha socayitvā;
Sā dakkhiṇā assumukhā sadaṇḍā,
Samena dinnassa na agghameti.
1.32.e:
“Some give based on immorality—
after slaying, killing, and tormenting.
Such an offering—tearful, violent—
in no way equals the value of a moral person’s gift.

1.32.s:
Evaṁ sataṁ sahassānaṁ sahassayāginaṁ,
Kalampi nāgghanti tathāvidhassa te”ti.
1.32.e:
That’s how it is that a hundred thousand people <j>making a thousand sacrifices
isn’t worth a fraction of what’s offered by that sort.”

1.33.s: Sāvatthinidānaṁ.
1.33.e: At Sāvatthī.

1.33.s: Atha kho sambahulā satullapakāyikā devatāyo abhikkantāya rattiyā abhikkantavaṇṇā kevalakappaṁ jetavanaṁ obhāsetvā yena bhagavā tenupasaṅkamiṁsu; upasaṅkamitvā bhagavantaṁ abhivādetvā ekamantaṁ aṭṭhaṁsu. Ekamantaṁ ṭhitā kho ekā devatā bhagavato santike imaṁ udānaṁ udānesi:
1.33.e: Then, late at night, several glorious deities of the host of a hundred felicities, lighting up the entire Jeta’s Grove, went up to the Buddha, bowed, and stood to one side. Standing to one side, one deity expressed this heartfelt sentiment in the Buddha’s presence:

“Good, good fellow, is giving!
Because of stinginess and negligence
a gift is not given.
Wanting merit,
a smart person would give.”

1.33.s: Atha kho aparā devatā bhagavato santike imaṁ udānaṁ udānesi:
1.33.e: Then another deity expressed this heartfelt sentiment in the Buddha’s presence:

1.33.s:
“Sādhu kho mārisa dānaṁ,
Api ca appakasmimpi sāhu dānaṁ.
1.33.e:
“Good, good fellow, is giving!
Even when one has little, giving is good.

1.33.s:
Appasmeke pavecchanti,
bahuneke na dicchare;
Appasmā dakkhiṇā dinnā,
sahassena samaṁ mitā”ti.
1.33.e:
Some who have little are happy to provide,
while some who have much don’t wish to give.
An offering given from little
is multiplied a thousand times.”

1.33.s: Atha kho aparā devatā bhagavato santike imaṁ udānaṁ udānesi:
1.33.e: Then another deity expressed this heartfelt sentiment in the Buddha’s presence:

“Good, good fellow, is giving!
Even when one has little, giving is good.
And it’s also good to give out of faith.
Giving and warfare are similar, they say,
for even a few of the good may conquer the many.
If a faithful person gives even a little,
it still brings them happiness in the hereafter.”

1.33.s: Atha kho aparā devatā bhagavato santike imaṁ udānaṁ udānesi:
1.33.e: Then another deity expressed this heartfelt sentiment in the Buddha’s presence:

1.33.s:
“Sādhu kho mārisa dānaṁ,
Appakasmimpi sāhu dānaṁ;
Saddhāyapi sāhu dānaṁ,
Api ca dhammaladdhassāpi sāhu dānaṁ.
1.33.e:
“Good, good fellow, is giving!
Even when one has little, giving is good.
And it’s also good to give out of faith.
And it’s also good to give legitimate wealth.

1.33.s:
Yo dhammaladdhassa dadāti dānaṁ,
Uṭṭhānavīriyādhigatassa jantu;
Atikkamma so vetaraṇiṁ yamassa,
Dibbāni ṭhānāni upeti macco”ti.
1.33.e:
A personage who gives legitimate wealth,
earned by his efforts and initiative,
has passed over Yama’s Vetaraṇī River;
that mortal arrives at celestial fields.”

1.33.s: Atha kho aparā devatā bhagavato santike imaṁ udānaṁ udānesi:
1.33.e: Then another deity expressed this heartfelt sentiment in the Buddha’s presence:

“Good, good fellow, is giving!
Even when one has little, giving is good.
And it’s also good to give out of faith.
And it’s also good to give legitimate wealth.
And it’s also good to give intelligently.

1.33.s:
Viceyya dānaṁ sugatappasatthaṁ,
Ye dakkhiṇeyyā idha jīvaloke;
Etesu dinnāni mahapphalāni,
Bījāni vuttāni yathā sukhette”ti.
1.33.e:
The Holy One praises giving intelligently
to those worthy of offerings here <j>in the world of the living.
What’s given to these is very fruitful,
like seeds sown in a fertile field.”

1.33.s: Atha kho aparā devatā bhagavato santike imaṁ udānaṁ udānesi:
1.33.e: Then another deity expressed this heartfelt sentiment in the Buddha’s presence:

“Good, good fellow, is giving!
Even when one has little, giving is good.
And it’s also good to give out of faith.
And it’s also good to give legitimate wealth.
And it’s also good to give intelligently.
And it’s also good to be restrained <j>when it comes to living creatures.

1.33.s:
Yo pāṇabhūtāni aheṭhayaṁ caraṁ,
Parūpavādā na karonti pāpaṁ;
Bhīruṁ pasaṁsanti na hi tattha sūraṁ,
Bhayā hi santo na karonti pāpan”ti.
1.33.e:
One who lives without harming any living being
does no bad because of others’ blame.
Were that the case they praise the coward, <j>not the brave;
for the virtuous do no bad out of fear.”

1.33.s: Atha kho aparā devatā bhagavantaṁ etadavoca: “kassa nu kho, bhagavā, subhāsitan”ti?
1.33.e: Then another deity said to the Buddha, “Sir, who has spoken well?”

1.33.s: “Sabbāsaṁ vo subhāsitaṁ pariyāyena, api ca mamapi suṇātha—
1.33.e: “You’ve all spoken well in your own way. However, listen to me also:

1.33.s:
Saddhā hi dānaṁ bahudhā pasatthaṁ,
Dānā ca kho dhammapadaṁva seyyo;
Pubbe ca hi pubbatare ca santo,
Nibbānamevajjhagamuṁ sapaññā”ti.
1.33.e:
A gift of faith is praised in many ways,
but a passage of teaching is better than giving,
for the virtuous, in days old and older still,
even attained extinction with wisdom.”

1.34.s: Ekaṁ samayaṁ bhagavā sāvatthiyaṁ viharati jetavane anāthapiṇḍikassa ārāme.
1.34.e: At one time the Buddha was staying near Sāvatthī in Jeta’s Grove, Anāthapiṇḍika’s monastery.

1.34.s: Atha kho sambahulā satullapakāyikā devatāyo abhikkantāya rattiyā abhikkantavaṇṇā kevalakappaṁ jetavanaṁ obhāsetvā yena bhagavā tenupasaṅkamiṁsu; upasaṅkamitvā bhagavantaṁ abhivādetvā ekamantaṁ aṭṭhaṁsu. Ekamantaṁ ṭhitā kho ekā devatā bhagavato santike imaṁ gāthaṁ abhāsi:
1.34.e: Then, late at night, several glorious deities of the host of a hundred felicities, lighting up the entire Jeta’s Grove, went up to the Buddha, bowed, and stood to one side. Standing to one side, one deity spoke this verse in the Buddha’s presence:

1.34.s:
“Na santi kāmā manujesu niccā,
Santīdha kamanīyāni yesu baddho;
Yesu pamatto apunāgamanaṁ,
Anāgantā puriso maccudheyyā”ti.
1.34.e:
“Among mankind there are no sensual pleasures that are permanent.
Here there are sensuous things, bound to which,
drunk on which, there’s no coming back.
That person doesn’t return from Death’s dominion.”

1.34.s: “Chandajaṁ aghaṁ chandajaṁ dukkhaṁ, Chandavinayā aghavinayo; Aghavinayā dukkhavinayo”ti.
1.34.e: “Gloom is born of desire; suffering is born of desire; when desire is removed, gloom is removed; when gloom is removed, suffering is removed.”

1.34.s:
“Na te kāmā yāni citrāni loke,
Saṅkapparāgo purisassa kāmo;
Tiṭṭhanti citrāni tatheva loke,
Athettha dhīrā vinayanti chandaṁ.
1.34.e:
“The world’s pretty things aren’t sensual pleasures.
Greedy intention is a person’s sensual pleasure.
The world’s pretty things stay just as they are,
but the attentive remove desire for them.

1.34.s:
Kodhaṁ jahe vippajaheyya mānaṁ,
Saṁyojanaṁ sabbamatikkameyya;
Taṁ nāmarūpasmimasajjamānaṁ,
Akiñcanaṁ nānupatanti dukkhā.
1.34.e:
Give up anger, get rid of conceit,
and get past all the fetters.
Sufferings don’t torment the one who has nothing,
not clinging to name and form.

They gave up judgment without falling into conceit;
craving for name and form was cut off right here.
They cut the ties, untroubled, <j>with no need for hope.
Though gods and humans search for them
in this life or the next, they never find them,
not in heaven nor in any abode.”

1.34.s:
“Tañce hi nāddakkhuṁ tathāvimuttaṁ, (iccāyasmā mogharājā)
Devā manussā idha vā huraṁ vā;
Naruttamaṁ atthacaraṁ narānaṁ,
Ye taṁ namassanti pasaṁsiyā te”ti.
1.34.e:
“If neither gods nor humans see one freed in this way,” said Venerable Mogharāja,
“in this life or the next,
are those who revere that supreme man,
who lives for the good of mankind, <j>also worthy of praise?”

1.34.s:
“Pasaṁsiyā tepi bhavanti bhikkhū, (mogharājāti bhagavā)
Ye taṁ namassanti tathāvimuttaṁ;
Aññāya dhammaṁ vicikicchaṁ pahāya,
Saṅgātigā tepi bhavanti bhikkhū”ti.
1.34.e:
“The mendicants who revere one freed in this way,” said the Buddha,
“are also worthy of praise, Mogharāja.
Having understood the teaching <j>and given up doubt,
those mendicants slip their chains.”

1.35.s: Ekaṁ samayaṁ bhagavā sāvatthiyaṁ viharati jetavane anāthapiṇḍikassa ārāme.
1.35.e: At one time the Buddha was staying near Sāvatthī in Jeta’s Grove, Anāthapiṇḍika’s monastery.

1.35.s: Atha kho sambahulā ujjhānasaññikā devatāyo abhikkantāya rattiyā abhikkantavaṇṇā kevalakappaṁ jetavanaṁ obhāsetvā yena bhagavā tenupasaṅkamiṁsu; upasaṅkamitvā vehāsaṁ aṭṭhaṁsu. Vehāsaṁ ṭhitā kho ekā devatā bhagavato santike imaṁ gāthaṁ abhāsi:
1.35.e: Then, late at night, several glorious deities of the host of the fault-finders, lighting up the entire Jeta’s Grove, went up to the Buddha, and stood in the air. Standing in the air, one deity spoke this verse in the Buddha’s presence:

1.35.s:
“Aññathā santamattānaṁ,
aññathā yo pavedaye;
Nikacca kitavasseva,
bhuttaṁ theyyena tassa taṁ.
1.35.e:
“Someone who pretends
to be other than they really are,
is like a cheating gambler
who enjoys what was gained by theft.

1.35.s:
Yañhi kayirā tañhi vade,
yaṁ na kayirā na taṁ vade;
Akarontaṁ bhāsamānaṁ,
parijānanti paṇḍitā”ti.
1.35.e:
You should only say what you would do;
you shouldn’t say what you wouldn’t do.
The wise will recognize
one who talks without doing.”

“Not just by speaking,
nor solely by listening,
are you able to progress
on this hard path,
by which the attentive practicing absorption
are released from Māra’s bonds.

1.35.s:
Na ve dhīrā pakubbanti,
viditvā lokapariyāyaṁ;
Aññāya nibbutā dhīrā,
tiṇṇā loke visattikan”ti.
1.35.e:
The attentive certainly don’t act like that,
for they understand the way of the world.
The attentive are quenched by understanding,
they’ve crossed over clinging to the world.”

1.35.s: Atha kho tā devatāyo pathaviyaṁ patiṭṭhahitvā bhagavato pādesu sirasā nipatitvā bhagavantaṁ etadavocuṁ: “accayo no, bhante, accagamā yathābālaṁ yathāmūḷhaṁ yathāakusalaṁ, yā mayaṁ bhagavantaṁ āsādetabbaṁ amaññimhā. Tāsaṁ no, bhante, bhagavā accayaṁ accayato paṭiggaṇhātu āyatiṁ saṁvarāyā”ti.
1.35.e: Then those deities landed on the ground, bowed with their heads to the Buddha’s feet and said, “We made a mistake, sir. It was foolish, stupid, and unskillful of us to presume to attack the Buddha! Please, sir, accept our mistake for what it is, so we will restrain ourselves in future.”

1.35.s: Atha kho tā devatāyo bhiyyoso mattāya ujjhāyantiyo vehāsaṁ abbhuggañchuṁ. Ekā devatā bhagavato santike imaṁ gāthaṁ abhāsi:
1.35.e: Then those deities, becoming even more fault-finding, flew up in the air. One deity spoke this verse in the Buddha’s presence:

1.35.s:
“Accayaṁ desayantīnaṁ,
yo ce na paṭigaṇhati;
Kopantaro dosagaru,
sa veraṁ paṭimuñcatī”ti.
1.35.e:
“If you don’t give your pardon
when a mistake is confessed,
with hidden anger and heavy hate,
you’re stuck in your enmity.”

1.35.s:
“Accayo ce na vijjetha,
nocidhāpagataṁ siyā;
Verāni na ca sammeyyuṁ,
kenīdha kusalo siyā”ti.
1.35.e:
“Suppose no mistake were found,
and no one here had gone astray:
if enmities were not settled,
how could that be skillful?”

1.35.s:
“Kassaccayā na vijjanti,
kassa natthi apāgataṁ;
Ko na sammohamāpādi,
ko ca dhīro sadā sato”ti.
1.35.e:
“Who makes no mistakes?
Who doesn’t go astray?
Who doesn’t fall into confusion?
Who is attentive, ever mindful?”

“The Realized One, the Buddha,
sympathetic for all beings:
that’s who makes no mistakes,
and that’s who doesn’t go astray.
He doesn’t fall into confusion,
for he’s attentive, ever mindful.

If you don’t give your pardon
when a mistake is confessed,
with hidden anger and heavy hate,
you’re stuck in your enmity.
I don’t approve of such enmity,
and so I pardon your mistake.”

1.36.s: Ekaṁ samayaṁ bhagavā sāvatthiyaṁ viharati jetavane anāthapiṇḍikassa ārāme.
1.36.e: At one time the Buddha was staying near Sāvatthī in Jeta’s Grove, Anāthapiṇḍika’s monastery.

1.36.s: Atha kho sambahulā satullapakāyikā devatāyo abhikkantāya rattiyā abhikkantavaṇṇā kevalakappaṁ jetavanaṁ obhāsetvā yena bhagavā tenupasaṅkamiṁsu; upasaṅkamitvā bhagavantaṁ abhivādetvā ekamantaṁ aṭṭhaṁsu. Ekamantaṁ ṭhitā kho ekā devatā bhagavato santike imaṁ gāthaṁ abhāsi:
1.36.e: Then, late at night, several glorious deities of the host of a hundred felicities, lighting up the entire Jeta’s Grove, went up to the Buddha, bowed, and stood to one side. Standing to one side, one deity spoke this verse in the Buddha’s presence:

1.36.s:
“Saddhā dutiyā purisassa hoti,
No ce assaddhiyaṁ avatiṭṭhati;
Yaso ca kittī ca tatvassa hoti,
Saggañca so gacchati sarīraṁ vihāyā”ti.
1.36.e:
“Faith is a person’s partner.
If faithlessness doesn’t linger,
fame and renown are theirs,
and when they discard this corpse they go to heaven.”

1.36.s: Atha kho aparā devatā bhagavato santike imā gāthāyo abhāsi:
1.36.e: Then another deity recited these verses in the Buddha’s presence:

1.36.s:
“Kodhaṁ jahe vippajaheyya mānaṁ,
Saṁyojanaṁ sabbamatikkameyya;
Taṁ nāmarūpasmimasajjamānaṁ,
Akiñcanaṁ nānupatanti saṅgā”ti.
1.36.e:
“Give up anger, get rid of conceit,
and get past all the fetters.
Chains don’t torment one who has nothing,
not clinging to name and form.”

1.36.s:
“Pamādamanuyuñjanti,
bālā dummedhino janā;
Appamādañca medhāvī,
dhanaṁ seṭṭhaṁva rakkhati.
1.36.e:
“Fools and simpletons
devote themselves to negligence.
But the wise protect diligence
as their best treasure.

1.36.s:
Mā pamādamanuyuñjetha,
mā kāmarati santhavaṁ;
Appamatto hi jhāyanto,
pappoti paramaṁ sukhan”ti.
1.36.e:
Don’t devote yourself to negligence,
or delight in erotic intimacy.
For if you’re diligent and practice absorption,
you’ll attain ultimate happiness.”

1.37.s: Evaṁ me sutaṁ— ekaṁ samayaṁ bhagavā sakkesu viharati kapilavatthusmiṁ mahāvane mahatā bhikkhusaṅghena saddhiṁ pañcamattehi bhikkhusatehi sabbeheva arahantehi; dasahi ca lokadhātūhi devatā yebhuyyena sannipatitā honti bhagavantaṁ dassanāya bhikkhusaṅghañca.
1.37.e: So I have heard. At one time the Buddha was staying in the land of the Sakyans, in the Great Wood near Kapilavatthu, together with a large Saṅgha of five hundred mendicants, all of whom were perfected ones. And most of the deities from ten solar systems had gathered to see the Buddha and the Saṅgha of mendicants.

1.37.s: Atha kho catunnaṁ suddhāvāsakāyikānaṁ devatānaṁ etadahosi: “ayaṁ kho bhagavā sakkesu viharati kapilavatthusmiṁ mahāvane mahatā bhikkhusaṅghena saddhiṁ pañcamattehi bhikkhusatehi sabbeheva arahantehi; dasahi ca lokadhātūhi devatā yebhuyyena sannipatitā honti bhagavantaṁ dassanāya bhikkhusaṅghañca. Yannūna mayampi yena bhagavā tenupasaṅkameyyāma; upasaṅkamitvā bhagavato santike paccekaṁ gāthaṁ bhāseyyāmā”ti.
1.37.e: Then four deities of the pure abodes, aware of what was happening, thought: “Why don’t we go to the Buddha and each recite a verse in his presence?”

1.37.s: Atha kho tā devatā—seyyathāpi nāma balavā puriso samiñjitaṁ vā bāhaṁ pasāreyya pasāritaṁ vā bāhaṁ samiñjeyya; evameva—suddhāvāsesu devesu antarahitā bhagavato purato pāturahesuṁ. Atha kho tā devatā bhagavantaṁ abhivādetvā ekamantaṁ aṭṭhaṁsu. Ekamantaṁ ṭhitā kho ekā devatā bhagavato santike imaṁ gāthaṁ abhāsi:
1.37.e: Then, as easily as a strong person would extend or contract their arm, they vanished from the Pure Abodes and reappeared in front of the Buddha. They bowed to the Buddha and stood to one side. Standing to one side, one deity spoke this verse in the Buddha’s presence:

1.37.s:
“Mahāsamayo pavanasmiṁ,
Devakāyā samāgatā;
Āgatamha imaṁ dhammasamayaṁ,
Dakkhitāye aparājitasaṅghan”ti.
1.37.e:
“There’s a great congregation in the woods,
where heavenly hosts have assembled.
We’ve come to this righteous congregation
to see the invincible Saṅgha!”

1.37.s: Atha kho aparā devatā bhagavato santike imaṁ gāthaṁ abhāsi:
1.37.e: Then another deity spoke this verse in the Buddha’s presence:

1.37.s:
“Tatra bhikkhavo samādahaṁsu,
Cittamattano ujukaṁ akaṁsu;
Sārathīva nettāni gahetvā,
Indriyāni rakkhanti paṇḍitā”ti.
1.37.e:
“The mendicants there are immersed in samādhi,
they’ve straightened their own minds.
Like a charioteer holding the reins,
the astute ones protect their senses.”

1.37.s: Atha kho aparā devatā bhagavato santike imaṁ gāthaṁ abhāsi:
1.37.e: Then another deity spoke this verse in the Buddha’s presence:

1.37.s:
“Chetvā khīlaṁ chetvā palighaṁ,
Indakhīlaṁ ūhacca manejā;
Te caranti suddhā vimalā,
Cakkhumatā sudantā susunāgā”ti.
1.37.e:
“They snapped the post and snapped the cross-bar,
unstirred, they tore out Indra’s pillar.
They live pure and immaculate,
the young giants tamed by the Clear-eyed One.”

1.37.s: Atha kho aparā devatā bhagavato santike imaṁ gāthaṁ abhāsi:
1.37.e: Then another deity spoke this verse in the Buddha’s presence:

1.37.s:
“Ye keci buddhaṁ saraṇaṁ gatāse,
Na te gamissanti apāyabhūmiṁ;
Pahāya mānusaṁ dehaṁ,
Devakāyaṁ paripūressantī”ti.
1.37.e:
“Anyone who has gone to the Buddha for refuge
won’t go to a plane of loss.
After giving up this human body,
they swell the heavenly host.”

1.38.s: Evaṁ me sutaṁ— ekaṁ samayaṁ bhagavā rājagahe viharati maddakucchismiṁ migadāye.
1.38.e: So I have heard. At one time the Buddha was staying near Rājagaha in the Maddakucchi deer park.

1.38.s: Tena kho pana samayena bhagavato pādo sakalikāya khato hoti. Bhusā sudaṁ bhagavato vedanā vattanti sārīrikā vedanā dukkhā tibbā kharā kaṭukā asātā amanāpā; tā sudaṁ bhagavā sato sampajāno adhivāseti avihaññamāno. Atha kho bhagavā catugguṇaṁ saṅghāṭiṁ paññāpetvā dakkhiṇena passena sīhaseyyaṁ kappeti pāde pādaṁ accādhāya sato sampajāno.
1.38.e: Now at that time the Buddha’s foot had been cut by a wooden splinter. The Buddha was stricken by harrowing pains; physical feelings that were painful, sharp, severe, acute, unpleasant, and disagreeable. But he endured unbothered, with mindfulness and situational awareness. And then he spread out his outer robe folded in four and laid down in the lion’s posture—on the right side, placing one foot on top of the other—mindful and aware.

1.38.s: Atha kho sattasatā satullapakāyikā devatāyo abhikkantāya rattiyā abhikkantavaṇṇā kevalakappaṁ maddakucchiṁ obhāsetvā yena bhagavā tenupasaṅkamiṁsu; upasaṅkamitvā bhagavantaṁ abhivādetvā ekamantaṁ aṭṭhaṁsu.
1.38.e: Then, late at night, seven hundred glorious deities of the host of a hundred felicities, lighting up the entire Maddakucchi, went up to the Buddha, bowed, and stood to one side.

1.38.s: Ekamantaṁ ṭhitā kho ekā devatā bhagavato santike imaṁ udānaṁ udānesi: “nāgo vata, bho, samaṇo gotamo; nāgavatā ca samuppannā sārīrikā vedanā dukkhā tibbā kharā kaṭukā asātā amanāpā sato sampajāno adhivāseti avihaññamāno”ti.
1.38.e: Standing to one side, one deity expressed this heartfelt sentiment in the Buddha’s presence: “The ascetic Gotama is such an elephant, sir! And as an elephant, he endures painful physical feelings that have come up—sharp, severe, acute, unpleasant, and disagreeable—unbothered, with mindfulness and situational awareness.”

1.38.s: Atha kho aparā devatā bhagavato santike imaṁ udānaṁ udānesi: “sīho vata, bho, samaṇo gotamo; sīhavatā ca samuppannā sārīrikā vedanā dukkhā tibbā kharā kaṭukā asātā amanāpā sato sampajāno adhivāseti avihaññamāno”ti.
1.38.e: Then another deity expressed this heartfelt sentiment in the Buddha’s presence: “The ascetic Gotama is such a lion, sir! And as a lion, he endures painful physical feelings … unbothered.”

1.38.s: Atha kho aparā devatā bhagavato santike imaṁ udānaṁ udānesi: “ājānīyo vata, bho, samaṇo gotamo; ājānīyavatā ca samuppannā sārīrikā vedanā dukkhā tibbā kharā kaṭukā asātā amanāpā sato sampajāno adhivāseti avihaññamāno”ti.
1.38.e: Then another deity expressed this heartfelt sentiment in the Buddha’s presence: “The ascetic Gotama is such a thoroughbred, sir! And as a thoroughbred, he endures painful physical feelings … unbothered.”

1.38.s: Atha kho aparā devatā bhagavato santike imaṁ udānaṁ udānesi: “nisabho vata, bho, samaṇo gotamo; nisabhavatā ca samuppannā sārīrikā vedanā dukkhā tibbā kharā kaṭukā asātā amanāpā sato sampajāno adhivāseti avihaññamāno”ti.
1.38.e: Then another deity expressed this heartfelt sentiment in the Buddha’s presence: “The ascetic Gotama is such a boss bull, sir! And as a boss bull, he endures painful physical feelings … unbothered.”

1.38.s: Atha kho aparā devatā bhagavato santike imaṁ udānaṁ udānesi: “dhorayho vata, bho, samaṇo gotamo; dhorayhavatā ca samuppannā sārīrikā vedanā dukkhā tibbā kharā kaṭukā asātā amanāpā sato sampajāno adhivāseti avihaññamāno”ti.
1.38.e: Then another deity expressed this heartfelt sentiment in the Buddha’s presence: “The ascetic Gotama is such a behemoth, sir! And as a behemoth, he endures painful physical feelings … unbothered.”

1.38.s: Atha kho aparā devatā bhagavato santike imaṁ udānaṁ udānesi: “danto vata, bho, samaṇo gotamo; dantavatā ca samuppannā sārīrikā vedanā dukkhā tibbā kharā kaṭukā asātā amanāpā sato sampajāno adhivāseti avihaññamāno”ti.
1.38.e: Then another deity expressed this heartfelt sentiment in the Buddha’s presence: “The ascetic Gotama is truly tamed, sir! And as someone tamed, he endures painful physical feelings … unbothered.”

1.38.s: Atha kho aparā devatā bhagavato santike imaṁ udānaṁ udānesi: “passa samādhiṁ subhāvitaṁ cittañca suvimuttaṁ, na cābhinataṁ na cāpanataṁ na ca sasaṅkhāraniggayhavāritagataṁ. Yo evarūpaṁ purisanāgaṁ purisasīhaṁ purisaājānīyaṁ purisanisabhaṁ purisadhorayhaṁ purisadantaṁ atikkamitabbaṁ maññeyya kimaññatra adassanā”ti.
1.38.e: Then another deity expressed this heartfelt sentiment in the Buddha’s presence: “See, his immersion is so well developed, and his mind is so well freed—not leaning forward or pulling back, and not held in place by forceful suppression. If anyone imagines that they can overcome such an elephant of a man, a lion of a man, a thoroughbred of a man, a boss bull of a man, a behemoth of a man, a tamed man—what is that but a failure to see?”

1.38.s:
“Pañcavedā sataṁ samaṁ,
Tapassī brāhmaṇā caraṁ;
Cittañca nesaṁ na sammā vimuttaṁ,
Hīnattharūpā na pāraṅgamā te.
1.38.e:
“Learned in the five branches of Vedic lore,
brahmins practice fervent mortification <j>for a full century.
But their minds are not properly freed,
for those of base character don’t cross to the far shore.

1.38.s:
Taṇhādhipannā vatasīlabaddhā,
Lūkhaṁ tapaṁ vassasataṁ carantā;
Cittañca nesaṁ na sammā vimuttaṁ,
Hīnattharūpā na pāraṅgamā te.
1.38.e:
Seized by craving, <j>attached to precept and observance,
they practice rough and fervent mortification <j>for a hundred years.
But their minds are not properly freed,
for those of base character don’t go to the far shore.

1.38.s:
Na mānakāmassa damo idhatthi,
Na monamatthi asamāhitassa;
Eko araññe viharaṁ pamatto,
Na maccudheyyassa tareyya pāran”ti.
1.38.e:
Someone who’s fond of conceit can’t be tamed,
and someone without immersion can’t be a sage.
Living negligent alone in the wilderness,
they can’t cross beyond Death’s dominion.”

1.38.s:
“Mānaṁ pahāya susamāhitatto,
Sucetaso sabbadhi vippamutto;
Eko araññe viharamappamatto,
Sa maccudheyyassa tareyya pāran”ti.
1.38.e:
“Having given up conceit, serene within oneself,
with a good heart, everywhere free;
living diligent alone in the wilderness,
they cross beyond Death’s dominion.”

1.39.s: Evaṁ me sutaṁ— ekaṁ samayaṁ bhagavā vesāliyaṁ viharati mahāvane kūṭāgārasālāyaṁ.
1.39.e: So I have heard. At one time the Buddha was staying near Vesālī, at the Great Wood, in the hall with the peaked roof.

1.39.s: Atha kho kokanadā pajjunnassa dhītā abhikkantāya rattiyā abhikkantavaṇṇā kevalakappaṁ mahāvanaṁ obhāsetvā yena bhagavā tenupasaṅkami; upasaṅkamitvā bhagavantaṁ abhivādetvā ekamantaṁ aṭṭhāsi. Ekamantaṁ ṭhitā kho sā devatā kokanadā pajjunnassa dhītā bhagavato santike imā gāthāyo abhāsi:
1.39.e: Then, late at night, the glorious Kokanadā, Pajjunna’s daughter, lighting up the entire Great Wood, went up to the Buddha, bowed, stood to one side, and recited these verses in the Buddha’s presence:

1.39.s:
“Vesāliyaṁ vane viharantaṁ,
Aggaṁ sattassa sambuddhaṁ;
Kokanadāhamasmi abhivande,
Kokanadā pajjunnassa dhītā.
1.39.e:
“Staying in the woods of Vesālī
is the Buddha, best of creation.
Kokanadā am I who worships him,
Kokanadā, Pajjuna’s daughter.

1.39.s:
Sutameva pure āsi,
Dhammo cakkhumatānubuddho;
Sāhaṁ dāni sakkhi jānāmi,
Munino desayato sugatassa.
1.39.e:
Previously I had only heard
the teaching realized by the Clear-eyed One.
But now I know it as a witness
while the sage, the Holy One teaches.

1.39.s:
Ye keci ariyaṁ dhammaṁ,
Vigarahantā caranti dummedhā;
Upenti roruvaṁ ghoraṁ,
Cirarattaṁ dukkhaṁ anubhavanti.
1.39.e:
There are simpletons who go about
denouncing the teaching of the noble ones.
They fall into the terrible Hell of Screams
where they suffer long.

1.39.s:
Ye ca kho ariye dhamme,
Khantiyā upasamena upetā;
Pahāya mānusaṁ dehaṁ,
Devakāyaṁ paripūressantī”ti.
1.39.e:
There are those who have found <j>acceptance and peace
in the teaching of the noble ones.
After giving up this human body,
they swell the heavenly host.”

1.40.s: Evaṁ me sutaṁ— ekaṁ samayaṁ bhagavā vesāliyaṁ viharati mahāvane kūṭāgārasālāyaṁ.
1.40.e: So I have heard. At one time the Buddha was staying near Vesālī, at the Great Wood, in the hall with the peaked roof.

1.40.s: Atha kho cūḷakokanadā pajjunnassa dhītā abhikkantāya rattiyā abhikkantavaṇṇā kevalakappaṁ mahāvanaṁ obhāsetvā yena bhagavā tenupasaṅkami; upasaṅkamitvā bhagavantaṁ abhivādetvā ekamantaṁ aṭṭhāsi. Ekamantaṁ ṭhitā kho sā devatā cūḷakokanadā pajjunnassa dhītā bhagavato santike imā gāthāyo abhāsi:
1.40.e: Then, late at night, the glorious Kokanadā the Younger, Pajjunna’s daughter, lighting up the entire Great Wood, went up to the Buddha, bowed, stood to one side, and recited these verses in the Buddha’s presence:

1.40.s:
“Idhāgamā vijjupabhāsavaṇṇā,
Kokanadā pajjunnassa dhītā;
Buddhañca dhammañca namassamānā,
Gāthācimā atthavatī abhāsi.
1.40.e:
“She came here, beautiful as a flash of lightning,
Kokanadā, Pajjunna’s daughter.
Revering the Buddha and the teaching,
she spoke these verses full of meaning.

1.40.s:
Bahunāpi kho taṁ vibhajeyyaṁ,
Pariyāyena tādiso dhammo;
Saṅkhittamatthaṁ lapayissāmi,
Yāvatā me manasā pariyattaṁ.
1.40.e:
The teaching is such that
I could analyze it in many different ways.
However, I will state the meaning in brief
as far as I have learned it by heart.

1.40.s:
Pāpaṁ na kayirā vacasā manasā,
Kāyena vā kiñcana sabbaloke;
Kāme pahāya satimā sampajāno,
Dukkhaṁ na sevetha anatthasaṁhitan”ti.
1.40.e:
You should never do anything bad
by speech or mind or body in all the world.
Having given up sensual pleasures, <j>mindful and aware,
you shouldn’t keep doing <j>what’s painful and pointless.”

1.41.s: Evaṁ me sutaṁ— ekaṁ samayaṁ bhagavā sāvatthiyaṁ viharati jetavane anāthapiṇḍikassa ārāme.
1.41.e: So I have heard. At one time the Buddha was staying near Sāvatthī in Jeta’s Grove, Anāthapiṇḍika’s monastery.

1.41.s: Atha kho aññatarā devatā abhikkantāya rattiyā abhikkantavaṇṇā kevalakappaṁ jetavanaṁ obhāsetvā yena bhagavā tenupasaṅkami; upasaṅkamitvā bhagavantaṁ abhivādetvā ekamantaṁ aṭṭhāsi. Ekamantaṁ ṭhitā kho sā devatā bhagavato santike imā gāthāyo abhāsi:
1.41.e: Then, late at night, a glorious deity, lighting up the entire Jeta’s Grove, went up to the Buddha, bowed, stood to one side, and recited these verses in the Buddha’s presence:

1.41.s:
“Ādittasmiṁ agārasmiṁ,
yaṁ nīharati bhājanaṁ;
Taṁ tassa hoti atthāya,
no ca yaṁ tattha ḍayhati.
1.41.e:
“When your house is on fire,
you rescue the pot
that’s useful,
not the one that’s burnt.

1.41.s:
Evaṁ ādittako loko,
jarāya maraṇena ca;
Nīharetheva dānena,
dinnaṁ hoti sunīhataṁ.
1.41.e:
And as the world is on fire
with old age and death,
you should rescue by giving,
for what’s given is rescued.

1.41.s:
Dinnaṁ sukhaphalaṁ hoti,
nādinnaṁ hoti taṁ tathā;
Corā haranti rājāno,
aggi ḍahati nassati.
1.41.e:
What’s given has happiness as its fruit,
but not what isn’t given.
Bandits take it, or rulers,
it’s consumed by fire, or lost.

Then in the end this corpse is cast off,
along with all your possessions.
Knowing this, an intelligent person
would enjoy what they have and also give it away.
After giving and using according to their means,
blameless, they go to a heavenly place.”

1.42.e:
“Giving what do you give strength?
Giving what do you give beauty?
Giving what do you give happiness?
Giving what do you give vision?
And who is the giver of all?
Please answer my question.”

1.42.s:
“Annado balado hoti,
vatthado hoti vaṇṇado;
Yānado sukhado hoti,
dīpado hoti cakkhudo.
1.42.e:
“Giving food you give strength.
Giving clothes you give beauty.
Giving a vehicle you give happiness.
Giving a lamp you give vision.

1.42.s:
So ca sabbadado hoti,
yo dadāti upassayaṁ;
Amataṁ dado ca so hoti,
yo dhammamanusāsatī”ti.
1.42.e:
And the giver of all
is the one who gives monastic quarters.
But one who teaches the Dhamma
gives the gift of freedom from death.”

1.43.s:
“Annamevābhinandanti,
ubhaye devamānusā;
Atha ko nāma so yakkho,
yaṁ annaṁ nābhinandatī”ti.
1.43.e:
“Both gods and humans
enjoy their food.
So what’s the name of the spirit
who doesn’t enjoy food?”

1.43.s:
“Ye naṁ dadanti saddhāya,
vippasannena cetasā;
Tameva annaṁ bhajati,
asmiṁ loke paramhi ca.
1.43.e:
“Those who give with faith
and a clear and confident heart,
partake of food
in this world and the next.

1.43.s:
Tasmā vineyya maccheraṁ,
dajjā dānaṁ malābhibhū;
Puññāni paralokasmiṁ,
patiṭṭhā honti pāṇinan”ti.
1.43.e:
So you should dispel stinginess,
overcoming that stain, and give a gift.
The good deeds of sentient beings
support them in the next world.”

1.44.s:
“Ekamūlaṁ dvirāvaṭṭaṁ,
timalaṁ pañcapattharaṁ;
Samuddaṁ dvādasāvaṭṭaṁ,
pātālaṁ atarī isī”ti.
1.44.e:
“One the root, two the loops,
three the stains, five the spreads,
and the ocean, the twelfth whirlpool:
such is the abyss crossed by the seer.”

1.45.s:
“Anomanāmaṁ nipuṇatthadassiṁ,
Paññādadaṁ kāmālaye asattaṁ;
Taṁ passatha sabbaviduṁ sumedhaṁ,
Ariye pathe kamamānaṁ mahesin”ti.
1.45.e:
“Behold him of peerless name <j>who sees the subtle meaning,
giver of wisdom, <j>unattached to the realm of sensuality:
the all-knower, so very intelligent,
the great seer treading the noble road.”

1.46.s:
“Accharāgaṇasaṅghuṭṭhaṁ,
pisācagaṇasevitaṁ;
Vanantaṁ mohanaṁ nāma,
kathaṁ yātrā bhavissatī”ti.
1.46.e:
“It’s resounding with a group of nymphs,
but haunted by a gang of goblins!
This grove is called ‘Deluding’.
How will I keep going?”

1.46.s:
“Ujuko nāma so maggo,
abhayā nāma sā disā;
Ratho akūjano nāma,
dhammacakkehi saṁyuto.
1.46.e:
“That path is called ‘the direct way’,
and it’s headed for the place called ‘fearless’.
The chariot is called ‘unswerving’,
fitted with wheels of the teaching.

1.46.s:
Hirī tassa apālambo,
satyassa parivāraṇaṁ;
Dhammāhaṁ sārathiṁ brūmi,
sammādiṭṭhipurejavaṁ.
1.46.e:
Conscience is its bench-back,
mindfulness its upholstery.
I say the teaching is the driver,
with right view running out in front.

1.46.s:
Yassa etādisaṁ yānaṁ,
itthiyā purisassa vā;
Sa ve etena yānena,
nibbānasseva santike”ti.
1.46.e:
Any woman or man
who has such a vehicle,
by means of this vehicle
has drawn near to extinguishment.”

1.47.s:
“Kesaṁ divā ca ratto ca,
sadā puññaṁ pavaḍḍhati;
Dhammaṭṭhā sīlasampannā,
ke janā saggagāmino”ti.
1.47.e:
“Whose merit always grows
by day and by night?
What people—firm in principle, <j>accomplished in conduct—
are going to heaven?”

1.47.s:
“Ārāmaropā vanaropā,
ye janā setukārakā;
Papañca udapānañca,
ye dadanti upassayaṁ.
1.47.e:
“Planters of parks or groves,
those who build a bridge,
a drinking place and well,
and those who give monastic quarters.

1.47.s:
Tesaṁ divā ca ratto ca,
sadā puññaṁ pavaḍḍhati;
Dhammaṭṭhā sīlasampannā,
te janā saggagāmino”ti.
1.47.e:
Their merit always grows
by day and by night.
Those people—firm in principle, <j>accomplished in conduct—
are going to heaven.”

1.48.s:
“Idañhi taṁ jetavanaṁ,
isisaṅghanisevitaṁ;
Āvutthaṁ dhammarājena,
pītisañjananaṁ mama.
1.48.e:
“This is indeed that Jeta’s Grove,
frequented by the Saṅgha of seers,
where the King of Dhamma stayed:
it brings me joy!

1.48.s:
Kammaṁ vijjā ca dhammo ca,
sīlaṁ jīvitamuttamaṁ;
Etena maccā sujjhanti,
na gottena dhanena vā.

Tasmā hi paṇḍito poso,
sampassaṁ atthamattano;
Yoniso vicine dhammaṁ,
evaṁ tattha visujjhati.
1.48.e:
That’s why an astute person,
seeing what’s good for themselves,
would examine the teaching rationally,
that’s how they become purified in that.

1.48.s:
Sāriputtova paññāya,
sīlena upasamena ca;
Yopi pāraṅgato bhikkhu,
etāvaparamo siyā”ti.
1.48.e:
Sāriputta is full of wisdom,
ethics, and peace.
Even a mendicant who has crossed over
might at best equal him.”

1.49.s:
“Yedha maccharino loke,
kadariyā paribhāsakā;
Aññesaṁ dadamānānaṁ,
antarāyakarā narā.
1.49.e:
“Those folk in the world who are stingy,
miserly and abusive,
setting up obstacles
for others who give.

1.49.s:
Kīdiso tesaṁ vipāko,
samparāyo ca kīdiso;
Bhagavantaṁ puṭṭhumāgamma,
kathaṁ jānemu taṁ mayan”ti.
1.49.e:
What kind of result do they reap?
What kind of future life?
We’ve come to ask the worthy sir:
how are we to understand this?”

1.49.s:
“Yedha maccharino loke,
kadariyā paribhāsakā;
Aññesaṁ dadamānānaṁ,
antarāyakarā narā.
1.49.e:
“Those folk in the world who are stingy,
miserly and abusive,
setting up obstacles
for others who give:

1.49.s:
Nirayaṁ tiracchānayoniṁ,
yamalokaṁ upapajjare;
Sace enti manussattaṁ,
dalidde jāyare kule.
1.49.e:
they’re reborn in hell,
the animal realm, or Yama’s world.
If they return to the human state,
they’re born in a poor family,

where clothes, food, pleasure, and play
are hard to find.
They don’t even get
what they hope for from others.
This is the result in the present life,
and in the next, a bad destination.”

1.49.s:
“Itihetaṁ vijānāma,
aññaṁ pucchāma gotama;
Yedha laddhā manussattaṁ,
vadaññū vītamaccharā.
1.49.e:
“We understand what you’re saying,
and ask another question, Gotama.
What about those who’ve gained the human state,
who are bountiful and rid of stinginess,

confident in the Buddha and the teaching,
with keen respect for the Saṅgha?
What kind of result do they reap?
What kind of future life?
We’ve come to ask the worthy sir:
how are we to understand this?”

“Those who’ve gained the human state
who are bountiful and rid of stinginess,
confident in the Buddha and the teaching,
with keen respect for the Saṅgha:
they illuminate the heavens
wherever they’re reborn.

1.49.s:
Sace enti manussattaṁ,
aḍḍhe ājāyare kule;
Coḷaṁ piṇḍo ratī khiḍḍā,
yatthākicchena labbhati.
1.49.e:
If they return to the human state,
they’re reborn in a rich family,
where clothes, food, pleasure, and play
are easy to find.

1.49.s:
Parasambhatesu bhogesu,
vasavattīva modare;
Diṭṭhe dhammesa vipāko,
samparāye ca suggatī”ti.
1.49.e:
They rejoice like those
who control the possessions of others.
This is the result in the present life,
and in the next, a good destination.”

1.50.s:
“Avihaṁ upapannāse,
vimuttā satta bhikkhavo;
Rāgadosaparikkhīṇā,
tiṇṇā loke visattikan”ti.
1.50.e:
“Seven mendicants reborn in Aviha
have been freed.
With the complete ending of greed and hate,
they’ve crossed over clinging to the world.”

1.50.s:
“Ke ca te ataruṁ paṅkaṁ,
maccudheyyaṁ suduttaraṁ;
Ke hitvā mānusaṁ dehaṁ,
dibbayogaṁ upaccagun”ti.
1.50.e:
“Who are those who’ve crossed the bog,
Death’s dominion so hard to pass?
Who, after leaving behind the human body,
have risen above celestial yokes?”

“Upaka and Palagaṇḍa,
and Pukkusāti, these three;
Bhaddiya and Bhaddadeva,
and Bāhudanti and Piṅgiya.
They, after leaving behind the human body,
have risen above celestial yokes.”

1.50.s:
“Kusalī bhāsasī tesaṁ,
mārapāsappahāyinaṁ;
Kassa te dhammamaññāya,
acchiduṁ bhavabandhanan”ti.
1.50.e:
“You speak well of them,
who have let go the snares of Māra.
Whose teaching did they understand
to cut the bonds of rebirth?”

1.50.s:
“Na aññatra bhagavatā,
nāññatra tava sāsanā;
Yassa te dhammamaññāya,
acchiduṁ bhavabandhanaṁ.
1.50.e:
“None other than the Blessed One!
None other than your instruction!
It was your teaching that they understood
to cut the bonds of rebirth.

1.50.s:
Yattha nāmañca rūpañca,
asesaṁ uparujjhati;
Taṁ te dhammaṁ idhaññāya,
acchiduṁ bhavabandhanan”ti.
1.50.e:
Where name and form
cease with no residue left behind;
understanding this teaching,
they cut the bonds of rebirth.”

1.50.s:
“Gambhīraṁ bhāsasī vācaṁ,
dubbijānaṁ sudubbudhaṁ;
Kassa tvaṁ dhammamaññāya,
vācaṁ bhāsasi īdisan”ti.
1.50.e:
“The words you say are deep,
hard to understand, so very hard to wake up to.
Whose teaching did you understand
that you can say such things?”

1.50.s:
“Kumbhakāro pure āsiṁ,
vekaḷiṅge ghaṭīkaro;
Mātāpettibharo āsiṁ,
kassapassa upāsako.
1.50.e:
“In the past I was a potter
in Vebhaliṅga named Ghaṭīkāra.
I took care of my parents
as a lay follower of Buddha Kassapa.

1.50.s:
Virato methunā dhammā,
brahmacārī nirāmiso;
Ahuvā te sagāmeyyo,
ahuvā te pure sakhā.
1.50.e:
I refrained from sexual intercourse,
I was chaste, spiritual.
We lived in the same village;
in the past I was your comrade.

1.50.s:
Sohamete pajānāmi,
vimutte satta bhikkhavo;
Rāgadosaparikkhīṇe,
tiṇṇe loke visattikan”ti.
1.50.e:
I am the one who understands
that these seven mendicants have been freed.
With the complete ending of greed and hate,
they’ve crossed over clinging to the world.”

“That’s exactly how it was,
just as you say, Bhaggava.
In the past you were a potter
in Vebhaliṅga named Ghaṭīkāra.
You took care of your parents
as a lay follower of Buddha Kassapa.

1.50.s:
Virato methunā dhammā,
brahmacārī nirāmiso;
Ahuvā me sagāmeyyo,
ahuvā me pure sakhā”ti.
1.50.e:
You refrained from sexual intercourse,
you were chaste, spiritual.
We lived in the same village;
in the past you were my comrade.”

1.50.s:
“Evametaṁ purāṇānaṁ,
sahāyānaṁ ahu saṅgamo;
Ubhinnaṁ bhāvitattānaṁ,
sarīrantimadhārinan”ti.
1.50.e:
That’s how it was
when those friends of old met again.
Both of them were evolved,
bearing their final body.

1.51.s:
“Kiṁsu yāva jarā sādhu,
kiṁsu sādhu patiṭṭhitaṁ;
Kiṁsu narānaṁ ratanaṁ,
kiṁsu corehi dūharan”ti.
1.51.e:
“What’s still good in old age?
What’s good when grounded?
What is people’s treasure?
What’s hard for thieves to take?”

1.51.s:
“Sīlaṁ yāva jarā sādhu,
saddhā sādhu patiṭṭhitā;
Paññā narānaṁ ratanaṁ,
puññaṁ corehi dūharan”ti.
1.51.e:
“Ethics are still good in old age.
Faith is good when grounded.
Wisdom is people’s treasure.
Merit’s hard for thieves to take.”

1.52.s:
“Kiṁsu ajarasā sādhu,
kiṁsu sādhu adhiṭṭhitaṁ;
Kiṁsu narānaṁ ratanaṁ,
kiṁsu corehyahāriyan”ti.
1.52.e:
“What’s good because it never gets old?
What’s good when committed?
What is people’s treasure?
What can thieves never take?”

1.52.s:
“Sīlaṁ ajarasā sādhu,
saddhā sādhu adhiṭṭhitā;
Paññā narānaṁ ratanaṁ,
puññaṁ corehyahāriyan”ti.
1.52.e:
“Ethics are good because they never grow old.
Faith is good when committed.
Wisdom is people’s treasure.
Merit’s what thieves can never take.”

1.53.s:
“Kiṁsu pavasato mittaṁ,
kiṁsu mittaṁ sake ghare;
Kiṁ mittaṁ atthajātassa,
kiṁ mittaṁ samparāyikan”ti.
1.53.e:
“Who’s your friend while journeying?
Who’s your friend at home?
Who’s your friend in time of need?
Who’s your friend in lives to come?”

“A caravan is your friend while journeying.
Mother is your friend at home.
An ally in time of need
is a friend time and again.
But the good deeds you’ve done yourself—
that’s your friend in lives to come.”

1.54.s:
“Kiṁsu vatthu manussānaṁ,
kiṁsūdha paramo sakhā;
Kiṁsu bhūtā upajīvanti,
ye pāṇā pathavissitā”ti.
1.54.e:
“What is the site for human beings?
What is the best comrade here?
By what do the creatures who live off the earth
sustain their life?”

1.54.s:
“Puttā vatthu manussānaṁ,
bhariyā ca paramo sakhā;
Vuṭṭhiṁ bhūtā upajīvanti,
ye pāṇā pathavissitā”ti.
1.54.e:
“Children are the site for human beings.
A wife is the best comrade.
The creatures who live off the earth
sustain their life by rain.”

1.55.s:
“Kiṁsu janeti purisaṁ,
kiṁsu tassa vidhāvati;
Kiṁsu saṁsāramāpādi,
kiṁsu tassa mahabbhayan”ti.
1.55.e:
“What gives birth to a person?
What do they have that runs about?
What enters transmigration?
What’s their greatest fear?”

1.55.s:
“Taṇhā janeti purisaṁ,
cittamassa vidhāvati;
Satto saṁsāramāpādi,
dukkhamassa mahabbhayan”ti.
1.55.e:
“Craving gives birth to a person.
Their mind is what runs about.
A sentient being enters transmigration.
