Suffering is their greatest fear.”

1.56.s:
“Kiṁsu janeti purisaṁ,
kiṁsu tassa vidhāvati;
Kiṁsu saṁsāramāpādi,
kismā na parimuccatī”ti.
1.56.e:
“What gives birth to a person?
What do they have that runs about?
What enters transmigration?
From what are they not free?”

1.56.s:
“Taṇhā janeti purisaṁ,
cittamassa vidhāvati;
Satto saṁsāramāpādi,
dukkhā na parimuccatī”ti.
1.56.e:
“Craving gives birth to a person.
Their mind is what runs about.
A sentient being enters transmigration.
From suffering they are not free.”

1.57.s:
“Kiṁsu janeti purisaṁ,
kiṁsu tassa vidhāvati;
Kiṁsu saṁsāramāpādi,
kiṁsu tassa parāyanan”ti.
1.57.e:
“What gives birth to a person?
What do they have that runs about?
What enters transmigration?
What is their destiny?”

1.57.s:
“Taṇhā janeti purisaṁ,
cittamassa vidhāvati;
Satto saṁsāramāpādi,
kammaṁ tassa parāyanan”ti.
1.57.e:
“Craving gives birth to a person.
Their mind is what runs about.
A sentient being enters transmigration.
Deeds are their final haven.”

1.58.s:
“Kiṁsu uppatho akkhāto,
kiṁsu rattindivakkhayo;
Kiṁ malaṁ brahmacariyassa,
kiṁ sinānamanodakan”ti.
1.58.e:
“What’s declared to be a deviation?
What is ending day and night?
What’s the stain of chastity?
What’s the waterless bath?”

“Lust is declared to be a deviation.
Youth is ending day and night.
Women are the stain of chastity,
to which this generation clings.
Fervor and chastity
are the waterless bath.”

1.59.s:
“Kiṁsu dutiyā purisassa hoti,
Kiṁsu cenaṁ pasāsati;
Kissa cābhirato macco,
Sabbadukkhā pamuccatī”ti.
1.59.e:
“What is a person’s partner?
What instructs them?
Enjoying what is a mortal
released from all suffering?”

1.59.s:
“Saddhā dutiyā purisassa hoti,
Paññā cenaṁ pasāsati;
Nibbānābhirato macco,
Sabbadukkhā pamuccatī”ti.
1.59.e:
“Faith is a person’s partner.
Wisdom instructs them.
Delighting in extinguishment a mortal
is released from all suffering.”

1.60.s:
“Kiṁsu nidānaṁ gāthānaṁ,
kiṁsu tāsaṁ viyañjanaṁ;
Kiṁsu sannissitā gāthā,
kiṁsu gāthānamāsayo”ti.
1.60.e:
“What’s the source of verses?
What constitutes their phrasing?
What do verses depend upon?
What underlies verses?”

1.60.s:
“Chando nidānaṁ gāthānaṁ,
akkharā tāsaṁ viyañjanaṁ;
Nāmasannissitā gāthā,
kavi gāthānamāsayo”ti.
1.60.e:
“Metre is the source of verses.
Syllables constitute their phrasing.
Verses depend on names.
A poet underlies verses.”

1.61.s:
“Kiṁsu sabbaṁ addhabhavi,
kismā bhiyyo na vijjati;
Kissassu ekadhammassa,
sabbeva vasamanvagū”ti.
1.61.e:
“What overcomes everything?
What is it that nothing excels?
What is the one thing
that has everything under its sway?”

1.61.s:
“Nāmaṁ sabbaṁ addhabhavi,
nāmā bhiyyo na vijjati;
Nāmassa ekadhammassa,
sabbeva vasamanvagū”ti.
1.61.e:
“Name overcomes everything.
Nothing excels name.
Name is the one thing
that has everything under its sway.”

1.62.s:
“Kenassu nīyati loko,
kenassu parikassati;
Kissassu ekadhammassa,
sabbeva vasamanvagū”ti.
1.62.e:
“What leads the world on?
What drags it around?
What is the one thing
that has everything under its sway?”

1.62.s:
“Cittena nīyati loko,
cittena parikassati;
Cittassa ekadhammassa,
sabbeva vasamanvagū”ti.
1.62.e:
“The mind leads the world on.
The mind drags it around.
Mind is the one thing
that has everything under its sway.”

1.63.s:
“Kenassu nīyati loko,
kenassu parikassati;
Kissassu ekadhammassa,
sabbeva vasamanvagū”ti.
1.63.e:
“What leads the world on?
What drags it around?
What is the one thing
that has everything under its sway?”

1.63.s:
“Taṇhāya nīyati loko,
taṇhāya parikassati;
Taṇhāya ekadhammassa,
sabbeva vasamanvagū”ti.
1.63.e:
“Craving leads the world on.
Craving drags it around.
Craving is the one thing
that has everything under its sway.”

1.64.s:
“Kiṁsu saṁyojano loko,
kiṁsu tassa vicāraṇaṁ;
Kissassu vippahānena,
nibbānaṁ iti vuccatī”ti.
1.64.e:
“What fetters the world?
How does it travel about?
With the giving up of what
is extinguishment spoken of?”

1.64.s:
“Nandīsaṁyojano loko,
vitakkassa vicāraṇaṁ;
Taṇhāya vippahānena,
nibbānaṁ iti vuccatī”ti.
1.64.e:
“Delight fetters the world.
It travels about by means of thought.
With the giving up of craving
extinguishment is spoken of.”

1.65.s:
“Kiṁsu sambandhano loko,
kiṁsu tassa vicāraṇaṁ;
Kissassu vippahānena,
sabbaṁ chindati bandhanan”ti.
1.65.e:
“What binds the world?
How does it travel about?
With the giving up of what
are all bonds severed?”

1.65.s:
“Nandīsambandhano loko,
vitakkassa vicāraṇaṁ;
Taṇhāya vippahānena,
sabbaṁ chindati bandhanan”ti.
1.65.e:
“Delight binds the world.
It travels about by means of thought.
With the giving up of craving
all bonds are severed.”

1.66.s:
“Kenassubbhāhato loko,
kenassu parivārito;
Kena sallena otiṇṇo,
kissa dhūpāyito sadā”ti.
1.66.e:
“By what is the world beaten down?
By what is it surrounded?
What dart has laid it low?
With what is it always fuming?”

1.66.s:
“Maccunābbhāhato loko,
jarāya parivārito;
Taṇhāsallena otiṇṇo,
icchādhūpāyito sadā”ti.
1.66.e:
“The world is beaten down by death.
It’s surrounded by old age.
The dart of craving has laid it low.
It’s always fuming with desire.”

1.67.s:
“Kenassu uḍḍito loko,
kenassu parivārito;
Kenassu pihito loko,
kismiṁ loko patiṭṭhito”ti.
1.67.e:
“By what is the world ensnared?
By what is it surrounded?
By what is the world fastened shut?
On what is the world grounded?”

1.67.s:
“Taṇhāya uḍḍito loko,
jarāya parivārito;
Maccunā pihito loko,
dukkhe loko patiṭṭhito”ti.
1.67.e:
“Craving has ensnared the world.
It’s surrounded by old age.
The world is fastened shut by mortality.
The world is grounded on suffering.”

1.68.s:
“Kenassu pihito loko,
kismiṁ loko patiṭṭhito;
Kenassu uḍḍito loko,
kenassu parivārito”ti.
1.68.e:
“By what is the world fastened shut?
On what is the world grounded?
By what is the world ensnared?
By what is it surrounded?”

1.68.s:
“Maccunā pihito loko,
dukkhe loko patiṭṭhito;
Taṇhāya uḍḍito loko,
jarāya parivārito”ti.
1.68.e:
“The world is fastened shut by mortality.
The world is grounded on suffering.
Craving has ensnared the world.
It’s surrounded by old age.”

1.69.s:
“Kenassu bajjhatī loko,
kissa vinayāya muccati;
Kissassu vippahānena,
sabbaṁ chindati bandhanan”ti.
1.69.e:
“What is it that binds the world?
By removing what is it freed?
With the giving up of what
are all bonds severed?”

1.69.s:
“Icchāya bajjhatī loko,
icchāvinayāya muccati;
Icchāya vippahānena,
sabbaṁ chindati bandhanan”ti.
1.69.e:
“Desire is what binds the world.
By the removing of desire it’s freed.
With the giving up of desire,
all bonds are severed.”

1.70.s:
“Kismiṁ loko samuppanno,
kismiṁ kubbati santhavaṁ;
Kissa loko upādāya,
kismiṁ loko vihaññatī”ti.
1.70.e:
“In what has the world arisen?
With what does it get intimate?
By grasping what
is the world troubled in what?”

1.70.s:
“Chasu loko samuppanno,
chasu kubbati santhavaṁ;
Channameva upādāya,
chasu loko vihaññatī”ti.
1.70.e:
“The world has arisen in six.
It gets intimate with six.
Derived from the six,
the world’s troubled in six.”

1.71.s: Ekamantaṁ ṭhitā kho sā devatā bhagavantaṁ gāthāya ajjhabhāsi:
1.71.e: Standing to one side, that deity addressed the Buddha in verse:

1.71.s:
“Kiṁsu chetvā sukhaṁ seti,
kiṁsu chetvā na socati;
Kissassu ekadhammassa,
vadhaṁ rocesi gotamā”ti.
1.71.e:
“When what is slain do you sleep at ease?
When what is slain is there no sorrow?
What is the one thing, Gotama,
whose killing you approve?”

“When anger’s slain you sleep at ease.
When anger’s slain there is no sorrow.
Anger has a poisonous root
and a sweet tip, O deity.
The noble ones praise its killing,
for when it’s slain there is no sorrow.”

1.72.s:
“Kiṁsu rathassa paññāṇaṁ,
kiṁsu paññāṇamaggino;
Kiṁsu raṭṭhassa paññāṇaṁ,
kiṁsu paññāṇamitthiyā”ti.
1.72.e:
“What is a chariot known by?
What is fire known by?
What is a nation known by?
What is a woman known by?”

1.72.s:
“Dhajo rathassa paññāṇaṁ,
dhūmo paññāṇamaggino;
Rājā raṭṭhassa paññāṇaṁ,
bhattā paññāṇamitthiyā”ti.
1.72.e:
“A chariot is known by a banner.
Fire is known by smoke.
A nation is known by its ruler.
A woman is known by her husband.”

1.73.s:
“Kiṁsūdha vittaṁ purisassa seṭṭhaṁ,
Kiṁsu suciṇṇo sukhamāvahati;
Kiṁsu have sādutaraṁ rasānaṁ,
Kathaṁjīviṁ jīvitamāhu seṭṭhan”ti.
1.73.e:
“What’s a person’s best wealth?
What brings happiness when practiced well?
What’s the sweetest taste of all?
The one they say has the best life: how do they live?”

1.73.s:
“Saddhīdha vittaṁ purisassa seṭṭhaṁ,
Dhammo suciṇṇo sukhamāvahati;
Saccaṁ have sādutaraṁ rasānaṁ,
Paññājīviṁ jīvitamāhu seṭṭhan”ti.
1.73.e:
“Faith here is a person’s best wealth.
The teaching brings happiness when practiced well.
Truth is the sweetest taste of all.
The one they say has the best life lives by wisdom.”

1.74.s:
“Kiṁsu uppatataṁ seṭṭhaṁ,
kiṁsu nipatataṁ varaṁ;
Kiṁsu pavajamānānaṁ,
kiṁsu pavadataṁ varan”ti.
1.74.e:
“What’s the best of things that rise?
And what’s the finest thing to fall?
And what of the things that go forth?
And who’s the finest speaker?”

1.74.s:
“Bījaṁ uppatataṁ seṭṭhaṁ,
vuṭṭhi nipatataṁ varā;
Gāvo pavajamānānaṁ,
putto pavadataṁ varo”ti.
1.74.e:
“A seed’s the best of things that rise.
Rain’s the finest thing to fall.
Cattle, of things that go forth.
And a child is the finest speaker.”

1.74.s:
“Vijjā uppatataṁ seṭṭhā,
avijjā nipatataṁ varā;
Saṅgho pavajamānānaṁ,
buddho pavadataṁ varo”ti.
1.74.e:
“Knowledge is best of things that rise.
Ignorance the finest thing to fall.
The Saṅgha, of things that go forth.
And the Buddha is the finest speaker.”

1.75.s:
“Kiṁsūdha bhītā janatā anekā,
Maggo canekāyatanappavutto;
Pucchāmi taṁ gotama bhūripañña,
Kismiṁ ṭhito paralokaṁ na bhāye”ti.
1.75.e:
“Why are so many people here afraid,
when the path has been taught <j>with so many dimensions?
I ask you, Gotama, whose wisdom is vast:
Standing on what need one not fear the next world?”

“When speech and mind are directed right,
and you don’t do anything bad with the body
while dwelling at home with plenty of food and drink.
Faithful, gentle, charitable, and bountiful:
one who stands on these four principles,
who stands on the teaching <j>need not fear the next world.”

1.76.e:
“What ages, what does not age?
What’s called a deviation?
What’s a roadblock for skillful qualities?
What is ending day and night?
What’s the stain of celibacy?
What’s the waterless bath?

1.76.s:
Kati lokasmiṁ chiddāni,
yattha vittaṁ na tiṭṭhati;
Bhagavantaṁ puṭṭhumāgamma,
kathaṁ jānemu taṁ mayan”ti.
1.76.e:
How many holes are there in the world,
where one’s wealth leaks out?
We’ve come to ask the worthy sir:
how are we to understand this?”

“The physical form of mortals gets old,
but their name and clan don’t.
Lust is called a deviation,

and greed is a roadblock for skillful qualities.
Youth is ending day and night.
Women are the stain of chastity,
to which this generation clings.
Fervor and chastity
are the waterless bath.

There are six holes in the world,
where one’s wealth leaks out:
laziness and negligence,
lack of initiative and lack of restraint,
sleepiness and sloth.
You should completely get rid of these holes!”

1.77.s:
“Kiṁsu issariyaṁ loke,
kiṁsu bhaṇḍānamuttamaṁ;
Kiṁsu satthamalaṁ loke,
kiṁsu lokasmimabbudaṁ.
1.77.e:
“What is authority in the world?
What’s the best of valuables?
What in the world is a rusty sword?
Who is a pest in the world?

1.77.s:
Kiṁsu harantaṁ vārenti,
haranto pana ko piyo;
Kiṁsu punappunāyantaṁ,
abhinandanti paṇḍitā”ti.
1.77.e:
Who gets arrested when they take things away?
And who is loved when they take things away?
And who is approved by the astute
when they come again and again?”

1.77.s:
“Vaso issariyaṁ loke,
itthī bhaṇḍānamuttamaṁ;
Kodho satthamalaṁ loke,
corā lokasmimabbudā.
1.77.e:
“Sway is authority in the world.
A woman is the best of valuables.
Anger in the world is a rusty sword.
A bandit is a pest in the world.

1.77.s:
Coraṁ harantaṁ vārenti,
haranto samaṇo piyo;
Samaṇaṁ punappunāyantaṁ,
abhinandanti paṇḍitā”ti.
1.77.e:
A bandit gets arrested when they take things away.
And an ascetic is loved when they take things away.
An ascetic is approved by the astute
when they come again and again.”

1.78.s:
“Kimatthakāmo na dade,
kiṁ macco na pariccaje;
Kiṁsu muñceyya kalyāṇaṁ,
pāpikaṁ na ca mocaye”ti.
1.78.e:
“What should one who wants what’s best <j>not give away?
What should a mortal not forsake?
What should be released when it’s good,
but not when it’s bad?”

1.78.s:
“Attānaṁ na dade poso,
attānaṁ na pariccaje;
Vācaṁ muñceyya kalyāṇaṁ,
pāpikañca na mocaye”ti.
1.78.e:
“A man shouldn’t give away himself.
He shouldn’t forsake himself.
Speech should be released when it’s good,
but not when it’s bad.”

1.79.e:
“What binds the provisions for a journey?
What’s the vault of wealth?
What drags a person around?
What in the world is hard to give up?
With what are ordinary beings bound,
like birds in a snare?”

“Faith binds the provisions for a journey.
Majesty is the vault of wealth.
Desire drags a person around.
Desire in the world is hard to give up.
Ordinary beings are bound by desire,
like birds in a snare.”

1.80.s:
“Kiṁsu lokasmi pajjoto,
kiṁsu lokasmi jāgaro;
Kiṁsu kamme sajīvānaṁ,
kimassa iriyāpatho.
1.80.e:
“What’s the lamp for the world?
What in the world is wakeful?
Who are one’s work colleagues?
What is one’s walk of life?

1.80.s:
Kiṁsu alasaṁ analasañca,
Mātā puttaṁva posati;
Kiṁ bhūtā upajīvanti,
Ye pāṇā pathavissitā”ti.
1.80.e:
What nurtures the idle and the tireless,
like a mother her child?
By what do the creatures who live off the earth
sustain their life?”

1.80.s:
“Paññā lokasmi pajjoto,
sati lokasmi jāgaro;
Gāvo kamme sajīvānaṁ,
sītassa iriyāpatho.
1.80.e:
“Wisdom is the lamp for the world.
Mindfulness in the world is wakeful.
Cattle are one’s work colleagues,
and the furrow is one’s walk of life.

1.80.s:
Vuṭṭhi alasaṁ analasañca,
Mātā puttaṁva posati;
Vuṭṭhiṁ bhūtā upajīvanti,
Ye pāṇā pathavissitā”ti.
1.80.e:
Rain nurtures the idle and the tireless,
like a mother her child.
The creatures who live off the earth
sustain their life by rain.”

1.81.s:
“Kesūdha araṇā loke,
kesaṁ vusitaṁ na nassati;
Kedha icchaṁ parijānanti,
kesaṁ bhojissiyaṁ sadā.
1.81.e:
“Who in the world is free of strife?
Whose life is not wasted?
Who here completely understands desire?
Who always lives as their own master?

1.81.s:
Kiṁsu mātā pitā bhātā,
vandanti naṁ patiṭṭhitaṁ;
Kiṁsu idha jātihīnaṁ,
abhivādenti khattiyā”ti.
1.81.e:
To whom do mother, father, and brothers
bow when they’re established?
Who here, though low born,
is bowed to even by aristocrats?”

1.81.s:
“Samaṇīdha araṇā loke,
Samaṇānaṁ vusitaṁ na nassati;
Samaṇā icchaṁ parijānanti,
Samaṇānaṁ bhojissiyaṁ sadā.
1.81.e:
“Ascetics are free of strife in the world.
The life of ascetics is not wasted.
Ascetics completely understand desire.
Ascetics always live as their own master.

1.81.s:
Samaṇaṁ mātā pitā bhātā,
vandanti naṁ patiṭṭhitaṁ;
Samaṇīdha jātihīnaṁ,
abhivādenti khattiyā”ti.
1.81.e:
Mother, father, and brothers
bow to ascetics when they’re established.
Even though an ascetic is low born,
they’re bowed to even by aristocrats.”

2.1.s: Evaṁ me sutaṁ— ekaṁ samayaṁ bhagavā sāvatthiyaṁ viharati jetavane anāthapiṇḍikassa ārāme.
2.1.e: So I have heard. At one time the Buddha was staying near Sāvatthī in Jeta’s Grove, Anāthapiṇḍika’s monastery.

2.1.s: Atha kho kassapo devaputto abhikkantāya rattiyā abhikkantavaṇṇo kevalakappaṁ jetavanaṁ obhāsetvā yena bhagavā tenupasaṅkami; upasaṅkamitvā bhagavantaṁ abhivādetvā ekamantaṁ aṭṭhāsi. Ekamantaṁ ṭhito kho kassapo devaputto bhagavantaṁ etadavoca: “bhikkhuṁ bhagavā pakāsesi, no ca bhikkhuno anusāsan”ti.
2.1.e: Then, late at night, the glorious godling Kassapa, lighting up the entire Jeta’s Grove, went up to the Buddha, bowed, stood to one side, and said to him, “The Buddha has revealed the mendicant, but not his instructions to a mendicant.”
“Well then, Kassapa, clarify this matter yourself.”

2.1.s:
“Subhāsitassa sikkhetha,
samaṇūpāsanassa ca;
Ekāsanassa ca raho,
cittavūpasamassa cā”ti.
2.1.e:
“You should all train <j>to learn well-spoken words,
to attend closely to ascetics,
to sit alone in hidden places,
and to settle the mind.”

2.1.s: Idamavoca kassapo devaputto; samanuñño satthā ahosi. Atha kho kassapo devaputto “samanuñño me satthā”ti bhagavantaṁ abhivādetvā padakkhiṇaṁ katvā tatthevantaradhāyīti.
2.1.e: That is what the godling Kassapa said, and the Teacher concurred. Then Kassapa, knowing that the Teacher concurred, bowed and respectfully circled the Buddha, keeping him on his right, before vanishing right there.

2.2.s: Ekamantaṁ ṭhito kho kassapo devaputto bhagavato santike imaṁ gāthaṁ abhāsi:
2.2.e: Standing to one side, the godling Kassapa spoke this verse in the Buddha’s presence:

2.2.s:
“Bhikkhu siyā jhāyī vimuttacitto,
Ākaṅkhe ce hadayassānupattiṁ;
Lokassa ñatvā udayabbayañca,
Sucetaso anissito tadānisaṁso”ti.
2.2.e:
“If a mendicant is a meditator, freed in mind,
and if they desire the heart’s fulfillment—
having known the arising and passing of the world,
good-hearted, independent, that is their reward.”

2.3.s: Atha kho māgho devaputto abhikkantāya rattiyā abhikkantavaṇṇo kevalakappaṁ jetavanaṁ obhāsetvā yena bhagavā tenupasaṅkami; upasaṅkamitvā bhagavantaṁ abhivādetvā ekamantaṁ aṭṭhāsi. Ekamantaṁ ṭhito kho māgho devaputto bhagavantaṁ gāthāya ajjhabhāsi:
2.3.e: Then, late at night, the glorious godling Māgha, lighting up the entire Jeta’s Grove, went up to the Buddha, bowed, stood to one side, and addressed the Buddha in verse:

2.3.s:
“Kiṁsu chetvā sukhaṁ seti,
kiṁsu chetvā na socati;
Kissassu ekadhammassa,
vadhaṁ rocesi gotamā”ti.
2.3.e:
“When what is slain do you sleep at ease?
When what is slain is there no sorrow?
What is the one thing
whose killing you approve?”

“When anger’s slain you sleep at ease.
When anger’s slain there is no sorrow.
Anger has a poisonous root
and a sweet tip, O Smiter of the Constrictor.
The noble ones praise its killing,
for when it’s slain there is no sorrow.”

2.4.s: Ekamantaṁ ṭhito kho māgadho devaputto bhagavantaṁ gāthāya ajjhabhāsi:
2.4.e: Standing to one side, the godling Maghada addressed the Buddha in verse:

2.4.s:
“Kati lokasmiṁ pajjotā,
yehi loko pakāsati;
Bhavantaṁ puṭṭhumāgamma,
kathaṁ jānemu taṁ mayan”ti.
2.4.e:
“How many lamps are there
that light up the world?
We’ve come to ask the Buddha;
how are we to understand this?”

2.4.s:
“Cattāro loke pajjotā,
pañcamettha na vijjati;
Divā tapati ādicco,
rattimābhāti candimā.
2.4.e:
“There are four lamps in the world,
a fifth is not found.
The sun blazes by day,
the moon radiates at night,

2.4.s:
Atha aggi divārattiṁ,
tattha tattha pakāsati;
Sambuddho tapataṁ seṭṭho,
esā ābhā anuttarā”ti.
2.4.e:
while a fire illuminates both
by day and by night.
But a Buddha is the best of blazes:
this is the supreme radiance.”

2.5.s: Atha kho dāmali devaputto abhikkantāya rattiyā abhikkantavaṇṇo kevalakappaṁ jetavanaṁ obhāsetvā yena bhagavā tenupasaṅkami; upasaṅkamitvā bhagavantaṁ abhivādetvā ekamantaṁ aṭṭhāsi. Ekamantaṁ ṭhito kho dāmali devaputto bhagavato santike imaṁ gāthaṁ abhāsi:
2.5.e: Then, late at night, the glorious godling Dāmali, lighting up the entire Jeta’s Grove, went up to the Buddha, bowed, stood to one side, and spoke this verse in the Buddha’s presence:

2.5.s:
“Karaṇīyametaṁ brāhmaṇena,
Padhānaṁ akilāsunā;
Kāmānaṁ vippahānena,
Na tenāsīsate bhavan”ti.
2.5.e:
“This is what should be done by a brahmin:
unrelenting striving.
Then, with the giving up of sensual pleasures,
they won’t hope to be reborn.”

“The brahmin has nothing left to do,” said the Buddha to Dāmali,
“for they’ve completed their task.
So long as a personage fails to gain a footing in the river,
they swim with every limb.
But someone who has gained a footing <j>and stands on dry land
need not swim, <j>for they have reached the far shore.

2.5.s:
Esūpamā dāmali brāhmaṇassa,
Khīṇāsavassa nipakassa jhāyino;
Pappuyya jātimaraṇassa antaṁ,
Nāyūhatī pāragato hi so”ti.
2.5.e:
Dāmali, this is a simile for the brahmin,
alert, a meditator who has ended defilements.
Since they’ve reached the end of rebirth and death,
they need not swim, <j>for they have reached the far shore.”

2.6.s: Ekamantaṁ ṭhito kho kāmado devaputto bhagavantaṁ etadavoca: “dukkaraṁ, bhagavā, sudukkaraṁ, bhagavā”ti.
2.6.e: Standing to one side, the godling Kāmada said to the Buddha, “It’s too hard, Blessed One! It’s just too hard!”

2.6.s:
“Dukkaraṁ vāpi karonti, (kāmadāti bhagavā)
Sekhā sīlasamāhitā;
Ṭhitattā anagāriyupetassa,
Tuṭṭhi hoti sukhāvahā”ti.
2.6.e:
“They do it even though it’s hard,” said the Buddha to Kāmada,
“the stable trainees with ethics, and immersion.
For one who has entered the homeless life,
contentment brings happiness.”
“Such contentment, Blessed One, is hard to find.”

2.6.s:
“Dullabhaṁ vāpi labhanti, (kāmadāti bhagavā)
Cittavūpasame ratā;
Yesaṁ divā ca ratto ca,
Bhāvanāya rato mano”ti.
2.6.e:
“They find it even though it’s hard,” said the Buddha to Kāmada,
“those who love to settle the mind;
whose minds love to meditate
day and night.”
“But it’s hard, Blessed One, to immerse this mind in samādhi.”

2.6.s:
“Dussamādahaṁ vāpi samādahanti, (kāmadāti bhagavā)
Indriyūpasame ratā;
Te chetvā maccuno jālaṁ,
Ariyā gacchanti kāmadā”ti.
2.6.e:
“They become immersed in samādhi <j>even though it’s hard,” said the Buddha to Kāmada,
“those who love calming the faculties.
Having cut through the net of Death,
the noble ones, Kāmada, go on their way.”
“But this path, Blessed One, is rough and hard to travel.”

“Though it’s rough, hard to travel,
the noble ones, Kāmada, go on their way.
The ignoble fall headfirst
on a rough path.
But the path of the noble ones is smooth,
for the noble ones are smooth amid the rough.”

2.7.s: Ekamantaṁ ṭhito kho pañcālacaṇḍo devaputto bhagavato santike imaṁ gāthaṁ abhāsi:
2.7.e: Standing to one side, the godling Pañcālacaṇḍa spoke this verse in the Buddha’s presence:

2.7.s:
“Sambādhe vata okāsaṁ,
Avindi bhūrimedhaso;
Yo jhānamabujjhi buddho,
Paṭilīnanisabho munī”ti.
2.7.e:
“The opening amid confinement
was discovered by the Buddha of vast intelligence,
who awakened to absorption,
the sage, the solitary boss bull.”

2.7.s:
“Sambādhe vāpi vindanti, (pañcālacaṇḍāti bhagavā)
Dhammaṁ nibbānapattiyā;
Ye satiṁ paccalatthaṁsu,
Sammā te susamāhitā”ti.
2.7.e:
“Even amid confinement they understand,” said the Buddha to Pañcālacaṇḍa,
“the principle for attaining extinguishment.
Those who have acquired mindfulness
are perfectly serene in samādhi.”

2.8.s: Atha kho tāyano devaputto purāṇatitthakaro abhikkantāya rattiyā abhikkantavaṇṇo kevalakappaṁ jetavanaṁ obhāsetvā yena bhagavā tenupasaṅkami; upasaṅkamitvā bhagavantaṁ abhivādetvā ekamantaṁ aṭṭhāsi. Ekamantaṁ ṭhito kho tāyano devaputto bhagavato santike imā gāthāyo abhāsi:
2.8.e: Then, late at night, the glorious godling Tāyana, formerly a religious founder, lighting up the entire Jeta’s Grove, went up to the Buddha, bowed, stood to one side, and recited these verses in the Buddha’s presence:

2.8.s:
“Chinda sotaṁ parakkamma,
kāme panuda brāhmaṇa;
Nappahāya munī kāme,
nekattamupapajjati.
2.8.e:
“Cut the stream, striving!
Cast aside sensual pleasures, brahmin.
A sage who doesn’t give up sensual pleasures
is not reborn in a unified state.

2.8.s:
Kayirā ce kayirāthenaṁ,
daḷhamenaṁ parakkame;
Sithilo hi paribbājo,
bhiyyo ākirate rajaṁ.
2.8.e:
If one is to do what should be done,
one should staunchly strive.
For the life gone forth when laxly led
just stirs up dust all the more.

2.8.s:
Akataṁ dukkaṭaṁ seyyo,
pacchā tapati dukkaṭaṁ;
Katañca sukataṁ seyyo,
yaṁ katvā nānutappati.
2.8.e:
A bad deed is better left undone,
for it will plague you later on.
A good deed is better done,
one that does not plague you.

2.8.s:
Kuso yathā duggahito,
hatthamevānukantati;
Sāmaññaṁ dupparāmaṭṭhaṁ,
nirayāyūpakaḍḍhati.
2.8.e:
When kusa grass is wrongly grasped
it only cuts the hand.
So too, the ascetic life, when wrongly taken,
drags you to hell.

2.8.s:
Yaṁ kiñci sithilaṁ kammaṁ,
saṅkiliṭṭhañca yaṁ vataṁ;
Saṅkassaraṁ brahmacariyaṁ,
na taṁ hoti mahapphalan”ti.
2.8.e:
Any lax act,
any corrupt observance,
or suspicious spiritual life,
is not very fruitful.”

2.8.s: Idamavoca tāyano devaputto; idaṁ vatvā bhagavantaṁ abhivādetvā padakkhiṇaṁ katvā tatthevantaradhāyīti.
2.8.e: That is what the godling Tāyana said. Then he bowed and respectfully circled the Buddha, keeping him on his right, before vanishing right there.

2.8.s: Atha kho bhagavā tassā rattiyā accayena bhikkhū āmantesi:
2.8.e: Then, when the night had passed, the Buddha told the mendicants all that had happened.

2.8.s: “imaṁ, bhikkhave, rattiṁ tāyano nāma devaputto purāṇatitthakaro abhikkantāya rattiyā abhikkantavaṇṇo kevalakappaṁ jetavanaṁ obhāsetvā yenāhaṁ tenupasaṅkami; upasaṅkamitvā maṁ abhivādetvā ekamantaṁ aṭṭhāsi. Ekamantaṁ ṭhito kho, bhikkhave, tāyano devaputto mama santike imā gāthāyo abhāsi:
2.8.e: “Mendicants, tonight, the glorious godling Tāyana, formerly a religious founder, lighting up the entire Jeta’s Grove, came to me, bowed, stood to one side, and recited these verses in my presence.” The Buddha repeated the verses in full, adding:

2.8.s:
‘Chinda sotaṁ parakkamma,
kāme panuda brāhmaṇa;
Nappahāya munī kāme,
nekattamupapajjati.

Kayirā ce kayirāthenaṁ,
daḷhamenaṁ parakkame;
Sithilo hi paribbājo,
bhiyyo ākirate rajaṁ.

Akataṁ dukkaṭaṁ seyyo,
pacchā tapati dukkaṭaṁ;
Katañca sukataṁ seyyo,
yaṁ katvā nānutappati.

Kuso yathā duggahito,
hatthamevānukantati;
Sāmaññaṁ dupparāmaṭṭhaṁ,
nirayāyūpakaḍḍhati.

Yaṁ kiñci sithilaṁ kammaṁ,
saṅkiliṭṭhañca yaṁ vataṁ;
Saṅkassaraṁ brahmacariyaṁ,
na taṁ hoti mahapphalan’ti.

Idamavoca, bhikkhave, tāyano devaputto, idaṁ vatvā maṁ abhivādetvā padakkhiṇaṁ katvā tatthevantaradhāyi. Uggaṇhātha, bhikkhave, tāyanagāthā; pariyāpuṇātha, bhikkhave, tāyanagāthā; dhāretha, bhikkhave, tāyanagāthā. Atthasaṁhitā, bhikkhave, tāyanagāthā ādibrahmacariyikā”ti.
2.8.e: “That is what the godling Tāyana said. Then he bowed and respectfully circled me, keeping me on his right side, before vanishing right there. Mendicants, learn the verses of Tāyana! Memorize the verses of Tāyana! Remember the verses of Tāyana! These verses are beneficial and relate to the fundamentals of the spiritual life.”

2.9.s: Tena kho pana samayena candimā devaputto rāhunā asurindena gahito hoti. Atha kho candimā devaputto bhagavantaṁ anussaramāno tāyaṁ velāyaṁ imaṁ gāthaṁ abhāsi:
2.9.e: Now at that time the Moon God had been seized by Rāhu, lord of titans. Then the Moon God, recollecting the Buddha, at that time spoke this verse:

2.9.s:
“Namo te buddha vīratthu,
vippamuttosi sabbadhi;
Sambādhapaṭipannosmi,
tassa me saraṇaṁ bhavā”ti.
2.9.e:
“Homage to you, Buddha, hero!
You’re free in every way.
I’ve wandered into confinement:
be my refuge!”

2.9.s: Atha kho bhagavā candimaṁ devaputtaṁ ārabbha rāhuṁ asurindaṁ gāthāya ajjhabhāsi:
2.9.e: Then the Buddha addressed Rāhu in verse concerning the Moon God:

2.9.s:
“Tathāgataṁ arahantaṁ,
candimā saraṇaṁ gato;
Rāhu candaṁ pamuñcassu,
buddhā lokānukampakā”ti.
2.9.e:
“The Moon God has gone for refuge
to the Realized One, the perfected one.
The Buddhas have compassion for the world—
so Rāhu, release the Moon!”

2.9.s: Atha kho rāhu asurindo candimaṁ devaputtaṁ muñcitvā taramānarūpo yena vepacitti asurindo tenupasaṅkami; upasaṅkamitvā saṁviggo lomahaṭṭhajāto ekamantaṁ aṭṭhāsi. Ekamantaṁ ṭhitaṁ kho rāhuṁ asurindaṁ vepacitti asurindo gāthāya ajjhabhāsi:
2.9.e: Then Rāhu, having released the Moon, rushed to see Vepacitti, lord of titans and stood to one side, shocked and awestruck. Vepacitti addressed him in verse:

2.9.s:
“Kiṁ nu santaramānova,
rāhu candaṁ pamuñcasi;
Saṁviggarūpo āgamma,
kiṁ nu bhītova tiṭṭhasī”ti.
2.9.e:
“Why the rush?
Rāhu, you released the Moon
and came here looking like you’re in shock:
why do you stand there so scared?”

2.9.s:
“Sattadhā me phale muddhā,
jīvanto na sukhaṁ labhe;
Buddhagāthābhigītomhi,
no ce muñceyya candiman”ti.
2.9.e:
“My head would have exploded in seven pieces,
I would have found no happiness in life,
if, when enchanted by the Buddha’s verse,
I had not released the Moon.”

2.10.s: Tena kho pana samayena sūriyo devaputto rāhunā asurindena gahito hoti. Atha kho sūriyo devaputto bhagavantaṁ anussaramāno tāyaṁ velāyaṁ imaṁ gāthaṁ abhāsi:
2.10.e: Now at that time the Sun God had been seized by Rāhu, lord of titans. Then the Sun God, recollecting the Buddha, at that time spoke this verse:

2.10.s:
“Namo te buddha vīratthu,
vippamuttosi sabbadhi;
Sambādhapaṭipannosmi,
tassa me saraṇaṁ bhavā”ti.
2.10.e:
“Homage to you, Buddha, hero!
You’re free in every way.
I’ve wandered into confinement:
be my refuge!”

2.10.s: Atha kho bhagavā sūriyaṁ devaputtaṁ ārabbha rāhuṁ asurindaṁ gāthāhi ajjhabhāsi:
2.10.e: Then the Buddha addressed Rāhu in verse concerning the Sun God:

2.10.s:
“Tathāgataṁ arahantaṁ,
sūriyo saraṇaṁ gato;
Rāhu sūriyaṁ pamuñcassu,
buddhā lokānukampakā.
2.10.e:
“The Sun God has gone for refuge
to the Realized One, the perfected one.
The Buddhas have compassion for the world—
so Rāhu, release the Sun!

2.10.s:
Yo andhakāre tamasi pabhaṅkaro,
Verocano maṇḍalī uggatejo;
Mā rāhu gilī caramantalikkhe,
Pajaṁ mamaṁ rāhu pamuñca sūriyan”ti.
2.10.e:
He is a beacon in the darkness,
the dazzling sun, circle of awesome might.
Rāhu, do not swallow him as he traverses the sky.
Rāhu, release my offspring, the Sun!”

2.10.s: Atha kho rāhu asurindo sūriyaṁ devaputtaṁ muñcitvā taramānarūpo yena vepacitti asurindo tenupasaṅkami; upasaṅkamitvā saṁviggo lomahaṭṭhajāto ekamantaṁ aṭṭhāsi. Ekamantaṁ ṭhitaṁ kho rāhuṁ asurindaṁ vepacitti asurindo gāthāya ajjhabhāsi:
2.10.e: Then Rāhu, having released the Sun, rushed to see Vepacitti, lord of titans and stood to one side, shocked and awestruck. Vepacitti addressed him in verse:

2.10.s:
“Kiṁ nu santaramānova,
rāhu sūriyaṁ pamuñcasi;
Saṁviggarūpo āgamma,
kiṁ nu bhītova tiṭṭhasī”ti.
2.10.e:
“Why the rush?
Rāhu, you released the Sun
and came here looking like you’re in shock:
why do you stand there so scared?”

2.10.s:
“Sattadhā me phale muddhā,
jīvanto na sukhaṁ labhe;
Buddhagāthābhigītomhi,
no ce muñceyya sūriyan”ti.
2.10.e:
“My head would have exploded in seven pieces,
I would have found no joy in life,
if, when enchanted by the Buddha’s verse,
I had not released the Sun.”

2.11.s: Atha kho candimaso devaputto abhikkantāya rattiyā abhikkantavaṇṇo kevalakappaṁ jetavanaṁ obhāsetvā yena bhagavā tenupasaṅkami; upasaṅkamitvā bhagavantaṁ abhivādetvā ekamantaṁ aṭṭhāsi. Ekamantaṁ ṭhito kho candimaso devaputto bhagavato santike imaṁ gāthaṁ abhāsi:
2.11.e: Then, late at night, the glorious godling Candimasa, lighting up the entire Jeta’s Grove, went up to the Buddha, bowed, stood to one side, and spoke this verse in the Buddha’s presence:

2.11.s:
“Te hi sotthiṁ gamissanti,
kacchevāmakase magā;
Jhānāni upasampajja,
ekodi nipakā satā”ti.
2.11.e:
“Like deer in a mosquito-free marsh,
they will reach a safe place
having entered the absorptions,
unified, alert, and mindful.”

2.11.s:
“Te hi pāraṁ gamissanti,
chetvā jālaṁva ambujo;
Jhānāni upasampajja,
appamattā raṇañjahā”ti.
2.11.e:
“Like fish when the net is cut,
they will reach the far shore
having entered the absorptions,
diligent, with strife discarded.”

2.12.s: Ekamantaṁ ṭhito kho veṇḍu devaputto bhagavato santike imaṁ gāthaṁ abhāsi:
2.12.e: Standing to one side, the godling Vishnu spoke this verse in the Buddha’s presence:

2.12.s:
“Sukhitāva te manujā,
sugataṁ payirupāsiya;
Yuñjaṁ gotamasāsane,
appamattā nu sikkhare”ti.
2.12.e:
“Happy are the men
who pay homage to the Holy One!
They apply themselves to Gotama’s instructions,
diligently training.”

2.12.s:
“Ye me pavutte siṭṭhipade, (veṇḍūti bhagavā)
Anusikkhanti jhāyino;
Kāle te appamajjantā,
Na maccuvasagā siyun”ti.
2.12.e:
“Those who practice absorption <j>in accord with the training”, said the Buddha to Vishnu,
“in the way of teaching I’ve proclaimed,
diligent while there is still time;
they won’t fall under the sway of Death.”

2.13.s: Evaṁ me sutaṁ— ekaṁ samayaṁ bhagavā rājagahe viharati veḷuvane kalandakanivāpe.
2.13.e: So I have heard. At one time the Buddha was staying near Rājagaha in the Bamboo Grove, the squirrels’ feeding ground.

2.13.s: Atha kho dīghalaṭṭhi devaputto abhikkantāya rattiyā abhikkantavaṇṇo kevalakappaṁ veḷuvanaṁ obhāsetvā yena bhagavā tenupasaṅkami; upasaṅkamitvā bhagavantaṁ abhivādetvā ekamantaṁ aṭṭhāsi. Ekamantaṁ ṭhito kho dīghalaṭṭhi devaputto bhagavato santike imaṁ gāthaṁ abhāsi:
2.13.e: Then, late at night, the glorious godling Dīghalaṭṭhi, lighting up the entire Bamboo Grove, went up to the Buddha, bowed, stood to one side, and spoke this verse in the Buddha’s presence:

2.13.s:
“Bhikkhu siyā jhāyī vimuttacitto,
Ākaṅkhe ce hadayassānupattiṁ;
Lokassa ñatvā udayabbayañca,
Sucetaso anissito tadānisaṁso”ti.
2.13.e:
“If a mendicant is a meditator, freed in mind,
and if they desire the heart’s fulfillment—
having known the arising and passing of the world,
good-hearted, independent, that is their reward.”

2.14.s: Ekamantaṁ ṭhito kho nandano devaputto bhagavantaṁ gāthāya ajjhabhāsi:
2.14.e: Standing to one side, the godling Nandana addressed the Buddha in verse:

“I ask you, Gotama, whose wisdom is vast,
the Blessed One <j>of unhindered knowledge and vision.
What sort do they call ethical?
What sort do they call wise?
What sort lives on after transcending suffering?
What sort is worshiped by the deities?”

2.14.s:
“Yo sīlavā paññavā bhāvitatto,
Samāhito jhānarato satīmā;
Sabbassa sokā vigatā pahīnā,
Khīṇāsavo antimadehadhārī.
2.14.e:
“Someone who is ethical, wise, evolved,
becomes serene, loving absorption, mindful,
who’s gotten rid of and given up all sorrows,
with defilements ended, they bear their final body.

2.14.s:
Tathāvidhaṁ sīlavantaṁ vadanti,
Tathāvidhaṁ paññavantaṁ vadanti;
Tathāvidho dukkhamaticca iriyati,
Tathāvidhaṁ devatā pūjayantī”ti.
2.14.e:
That sort they call ethical.
That sort they call wise.
That sort lives on after transcending suffering.
That sort is worshiped by the deities.”

2.15.s: Ekamantaṁ ṭhito kho candano devaputto bhagavantaṁ gāthāya ajjhabhāsi:
2.15.e: Standing to one side, the godling Candana addressed the Buddha in verse:

2.15.s:
“Kathaṁsu tarati oghaṁ,
rattindivamatandito;
Appatiṭṭhe anālambe,
ko gambhīre na sīdatī”ti.
2.15.e:
“Who here crosses the flood,
tireless all day and night?
Who, not standing and unsupported,
does not sink in the deep?”

2.15.s:
“Sabbadā sīlasampanno,
Paññavā susamāhito;
Āraddhavīriyo pahitatto,
Oghaṁ tarati duttaraṁ.
2.15.e:
“Someone who is always endowed with ethics,
wise and serene,
energetic and resolute,
crosses the flood so hard to cross.

2.15.s:
Virato kāmasaññāya,
rūpasaṁyojanātigo;
Nandīrāgaparikkhīṇo,
so gambhīre na sīdatī”ti.
2.15.e:
Someone who desists from sensual perception,
has moved past the fetter of form,
and has finished with relishing and greed
does not sink in the deep.”

2.16.s: Ekamantaṁ ṭhito kho vāsudatto devaputto bhagavato santike imaṁ gāthaṁ abhāsi:
2.16.e: Standing to one side, the godling Vāsudatta spoke this verse in the Buddha’s presence:

2.16.s:
“Sattiyā viya omaṭṭho,
ḍayhamānova matthake;
Kāmarāgappahānāya,
sato bhikkhu paribbaje”ti.
2.16.e:
“Like they’re struck by a sword,
like their head was on fire,
a mendicant should wander mindful,
to give up sensual desire.”

2.16.s:
“Sattiyā viya omaṭṭho,
ḍayhamānova matthake;
Sakkāyadiṭṭhippahānāya,
sato bhikkhu paribbaje”ti.
2.16.e:
“Like they’re struck by a sword,
like their head was on fire,
a mendicant should wander mindful,
to give up substantialist view.”

2.17.s: Ekamantaṁ ṭhito kho subrahmā devaputto bhagavantaṁ gāthāya ajjhabhāsi:
2.17.e: Standing to one side, the godling Subrahmā addressed the Buddha in verse:

“This mind is always anxious,
this mind is always stressed
about stresses that haven’t arisen
and those that have.
If there is a state free of anxiety,
please answer my question.”

2.17.s:
“Nāññatra bojjhā tapasā,
nāññatrindriyasaṁvarā;
Nāññatra sabbanissaggā,
sotthiṁ passāmi pāṇinan”ti.
2.17.e:
“Not without understanding and fervor,
not without restraining the sense faculties,
not without letting go of everything,
do I see safety for living creatures.”
That is what the Buddha said. … The godling vanished right there.

2.18.s: Evaṁ me sutaṁ— ekaṁ samayaṁ bhagavā sākete viharati añjanavane migadāye.
2.18.e: So I have heard. At one time the Buddha was staying near Sāketa in the deer park at the Añjana Wood.

2.18.s: Atha kho kakudho devaputto abhikkantāya rattiyā abhikkantavaṇṇo kevalakappaṁ añjanavanaṁ obhāsetvā yena bhagavā tenupasaṅkami; upasaṅkamitvā bhagavantaṁ abhivādetvā ekamantaṁ aṭṭhāsi. Ekamantaṁ ṭhito kho kakudho devaputto bhagavantaṁ etadavoca: “nandasi, samaṇā”ti?
2.18.e: Then, late at night, the glorious godling Kakudha, lighting up the entire Añjana Wood, went up to the Buddha, bowed, stood to one side, and said to him, “Do you delight, ascetic?”

2.18.s: “Tena hi, samaṇa, neva nandasi na ca socasī”ti?
2.18.e: “Well then, ascetic, do you neither delight nor sorrow?”

2.18.s:
“Kacci tvaṁ anagho bhikkhu,
kacci nandī na vijjati;
Kacci taṁ ekamāsīnaṁ,
aratī nābhikīratī”ti.
2.18.e:
“I hope you’re not gloomy, mendicant,
I hope that delight isn’t found in you.
I hope that discontent doesn’t
overwhelm you as you sit alone.”

2.18.s:
“Anagho ve ahaṁ yakkha,
atho nandī na vijjati;
Atho maṁ ekamāsīnaṁ,
aratī nābhikīratī”ti.
2.18.e:
“I’m genuinely not gloomy, spirit,
and no delight is found in me.
And also discontent doesn’t
overwhelm me as I sit alone.”

2.18.s:
“Kathaṁ tvaṁ anagho bhikkhu,
kathaṁ nandī na vijjati;
Kathaṁ taṁ ekamāsīnaṁ,
aratī nābhikīratī”ti.
2.18.e:
“How are you not gloomy, mendicant?
How is delight not found in you?
How does discontent not
overwhelm you as you sit alone?”

2.18.s:
“Aghajātassa ve nandī,
nandījātassa ve aghaṁ;
Anandī anagho bhikkhu,
evaṁ jānāhi āvuso”ti.
2.18.e:
“Delight is born from gloom,
gloom is born from delight;
sir, you should know me as
a mendicant free of delight and gloom.”

2.18.s:
“Cirassaṁ vata passāmi,
brāhmaṇaṁ parinibbutaṁ;
Anandiṁ anaghaṁ bhikkhuṁ,
tiṇṇaṁ loke visattikan”ti.
2.18.e:
“After a long time I see
a brahmin fully quenched.
A mendicant free of delight and gloom,
he has crossed over clinging to the world.”

2.19.s: Rājagahanidānaṁ. Ekamantaṁ ṭhito kho uttaro devaputto bhagavato santike imaṁ gāthaṁ abhāsi:
2.19.e: At Rājagaha. Standing to one side, the godling Uttara spoke this verse in the Buddha’s presence:

2.19.s:
“Upanīyati jīvitamappamāyu,
Jarūpanītassa na santi tāṇā;
Etaṁ bhayaṁ maraṇe pekkhamāno,
Puññāni kayirātha sukhāvahānī”ti.
2.19.e:
“This life, so very short, is led onward.
One led on to old age has no shelter.
Seeing this peril in death,
do good deeds that bring you joy.”

2.19.s:
“Upanīyati jīvitamappamāyu,
Jarūpanītassa na santi tāṇā;
Etaṁ bhayaṁ maraṇe pekkhamāno,
Lokāmisaṁ pajahe santipekkho”ti.
2.19.e:
“This life, so very short, is led onward.
One led on to old age has no shelter.
Seeing this peril in death,
a seeker of peace would drop the world’s bait.”

2.20.s: Ekamantaṁ ṭhito kho anāthapiṇḍiko devaputto bhagavato santike imā gāthāyo abhāsi:
2.20.e: Standing to one side, the godling Anāthapiṇḍika recited these verses in the Buddha’s presence:

2.20.s:
“Idañhi taṁ jetavanaṁ,
isisaṅghanisevitaṁ;
Āvutthaṁ dhammarājena,
pītisañjananaṁ mama.
2.20.e:
“This is indeed that Jeta’s Grove,
frequented by the Saṅgha of seers,
where the King of Dhamma stayed:
it brings me joy!

2.20.s:
Kammaṁ vijjā ca dhammo ca,
sīlaṁ jīvitamuttamaṁ;
Etena maccā sujjhanti,
na gottena dhanena vā.

Tasmā hi paṇḍito poso,
sampassaṁ atthamattano;
Yoniso vicine dhammaṁ,
evaṁ tattha visujjhati.
2.20.e:
That’s why an astute person,
seeing what’s good for themselves,
would examine the teaching rationally,
that’s how they become purified in that.

2.20.s:
Sāriputtova paññāya,
sīlena upasamena ca;
Yopi pāraṅgato bhikkhu,
etāvaparamo siyā”ti.
2.20.e:
Sāriputta is full of wisdom,
ethics, and peace.
Even a mendicant who has crossed over
might at best equal him.”

2.20.s: Idamavoca anāthapiṇḍiko devaputto. Idaṁ vatvā bhagavantaṁ abhivādetvā padakkhiṇaṁ katvā tatthevantaradhāyi.
2.20.e: That is what the godling Anāthapiṇḍika said. Then he bowed and respectfully circled the Buddha, keeping him on his right, before vanishing right there.

2.20.s: Atha kho bhagavā tassā rattiyā accayena bhikkhū āmantesi: “imaṁ, bhikkhave, rattiṁ aññataro devaputto abhikkantāya rattiyā abhikkantavaṇṇo kevalakappaṁ jetavanaṁ obhāsetvā yenāhaṁ tenupasaṅkami; upasaṅkamitvā maṁ abhivādetvā ekamantaṁ aṭṭhāsi. Ekamantaṁ ṭhito kho, bhikkhave, so devaputto mama santike imā gāthāyo abhāsi:
2.20.e: Then, when the night had passed, the Buddha addressed the mendicants: “Mendicants, tonight, a certain glorious godling, lighting up the entire Jeta’s Grove, came to me, bowed, stood to one side, and recited these verses in my presence.” The Buddha then repeated the verses in full.

2.20.s:
‘Idañhi taṁ jetavanaṁ,
isisaṅghanisevitaṁ;
Āvutthaṁ dhammarājena,
pītisañjananaṁ mama.

Kammaṁ vijjā ca dhammo ca,
sīlaṁ jīvitamuttamaṁ;
Etena maccā sujjhanti,
na gottena dhanena vā.

Tasmā hi paṇḍito poso,
sampassaṁ atthamattano;
Yoniso vicine dhammaṁ,
evaṁ tattha visujjhati.

Sāriputtova paññāya,
sīlena upasamena ca;
Yopi pāraṅgato bhikkhu,
etāvaparamo siyā’ti.
Idamavoca, bhikkhave, so devaputto. Idaṁ vatvā maṁ abhivādetvā padakkhiṇaṁ katvā tatthevantaradhāyī”ti.
Evaṁ vutte, āyasmā ānando bhagavantaṁ etadavoca: “so hi nūna, bhante, anāthapiṇḍiko devaputto bhavissati. Anāthapiṇḍiko gahapati āyasmante sāriputte abhippasanno ahosī”ti.
2.20.e: When he said this, Venerable Ānanda said to the Buddha, “Sir, that godling must surely have been Anāthapiṇḍika. For the householder Anāthapiṇḍika was devoted to Venerable Sāriputta.”

2.20.s: “Sādhu sādhu, ānanda, yāvatakaṁ kho, ānanda, takkāya pattabbaṁ anuppattaṁ taṁ tayā. Anāthapiṇḍiko hi so, ānanda, devaputto”ti.
2.20.e: “Good, good, Ānanda. You’ve reached the logical conclusion, as far as logic goes. For that was indeed the godling Anāthapiṇḍika.”

2.21.s: Evaṁ me sutaṁ— ekaṁ samayaṁ bhagavā sāvatthiyaṁ viharati jetavane anāthapiṇḍikassa ārāme.
2.21.e: So I have heard. At one time the Buddha was staying near Sāvatthī in Jeta’s Grove, Anāthapiṇḍika’s monastery.

2.21.s: Atha kho sivo devaputto abhikkantāya rattiyā abhikkantavaṇṇo kevalakappaṁ jetavanaṁ obhāsetvā yena bhagavā tenupasaṅkami; upasaṅkamitvā bhagavantaṁ abhivādetvā ekamantaṁ aṭṭhāsi. Ekamantaṁ ṭhito kho sivo devaputto bhagavato santike imā gāthāyo abhāsi:
2.21.e: Then, late at night, the glorious godling Shiva, lighting up the entire Jeta’s Grove, went up to the Buddha, bowed, stood to one side, and recited these verses in the Buddha’s presence:

2.21.s:
“Sabbhireva samāsetha,
sabbhi kubbetha santhavaṁ;
Sataṁ saddhammamaññāya,
seyyo hoti na pāpiyo.
2.21.e:
“Associate only with the virtuous!
Try to get close to the virtuous!
Understanding the true teaching of the good,
things get better, not worse.

2.21.s:
Sabbhireva samāsetha,
sabbhi kubbetha santhavaṁ;
Sataṁ saddhammamaññāya,
paññā labbhati nāññato.
2.21.e:
Associate only with the virtuous!
Try to get close to the virtuous!
Understanding the true teaching of the good,
wisdom is gained—but not from anyone else.

2.21.s:
Sabbhireva samāsetha,
sabbhi kubbetha santhavaṁ;
Sataṁ saddhammamaññāya,
sokamajjhe na socati.
2.21.e:
Associate only with the virtuous!
Try to get close to the virtuous!
Understanding the true teaching of the good,
you grieve not among the grieving.

2.21.s:
Sabbhireva samāsetha,
sabbhi kubbetha santhavaṁ;
Sataṁ saddhammamaññāya,
ñātimajjhe virocati.
2.21.e:
Associate only with the virtuous!
Try to get close to the virtuous!
Understanding the true teaching of the good,
you dazzle among your relatives.

2.21.s:
Sabbhireva samāsetha,
sabbhi kubbetha santhavaṁ;
Sataṁ saddhammamaññāya,
sattā gacchanti suggatiṁ.
2.21.e:
Associate only with the virtuous!
Try to get close to the virtuous!
Understanding the true teaching of the good,
sentient beings go to a good place.

2.21.s:
Sabbhireva samāsetha,
sabbhi kubbetha santhavaṁ;
Sataṁ saddhammamaññāya,
sattā tiṭṭhanti sātatan”ti.
2.21.e:
Associate only with the virtuous!
Try to get close to the virtuous!
Understanding the true teaching of the good,
sentient beings live happily.”

2.21.s: Atha kho bhagavā sivaṁ devaputtaṁ gāthāya paccabhāsi:
2.21.e: Then the Buddha replied to Shiva in verse:

2.21.s:
“Sabbhireva samāsetha,
sabbhi kubbetha santhavaṁ;
Sataṁ saddhammamaññāya,
sabbadukkhā pamuccatī”ti.
2.21.e:
“Associate only with the virtuous!
Try to get close to the virtuous!
Understanding the true teaching of the good,
you’re released from all suffering.”

2.22.s: Ekamantaṁ ṭhito kho khemo devaputto bhagavato santike imā gāthāyo abhāsi:
2.22.e: Standing to one side, the godling Khema recited these verses in the Buddha’s presence:

2.22.s:
“Caranti bālā dummedhā,
amitteneva attanā;
Karontā pāpakaṁ kammaṁ,
yaṁ hoti kaṭukapphalaṁ.
2.22.e:
“Fools and simpletons behave
like their own worst enemies,
doing wicked deeds
that ripen as bitter fruit.

2.22.s:
Na taṁ kammaṁ kataṁ sādhu,
yaṁ katvā anutappati;
Yassa assumukho rodaṁ,
vipākaṁ paṭisevati.
2.22.e:
It’s not good to do a deed
that plagues you later on,
for which you weep and wail,
as its effect stays with you.

2.22.s:
Tañca kammaṁ kataṁ sādhu,
yaṁ katvā nānutappati;
Yassa patīto sumano,
vipākaṁ paṭisevati.
2.22.e:
It is good to do a deed
that doesn’t plague you later on,
that gladdens and cheers,
as its effect stays with you.”

2.22.s:
Paṭikacceva taṁ kayirā,
yaṁ jaññā hitamattano;
Na sākaṭikacintāya,
mantā dhīro parakkame.
2.22.e:
“As a precaution, you should do
what you know is for your own welfare.
A thinker, an attentive one would not proceed
thinking like the cart driver.

2.22.s:
Yathā sākaṭiko maṭṭhaṁ,
samaṁ hitvā mahāpathaṁ;
Visamaṁ maggamāruyha,
akkhacchinnova jhāyati.
2.22.e:
Suppose a cart driver leaves the highway,
so even and well compacted.
They enter upon a rough road,
and fret as soon as their axle is broken.

2.22.s:
Evaṁ dhammā apakkamma,
adhammamanuvattiya;
Mando maccumukhaṁ patto,
akkhacchinnova jhāyatī”ti.
2.22.e:
So too, a dullard leaves the good
to follow what’s against the good.
Fallen in the jaws of death,
they fret like one whose axle is broken.”

2.23.s: Ekamantaṁ ṭhito kho serī devaputto bhagavantaṁ gāthāya ajjhabhāsi:
2.23.e: Standing to one side, the godling Serī addressed the Buddha in verse:

2.23.s:
“Annamevābhinandanti,
ubhaye devamānusā;
Atha ko nāma so yakkho,
yaṁ annaṁ nābhinandatī”ti.
2.23.e:
“Both gods and humans
enjoy their food.
So what’s the name of the spirit
who doesn’t like food?”

2.23.s:
“Ye naṁ dadanti saddhāya,
vippasannena cetasā;
Tameva annaṁ bhajati,
asmiṁ loke paramhi ca.
2.23.e:
“Those who give with faith
and a clear and confident heart,
partake of food
in this world and the next.

2.23.s:
Tasmā vineyya maccheraṁ,
dajjā dānaṁ malābhibhū;
Puññāni paralokasmiṁ,
patiṭṭhā honti pāṇinan”ti.
2.23.e:
So you should dispel stinginess,
overcoming that stain, and give a gift.
The good deeds of sentient beings
support them in the next world.”

2.23.s: “Acchariyaṁ, bhante, abbhutaṁ, bhante. Yāvasubhāsitamidaṁ, bhante, bhagavatā:
2.23.e: “It’s incredible, sir, it’s amazing, how well said this was by the Buddha.” He repeated the Buddha’s verses, and said:

2.23.s:
‘Ye naṁ dadanti saddhāya,
vippasannena cetasā;
Tameva annaṁ bhajati,
asmiṁ loke paramhi ca.

Tasmā vineyya maccheraṁ,
dajjā dānaṁ malābhibhū;
Puññāni paralokasmiṁ,
patiṭṭhā honti pāṇinan’ti.

Bhūtapubbāhaṁ, bhante, sirī nāma rājā ahosiṁ dāyako dānapati dānassa vaṇṇavādī. Tassa mayhaṁ, bhante, catūsu dvāresu dānaṁ dīyittha samaṇabrāhmaṇakapaṇaddhikavanibbakayācakānaṁ. Atha kho maṁ, bhante, itthāgāraṁ upasaṅkamitvā etadavoca: ‘devassa kho dānaṁ dīyati; amhākaṁ dānaṁ na dīyati. Sādhu mayampi devaṁ nissāya dānāni dadeyyāma, puññāni kareyyāmā’ti. Tassa mayhaṁ, bhante, etadahosi: ‘ahaṁ khosmi dāyako dānapati dānassa vaṇṇavādī. Dānaṁ dassāmāti vadante kinti vadeyyan’ti? So khvāhaṁ, bhante, paṭhamaṁ dvāraṁ itthāgārassa adāsiṁ. Tattha itthāgārassa dānaṁ dīyittha; mama dānaṁ paṭikkami.
2.23.e: “Once upon a time, sir, I was a king named Serī, a giver, a donor, who praised giving. I gave gifts at the four gates to ascetics and brahmins, to paupers, vagrants, supplicants, and beggars. Then the ladies of my harem approached me and said, ‘Your Majesty gives gifts, but we don’t. Your Majesty, please support us to give gifts and make merit.’ Then it occurred to me, ‘I’m a giver, a donor, who praises giving. When they say, “We would give gifts”, what am I to say?’ And so I gave the first gate to the ladies of my harem. There they gave gifts, while my own giving dwindled.

2.23.s: Atha kho maṁ, bhante, khattiyā anuyantā upasaṅkamitvā etadavocuṁ: ‘devassa kho dānaṁ dīyati; itthāgārassa dānaṁ dīyati; amhākaṁ dānaṁ na dīyati. Sādhu mayampi devaṁ nissāya dānāni dadeyyāma, puññāni kareyyāmā’ti. Tassa mayhaṁ, bhante, etadahosi: ‘ahaṁ khosmi dāyako dānapati dānassa vaṇṇavādī. Dānaṁ dassāmāti vadante kinti vadeyyan’ti? So khvāhaṁ, bhante, dutiyaṁ dvāraṁ khattiyānaṁ anuyantānaṁ adāsiṁ. Tattha khattiyānaṁ anuyantānaṁ dānaṁ dīyittha, mama dānaṁ paṭikkami.
2.23.e: Then my aristocrat vassals approached me and said, ‘Your Majesty gives gifts, the ladies of your harem give gifts, but we don’t. Your Majesty, please support us to give gifts and make merit.’ Then it occurred to me, ‘I’m a giver, a donor, who praises giving. When they say, “We would give gifts”, what am I to say?’ And so I gave the second gate to my aristocrat vassals. There they gave gifts, while my own giving dwindled.

2.23.s: Atha kho maṁ, bhante, balakāyo upasaṅkamitvā etadavoca: ‘devassa kho dānaṁ dīyati; itthāgārassa dānaṁ dīyati; khattiyānaṁ anuyantānaṁ dānaṁ dīyati; amhākaṁ dānaṁ na dīyati. Sādhu mayampi devaṁ nissāya dānāni dadeyyāma, puññāni kareyyāmā’ti. Tassa mayhaṁ, bhante, etadahosi: ‘ahaṁ khosmi dāyako dānapati dānassa vaṇṇavādī. Dānaṁ dassāmāti vadante kinti vadeyyan’ti? So khvāhaṁ, bhante, tatiyaṁ dvāraṁ balakāyassa adāsiṁ. Tattha balakāyassa dānaṁ dīyittha, mama dānaṁ paṭikkami.
2.23.e: Then my troops approached me and said, ‘Your Majesty gives gifts, the ladies of your harem give gifts, your aristocrat vassals give gifts, but we don’t. Your Majesty, please support us to give gifts and make merit.’ Then it occurred to me, ‘I’m a giver, a donor, who praises giving. When they say, “We would give gifts”, what am I to say?’ And so I gave the third gate to my troops. There they gave gifts, while my own giving dwindled.

2.23.s: Atha kho maṁ, bhante, brāhmaṇagahapatikā upasaṅkamitvā etadavocuṁ: ‘devassa kho dānaṁ dīyati; itthāgārassa dānaṁ dīyati; khattiyānaṁ anuyantānaṁ dānaṁ dīyati; balakāyassa dānaṁ dīyati; amhākaṁ dānaṁ na dīyati. Sādhu mayampi devaṁ nissāya dānāni dadeyyāma, puññāni kareyyāmā’ti. Tassa mayhaṁ, bhante, etadahosi: ‘ahaṁ khosmi dāyako dānapati dānassa vaṇṇavādī. Dānaṁ dassāmāti vadante kinti vadeyyan’ti? So khvāhaṁ, bhante, catutthaṁ dvāraṁ brāhmaṇagahapatikānaṁ adāsiṁ. Tattha brāhmaṇagahapatikānaṁ dānaṁ dīyittha, mama dānaṁ paṭikkami.
2.23.e: Then my brahmins and householders approached me and said, ‘Your Majesty gives gifts, the ladies of your harem give gifts, your aristocrat vassals give gifts, your troops give gifts, but we don’t. Your Majesty, please support us to give gifts and make merit.’ Then it occurred to me, ‘I’m a giver, a donor, who praises giving. When they say, “We would give gifts”, what am I to say?’ And so I gave the fourth gate to my brahmins and householders. There they gave gifts, while my own giving dwindled.

2.23.s: Atha kho maṁ, bhante, purisā upasaṅkamitvā etadavocuṁ: ‘na kho dāni devassa koci dānaṁ dīyatī’ti. Evaṁ vuttāhaṁ, bhante, te purise etadavocaṁ: ‘tena hi, bhaṇe, yo bāhiresu janapadesu āyo sañjāyati tato upaḍḍhaṁ antepure pavesetha, upaḍḍhaṁ tattheva dānaṁ detha samaṇabrāhmaṇakapaṇaddhikavanibbakayācakānan’ti. So khvāhaṁ, bhante, evaṁ dīgharattaṁ katānaṁ puññānaṁ evaṁ dīgharattaṁ katānaṁ kusalānaṁ dhammānaṁ pariyantaṁ nādhigacchāmi— ettakaṁ puññanti vā ettako puññavipākoti vā ettakaṁ sagge ṭhātabbanti vāti. Acchariyaṁ, bhante, abbhutaṁ, bhante. Yāvasubhāsitamidaṁ, bhante, bhagavatā:
2.23.e: Then my men approached me and said, ‘Now Your Majesty is not giving gifts anywhere!’ When they said this, I said to those men, ‘Well then, lads, deposit half the revenue generated in the outer districts in the royal compound. Give the other half as charity to ascetics and brahmins, to paupers, vagrants, supplicants, and beggars in those districts.’ Sir, for a long time I made so much merit and did so many skillful deeds. I never reached any limit so as to say ‘there’s this much merit’ or ‘there’s this much result of merit’ or ‘for so long I’ll remain in heaven’. It’s incredible, sir, it’s amazing, how well said this was by the Buddha.

2.23.s:
‘Ye naṁ dadanti saddhāya,
vippasannena cetasā;
Tameva annaṁ bhajati,
asmiṁ loke paramhi ca.
2.23.e:
‘Those who give with faith
and a clear and confident heart,
partake of food
in this world and the next.

2.23.s:
Tasmā vineyya maccheraṁ,
dajjā dānaṁ malābhibhū;
Puññāni paralokasmiṁ,
patiṭṭhā honti pāṇinan’”ti.
2.23.e:
So you should dispel stinginess,
overcoming that stain, and give a gift.
The good deeds of sentient beings
support them in the next world.’”

2.24.s: Ekamantaṁ ṭhito kho ghaṭīkāro devaputto bhagavato santike imaṁ gāthaṁ abhāsi:
2.24.e: Standing to one side, the godling Ghaṭīkāra spoke this verse in the Buddha’s presence:

2.24.s:
“Avihaṁ upapannāse,
vimuttā satta bhikkhavo;
Rāgadosaparikkhīṇā,
tiṇṇā loke visattikan”ti.
2.24.e:
“Seven mendicants reborn in Aviha
have been freed.
With the complete ending of greed and hate,
they’ve crossed over clinging to the world.”

2.24.s:
“Ke ca te ataruṁ paṅkaṁ,
maccudheyyaṁ suduttaraṁ;
Ke hitvā mānusaṁ dehaṁ,
dibbayogaṁ upaccagun”ti.
2.24.e:
“Who are those who’ve crossed the bog,
Death’s dominion so hard to pass?
Who, after leaving behind the human body,
have risen above celestial yokes?”

“Upaka and Palagaṇḍa,
and Pukkusāti, these three;
Bhaddiya and Bhaddadeva,
and Bāhudantī and Piṅgiya.
They, after leaving behind the human body,
have risen above celestial yokes.”

2.24.s:
“Kusalī bhāsasī tesaṁ,
mārapāsappahāyinaṁ;
Kassa te dhammamaññāya,
acchiduṁ bhavabandhanan”ti.
2.24.e:
“You speak well of them,
who have let go the snares of Māra.
Whose teaching did they understand
to cut the bonds of rebirth?”

2.24.s:
“Na aññatra bhagavatā,
nāññatra tava sāsanā;
Yassa te dhammamaññāya,
acchiduṁ bhavabandhanaṁ.
2.24.e:
“None other than the Blessed One!
None other than your instruction!
It was your teaching that they understood
to cut the bonds of rebirth.

2.24.s:
Yattha nāmañca rūpañca,
asesaṁ uparujjhati;
Taṁ te dhammaṁ idhaññāya,
acchiduṁ bhavabandhanan”ti.
2.24.e:
Where name and form
cease with no residue left behind;
understanding this teaching,
they cut the bonds of rebirth.”

2.24.s:
“Gambhīraṁ bhāsasī vācaṁ,
dubbijānaṁ sudubbudhaṁ;
Kassa tvaṁ dhammamaññāya,
vācaṁ bhāsasi īdisan”ti.
2.24.e:
“The words you say are deep,
hard to understand, so very hard to wake up to.
Whose teaching did you understand
to be able to say such things?”

2.24.s:
“Kumbhakāro pure āsiṁ,
vekaḷiṅge ghaṭīkaro;
Mātāpettibharo āsiṁ,
kassapassa upāsako.
2.24.e:
“In the past I was a potter
in Vebhaliṅga named Ghaṭīkāra.
I took care of my parents
as a lay follower of Buddha Kassapa.

2.24.s:
Virato methunā dhammā,
brahmacārī nirāmiso;
Ahuvā te sagāmeyyo,
ahuvā te pure sakhā.
2.24.e:
I refrained from sexual intercourse,
I was chaste, spiritual.
We lived in the same village;
in the past I was your comrade.

2.24.s:
Sohamete pajānāmi,
vimutte satta bhikkhavo;
Rāgadosaparikkhīṇe,
tiṇṇe loke visattikan”ti.
2.24.e:
I am the one who understands
that these seven mendicants have been freed.
With the complete ending of greed and hate,
they’ve crossed over clinging to the world.”

2.24.s:
“Evametaṁ tadā āsi,
yathā bhāsasi bhaggava;
Kumbhakāro pure āsi,
vekaḷiṅge ghaṭīkaro.
2.24.e:
“That’s exactly how it was,
just as you say, Bhaggava.
In the past you were a potter
in Vebhaliṅga named Ghaṭīkāra.

You took care of your parents
as a lay follower of Buddha Kassapa.
You refrained from sexual intercourse,
you were chaste, spiritual.
We lived in the same village;
in the past you were my comrade.”

2.24.s:
“Evametaṁ purāṇānaṁ,
sahāyānaṁ ahu saṅgamo;
Ubhinnaṁ bhāvitattānaṁ,
sarīrantimadhārinan”ti.
2.24.e:
“That’s how it was
when those friends of old met again.
Both of them are evolved,
and bear their final body.”

2.25.s: ekaṁ samayaṁ sambahulā bhikkhū, kosalesu viharanti himavantapasse araññakuṭikāya uddhatā unnaḷā capalā mukharā vikiṇṇavācā muṭṭhassatino asampajānā asamāhitā vibbhantacittā pākatindriyā.
2.25.e: At one time several mendicants were staying in the Kosalan lands, in a wilderness hut on the slopes of the Himalayas. They were haughty, insolent, fickle, scurrilous, loose-tongued, unmindful, lacking situational awareness and immersion, with straying minds and undisciplined faculties.

2.25.s: Atha kho jantu devaputto tadahuposathe pannarase yena te bhikkhū tenupasaṅkami; upasaṅkamitvā te bhikkhū gāthāhi ajjhabhāsi:
2.25.e: Then on the fifteenth day sabbath the godling Jantu went up to those mendicants and addressed them in verse:

“The mendicants used to live happily,
as disciples of Gotama.
Desireless they sought alms;
desireless they used their lodgings.
Knowing that the world was impermanent
they made an end of suffering.

2.25.s:
Dupposaṁ katvā attānaṁ,
gāme gāmaṇikā viya;
Bhutvā bhutvā nipajjanti,
parāgāresu mucchitā.
2.25.e:
But now they’ve made themselves hard to look after,
like chiefs in a village.
They eat and eat and then lie down,
passed out in the homes of others.

2.25.s:
Saṅghassa añjaliṁ katvā,
idhekacce vadāmahaṁ;
Apaviddhā anāthā te,
yathā petā tatheva te.
2.25.e:
Having raised my cupped palms to the Saṅgha,
I speak here only about certain people.
They’re dregs, with no protector,
just like those who have passed away.

2.25.s:
Ye kho pamattā viharanti,
te me sandhāya bhāsitaṁ;
Ye appamattā viharanti,
namo tesaṁ karomahan”ti.
2.25.e:
I’m speaking about
those who live negligently.
To those who live diligently
I pay homage.”

2.26.s: Ekamantaṁ ṭhito kho rohitasso devaputto bhagavantaṁ etadavoca:
2.26.e: Standing to one side, the godling Rohitassa said to the Buddha:

2.26.s: “yattha nu kho, bhante, na jāyati na jīyati na mīyati na cavati na upapajjati, sakkā nu kho so, bhante, gamanena lokassa anto ñātuṁ vā daṭṭhuṁ vā pāpuṇituṁ vā”ti?
2.26.e: “Sir, is it possible to know or see or reach the end of the world by traveling to a place where there’s no being born, growing old, dying, passing away, or being reborn?”

2.26.s: “Yattha kho, āvuso, na jāyati na jīyati na mīyati na cavati na upapajjati, nāhaṁ taṁ gamanena lokassa antaṁ ñāteyyaṁ daṭṭheyyaṁ patteyyanti vadāmī”ti.
2.26.e: “Reverend, I say it’s not possible to know or see or reach the end of the world by traveling to a place where there’s no being born, growing old, dying, passing away, or being reborn.”

2.26.s: “Acchariyaṁ, bhante, abbhutaṁ, bhante. Yāvasubhāsitamidaṁ, bhante, bhagavatā: ‘yattha kho, āvuso, na jāyati na jīyati na mīyati na cavati na upapajjati, nāhaṁ taṁ gamanena lokassa antaṁ ñāteyyaṁ daṭṭheyyaṁ patteyyanti vadāmī’ti.
2.26.e: “It’s incredible, sir, it’s amazing, how well said this was by the Buddha.

2.26.s: Bhūtapubbāhaṁ, bhante, rohitasso nāma isi ahosiṁ bhojaputto iddhimā vehāsaṅgamo. Tassa mayhaṁ, bhante, evarūpo javo ahosi; seyyathāpi nāma daḷhadhammā dhanuggaho susikkhito katahattho katayoggo katūpāsano lahukena asanena appakasireneva tiriyaṁ tālacchāyaṁ atipāteyya. Tassa mayhaṁ, bhante, evarūpo padavītihāro ahosi; seyyathāpi nāma puratthimā samuddā pacchimo samuddo. Tassa mayhaṁ, bhante, evarūpaṁ icchāgataṁ uppajji: ‘ahaṁ gamanena lokassa antaṁ pāpuṇissāmī’ti. So khvāhaṁ, bhante, evarūpena javena samannāgato evarūpena ca padavītihārena, aññatreva asitapītakhāyitasāyitā aññatra uccārapassāvakammā aññatra niddākilamathapaṭivinodanā vassasatāyuko vassasatajīvī vassasataṁ gantvā appatvāva lokassa antaṁ antarāva kālaṅkato.
2.26.e: Once upon a time, I was a seer named Rohitassa, son of the benefactors. I was a sky-walker with psychic powers. I was as fast as a light arrow easily shot across the shadow of a palm tree by a well-trained expert archer with a strong bow. My stride was such that it could span from the eastern ocean to the western ocean. This wish came to me: ‘I will reach the end of the world by traveling.’ Having such speed and stride, I traveled for my whole lifespan of a hundred years—pausing only to eat and drink, go to the toilet, and sleep to dispel weariness—and I passed away along the way, never reaching the end of the world.

2.26.s: Acchariyaṁ, bhante, abbhutaṁ, bhante. Yāvasubhāsitamidaṁ, bhante, bhagavatā: ‘yattha kho, āvuso, na jāyati na jīyati na mīyati na cavati na upapajjati, nāhaṁ taṁ gamanena lokassa antaṁ ñāteyyaṁ daṭṭheyyaṁ patteyyanti vadāmī’”ti.
2.26.e: It’s incredible, sir, it’s amazing, how well said this was by the Buddha. ‘Reverend, I say it’s not possible to know or see or reach the end of the world by traveling to a place where there’s no being born, growing old, dying, passing away, or being reborn.’”

2.26.s: “Na kho panāhaṁ, āvuso, appatvā lokassa antaṁ dukkhassa antakiriyaṁ vadāmi. Api ca khvāhaṁ, āvuso, imasmiṁyeva byāmamatte kaḷevare sasaññimhi samanake lokañca paññapemi lokasamudayañca lokanirodhañca lokanirodhagāminiñca paṭipadanti.
2.26.e: “But Reverend, I also say there’s no making an end of suffering without reaching the end of the world. For it is in this fathom-long carcass with its perception and mind that I describe the world, its origin, its cessation, and the practice that leads to its cessation.

2.26.s:
Gamanena na pattabbo,
lokassanto kudācanaṁ;
Na ca appatvā lokantaṁ,
dukkhā atthi pamocanaṁ.
2.26.e:
The end of the world can never
be reached by traveling.
But without reaching the end of the world,
there’s no release from suffering.

2.26.s:
Tasmā have lokavidū sumedho,
Lokantagū vusitabrahmacariyo;
Lokassa antaṁ samitāvi ñatvā,
Nāsīsati lokamimaṁ parañcā”ti.
2.26.e:
So an intelligent person, understanding the world,
has completed the spiritual journey <j>and gone to the end of the world.
Assuaged, knowing the end of the world,
they do not hope for this world or the next.”

2.27.s: Ekamantaṁ ṭhito kho nando devaputto bhagavato santike imaṁ gāthaṁ abhāsi:
2.27.e: Standing to one side, the godling Nanda spoke this verse in the Buddha’s presence:

2.27.s:
“Accenti kālā tarayanti rattiyo,
Vayoguṇā anupubbaṁ jahanti;
Etaṁ bhayaṁ maraṇe pekkhamāno,
Puññāni kayirātha sukhāvahānī”ti.
2.27.e:
“Time flies, nights pass by,
the stages of life leave us one by one.
Seeing this peril in death,
do good deeds that bring you joy.”

2.27.s:
“Accenti kālā tarayanti rattiyo,
Vayoguṇā anupubbaṁ jahanti;
Etaṁ bhayaṁ maraṇe pekkhamāno,
Lokāmisaṁ pajahe santipekkho”ti.
2.27.e:
“Time flies, nights pass by,
the stages of life leave us one by one.
Seeing this peril in death,
a seeker of peace would drop the world’s bait.”

2.28.s: Ekamantaṁ ṭhito kho nandivisālo devaputto bhagavantaṁ gāthāya ajjhabhāsi:
2.28.e: Standing to one side, the godling Nandivisāla addressed the Buddha in verse:

2.28.s:
“Catucakkaṁ navadvāraṁ,
puṇṇaṁ lobhena saṁyutaṁ;
Paṅkajātaṁ mahāvīra,
kathaṁ yātrā bhavissatī”ti.
2.28.e:
“Four are its wheels, and nine its doors;
it’s stuffed full, bound with greed,
and born from a bog.
Great hero, how will I keep going?”

2.28.s:
“Chetvā naddhiṁ varattañca,
icchālobhañca pāpakaṁ;
Samūlaṁ taṇhamabbuyha,
evaṁ yātrā bhavissatī”ti.
2.28.e:
“Having cut the strap and harness—
wicked desire and greed—
and having plucked out craving, root and all:
that’s how you will keep going.”

2.29.s: Atha kho āyasmā ānando yena bhagavā tenupasaṅkami; upasaṅkamitvā bhagavantaṁ abhivādetvā ekamantaṁ nisīdi. Ekamantaṁ nisinnaṁ kho āyasmantaṁ ānandaṁ bhagavā etadavoca: “tuyhampi no, ānanda, sāriputto ruccatī”ti?
2.29.e: Then Venerable Ānanda went up to the Buddha, bowed, and sat down to one side. The Buddha said to him, “Ānanda, do you endorse Sāriputta?”

2.29.s: “Kassa hi nāma, bhante, abālassa aduṭṭhassa amūḷhassa avipallatthacittassa āyasmā sāriputto na rucceyya? Paṇḍito, bhante, āyasmā sāriputto. Mahāpañño, bhante, āyasmā sāriputto. Puthupañño, bhante, āyasmā sāriputto. Hāsapañño, bhante, āyasmā sāriputto. Javanapañño, bhante, āyasmā sāriputto. Tikkhapañño, bhante, āyasmā sāriputto. Nibbedhikapañño, bhante, āyasmā sāriputto. Appiccho, bhante, āyasmā sāriputto. Santuṭṭho, bhante, āyasmā sāriputto. Pavivitto, bhante, āyasmā sāriputto. Asaṁsaṭṭho, bhante, āyasmā sāriputto. Āraddhavīriyo, bhante, āyasmā sāriputto. Vattā, bhante, āyasmā sāriputto. Vacanakkhamo, bhante, āyasmā sāriputto. Codako, bhante, āyasmā sāriputto. Pāpagarahī, bhante, āyasmā sāriputto. Kassa hi nāma, bhante, abālassa aduṭṭhassa amūḷhassa avipallatthacittassa āyasmā sāriputto na rucceyyā”ti?
2.29.e: “Sir, who on earth would not endorse Venerable Sāriputta unless they’re a fool, a hater, delusional, or mentally deranged? Venerable Sāriputta is astute, he has great wisdom, widespread wisdom, laughing wisdom, swift wisdom, sharp wisdom, and penetrating wisdom. He has few wishes, he’s content, secluded, aloof, and energetic. He is a preacher, and he accepts advice; he accuses and criticizes wickedness. Who on earth would not endorse Venerable Sāriputta unless they’re a fool, a hater, delusional, or mentally deranged?”

2.29.s: “Evametaṁ, ānanda, evametaṁ, ānanda. Kassa hi nāma, ānanda, abālassa aduṭṭhassa amūḷhassa avipallatthacittassa sāriputto na rucceyya? Paṇḍito, ānanda, sāriputto. Mahāpañño, ānanda, sāriputto. Puthupañño, ānanda, sāriputto. Hāsapañño, ānanda, sāriputto. Javanapañño, ānanda, sāriputto. Tikkhapañño, ānanda, sāriputto. Nibbedhikapañño, ānanda, sāriputto. Appiccho, ānanda, sāriputto. Santuṭṭho, ānanda, sāriputto. Pavivitto, ānanda, sāriputto. Asaṁsaṭṭho, ānanda, sāriputto. Āraddhavīriyo, ānanda, sāriputto. Vattā, ānanda, sāriputto. Vacanakkhamo, ānanda, sāriputto. Codako, ānanda, sāriputto. Pāpagarahī, ānanda, sāriputto. Kassa hi nāma, ānanda, abālassa aduṭṭhassa amūḷhassa avipallatthacittassa sāriputto na rucceyyā”ti?
2.29.e: “That’s so true, Ānanda! That’s so true! Who on earth would not endorse Venerable Sāriputta unless they’re a fool, a hater, delusional, or mentally deranged?” And the Buddha repeated all of Ānanda’s terms of praise.

2.29.s: Atha kho susimo devaputto āyasmato sāriputtassa vaṇṇe bhaññamāne mahatiyā devaputtaparisāya parivuto yena bhagavā tenupasaṅkami; upasaṅkamitvā bhagavantaṁ abhivādetvā ekamantaṁ aṭṭhāsi. Ekamantaṁ ṭhito kho susimo devaputto bhagavantaṁ etadavoca:
2.29.e: While this praise of Sāriputta was being spoken, the godling Susīma approached the Buddha, escorted by a large assembly of godlings. He bowed, stood to one side, and said to him:

2.29.s: “Evametaṁ, bhagavā, evametaṁ, sugata. Kassa hi nāma, bhante, abālassa aduṭṭhassa amūḷhassa avipallatthacittassa āyasmā sāriputto na rucceyya? Paṇḍito, bhante, āyasmā sāriputto. Mahāpañño, bhante, puthupañño, bhante, hāsapañño, bhante, javanapañño, bhante, tikkhapañño, bhante, nibbedhikapañño, bhante, appiccho, bhante, santuṭṭho, bhante, pavivitto, bhante, asaṁsaṭṭho, bhante, āraddhavīriyo, bhante, vattā, bhante, vacanakkhamo, bhante, codako, bhante, pāpagarahī, bhante, āyasmā sāriputto. Kassa hi nāma, bhante, abālassa aduṭṭhassa amūḷhassa avipallatthacittassa āyasmā sāriputto na rucceyya? Ahampi hi, bhante, yaññadeva devaputtaparisaṁ upasaṅkamiṁ, etadeva bahulaṁ saddaṁ suṇāmi: ‘paṇḍito āyasmā sāriputto; mahāpañño āyasmā, puthupañño āyasmā, hāsapañño āyasmā, javanapañño āyasmā, tikkhapañño āyasmā, nibbedhikapañño āyasmā, appiccho āyasmā, santuṭṭho āyasmā, pavivitto āyasmā, asaṁsaṭṭho āyasmā, āraddhavīriyo āyasmā, vattā āyasmā, vacanakkhamo āyasmā, codako āyasmā, pāpagarahī āyasmā sāriputto’ti. Kassa hi nāma, bhante, abālassa aduṭṭhassa amūḷhassa avipallatthacittassa āyasmā sāriputto na rucceyyā”ti?
2.29.e: “That’s so true, Blessed One! That’s so true, Holy One! Who on earth would not endorse Venerable Sāriputta unless they’re a fool, a hater, delusional, or mentally deranged?” And he too repeated all the terms of praise of Sāriputta, adding, “For I too, sir, whenever I go to an assembly of godlings, frequently hear the same terms of praise.”

2.29.s: Atha kho susimassa devaputtassa devaputtaparisā āyasmato sāriputtassa vaṇṇe bhaññamāne attamanā pamuditā pītisomanassajātā uccāvacā vaṇṇanibhā upadaṁseti.
2.29.e: While this praise of Sāriputta was being spoken, the godlings of Susīma’s assembly—uplifted and overjoyed, full of rapture and happiness—displayed a rainbow of bright colors.

2.29.s: Seyyathāpi nāma maṇi veḷuriyo subho jātimā aṭṭhaṁso suparikammakato paṇḍukambale nikkhitto bhāsate ca tapate ca virocati ca; evamevaṁ susimassa devaputtassa devaputtaparisā āyasmato sāriputtassa vaṇṇe bhaññamāne attamanā pamuditā pītisomanassajātā uccāvacā vaṇṇanibhā upadaṁseti.
2.29.e: Suppose there was a beryl gem that was naturally lustrous, eight-faceted, well-worked. When placed on a cream rug it would sine and glow and dazzle. In the same way, the godlings of Susīma’s assembly displayed a rainbow of bright colors.

2.29.s: Seyyathāpi nāma nikkhaṁ jambonadaṁ dakkhakammāraputtaukkāmukhasukusalasampahaṭṭhaṁ paṇḍukambale nikkhittaṁ bhāsate ca tapate ca virocati ca; evamevaṁ susimassa devaputtassa devaputtaparisā āyasmato sāriputtassa vaṇṇe bhaññamāne attamanā pamuditā pītisomanassajātā uccāvacā vaṇṇanibhā upadaṁseti.
2.29.e: Suppose there was a pendant of Black Plum River gold, fashioned by a deft smith, well wrought in the forge. When placed on a cream rug it would shine and glow and dazzle. In the same way, the godlings of Susīma’s assembly displayed a rainbow of bright colors.

2.29.s: Seyyathāpi nāma saradasamaye viddhe vigatavalāhake deve rattiyā paccūsasamayaṁ osadhitārakā bhāsate ca tapate ca virocati ca; evamevaṁ susimassa devaputtassa devaputtaparisā āyasmato sāriputtassa vaṇṇe bhaññamāne attamanā pamuditā pītisomanassajātā uccāvacā vaṇṇanibhā upadaṁseti.
2.29.e: Suppose that in the autumn the heavens were clear and cloudless. At the crack of dawn, the morning star shines and glows and dazzles. In the same way, the godlings of Susīma’s assembly displayed a rainbow of bright colors.

2.29.s: Seyyathāpi nāma saradasamaye viddhe vigatavalāhake deve ādicco nabhaṁ abbhussakkamāno sabbaṁ ākāsagataṁ tamagataṁ abhivihacca bhāsate ca tapate ca virocati ca; evamevaṁ susimassa devaputtassa devaputtaparisā āyasmato sāriputtassa vaṇṇe bhaññamāne attamanā pamuditā pītisomanassajātā uccāvacā vaṇṇanibhā upadaṁseti.
2.29.e: Suppose that in the autumn the heavens were clear and cloudless. As the sun is rising to the firmament, having dispelled all the darkness of space, shines and glows and dazzles. In the same way, the godlings of Susīma’s assembly displayed a rainbow of bright colors.

2.29.s: Atha kho susimo devaputto āyasmantaṁ sāriputtaṁ ārabbha bhagavato santike imaṁ gāthaṁ abhāsi:
2.29.e: Then the godling Susīma spoke this verse about Venerable Sāriputta in the Buddha’s presence:

2.29.s:
“Paṇḍitoti samaññāto,
sāriputto akodhano;
Appiccho sorato danto,
satthuvaṇṇābhato isī”ti.
2.29.e:
“He’s considered astute,
Sāriputta, free of anger.
Few in wishes, gentle, tamed,
the seer shines in the Teacher’s praise!”

2.29.s: Atha kho bhagavā āyasmantaṁ sāriputtaṁ ārabbha susimaṁ devaputtaṁ gāthāya paccabhāsi:
2.29.e: Then the Buddha replied to Susīma with this verse about Venerable Sāriputta:

2.29.s:
“Paṇḍitoti samaññāto,
sāriputto akodhano;
Appiccho sorato danto,
kālaṁ kaṅkhati sudanto”ti.
2.29.e:
“He’s considered astute,
Sāriputta, free of anger.
Few in wishes, gentle, tamed;
developed and well-tamed, he awaits his time.”

2.30.s: Evaṁ me sutaṁ— ekaṁ samayaṁ bhagavā rājagahe viharati veḷuvane kalandakanivāpe.
2.30.e: So I have heard. At one time the Buddha was staying near Rājagaha in the Bamboo Grove, the squirrels’ feeding ground.
2.30.t: The Disciples of Various Monastics of Other Religions (Nānātitthiyasāvakasutta)

2.30.s: Atha kho sambahulā nānātitthiyasāvakā devaputtā asamo ca sahali ca nīko ca ākoṭako ca vegabbhari ca māṇavagāmiyo ca abhikkantāya rattiyā abhikkantavaṇṇā kevalakappaṁ veḷuvanaṁ obhāsetvā yena bhagavā tenupasaṅkamiṁsu; upasaṅkamitvā bhagavantaṁ abhivādetvā ekamantaṁ aṭṭhaṁsu.
2.30.e: Then, late at night, several glorious godlings lit up the entire Bamboo Grove. They were Asama, Sahalī, Niṅka, Ākoṭaka, Veṭambarī, and Māṇavagāmiya, and all of them were disciples of various monastics of other religions. They went up to the Buddha, bowed, and stood to one side.

2.30.s: Ekamantaṁ ṭhito kho asamo devaputto pūraṇaṁ kassapaṁ ārabbha bhagavato santike imaṁ gāthaṁ abhāsi:
2.30.e: Standing to one side, the godling Asama spoke this verse about Pūraṇa Kassapa in the Buddha’s presence:

“In injuring and killing here,
in beating and extortion,
Kassapa saw no evil,
nor any merit for oneself.
What he taught should truly be trusted,
he’s worthy of esteem as Teacher.”

2.30.s: Atha kho sahali devaputto makkhaliṁ gosālaṁ ārabbha bhagavato santike imaṁ gāthaṁ abhāsi:
2.30.e: Then the godling Sahalī spoke this verse about the bamboo-staffed ascetic Gosāla in the Buddha’s presence:

2.30.s:
“Tapojigucchāya susaṁvutatto,
Vācaṁ pahāya kalahaṁ janena;
Samosavajjā virato saccavādī,
Na hi nūna tādisaṁ karoti pāpan”ti.
2.30.e:
“Through fervent mortification in disgust of sin he became well restrained.
He gave up quarreling with people.
Refraining from false speech, he spoke the truth.
Surely such a man does no wrong!”

2.30.s: Atha kho nīko devaputto nigaṇṭhaṁ nāṭaputtaṁ ārabbha bhagavato santike imaṁ gāthaṁ abhāsi:
2.30.e: Then the godling Niṅka spoke this verse about the Jain ascetic of the Ñātika clan in the Buddha’s presence:

2.30.s:
“Jegucchī nipako bhikkhu,
Cātuyāmasusaṁvuto;
Diṭṭhaṁ sutañca ācikkhaṁ,
Na hi nūna kibbisī siyā”ti.
2.30.e:
“Disgusted at sin, an alert mendicant,
well restrained in the fourfold constraint;
explaining what is seen and heard:
surely he can be no sinner!”

2.30.s: Atha kho ākoṭako devaputto nānātitthiye ārabbha bhagavato santike imaṁ gāthaṁ abhāsi:
2.30.e: Then the godling Ākoṭaka spoke this verse about various sectarian teachers in the Buddha’s presence:

2.30.s:
“Pakudhako kātiyāno nigaṇṭho,
Ye cāpime makkhalipūraṇāse;
Gaṇassa satthāro sāmaññappattā,
Na hi nūna te sappurisehi dūre”ti.
2.30.e:
“Pakudhaka Kātiyāna and the Jain ascetic,
as well as this bamboo-staffed ascetic and Pūraṇa:
Teachers of communities, attained ascetics,
surely they weren’t far from truly good men!”

2.30.s: Atha kho vegabbhari devaputto ākoṭakaṁ devaputtaṁ gāthāya paccabhāsi:
2.30.e: Then the godling Veṭambarī replied to the godling Ākoṭaka in verse:

2.30.s:
“Sahācaritena chavo sigālo,
Na kotthuko sīhasamo kadāci;
Naggo musāvādī gaṇassa satthā,
Saṅkassarācāro na sataṁ sarikkho”ti.
2.30.e:
“Though the wretched jackal howls along,
it never equals the lion.
A nude liar with suspicious conduct,
though they teach a community, is not like the good.”

2.30.s: Atha kho māro pāpimā begabbhariṁ devaputtaṁ anvāvisitvā bhagavato santike imaṁ gāthaṁ abhāsi:
2.30.e: Then Māra the Wicked took possession of the godling Veṭambarī and spoke this verse in the Buddha’s presence:

“Those dedicated to mortification in disgust of sin,
safeguarding their seclusion,
entrenched in form,
they rejoice in the heavenly realm.
Indeed, those mortals give correct instructions
regarding the next world.”

2.30.s: Atha kho bhagavā “māro ayaṁ pāpimā” iti viditvā, māraṁ pāpimantaṁ gāthāya paccabhāsi:
2.30.e: Then the Buddha, knowing that this was Māra the Wicked, replied to him in verse:

2.30.s:
“Ye keci rūpā idha vā huraṁ vā,
Ye cantalikkhasmiṁ pabhāsavaṇṇā;
Sabbeva te te namucippasatthā,
Āmisaṁva macchānaṁ vadhāya khittā”ti.
2.30.e:
“Whatever forms there are in this life or the next,
and those of shining beauty in the sky,
all of these you praise, Namuci,
like bait tossed out for catching fish.”

2.30.s: Atha kho māṇavagāmiyo devaputto bhagavantaṁ ārabbha bhagavato santike imā gāthāyo abhāsi:
2.30.e: Then the godling Māṇavagāmiya spoke this verse about the Buddha in his presence:

2.30.s:
“Vipulo rājagahīyānaṁ,
giri seṭṭho pavuccati;
Seto himavataṁ seṭṭho,
ādicco aghagāminaṁ.
2.30.e:
“Of all the mountains of Rājagaha,
Vepulla’s said to be the best.
Seta is the best of the Himalayan peaks,
and the sun, of travelers in space.

2.30.s:
Samuddo udadhinaṁ seṭṭho,
nakkhattānaṁva candimā;
Sadevakassa lokassa,
buddho aggo pavuccatī”ti.
2.30.e:
The ocean is the best of seas,
and the moon, of lights that shine at night.
But in all the world with its gods,
the Buddha is declared foremost.”

3.1.s: Evaṁ me sutaṁ— ekaṁ samayaṁ bhagavā sāvatthiyaṁ viharati jetavane anāthapiṇḍikassa ārāme.
3.1.e: So I have heard. At one time the Buddha was staying near Sāvatthī in Jeta’s Grove, Anāthapiṇḍika’s monastery.

3.1.s: Atha kho rājā pasenadi kosalo yena bhagavā tenupasaṅkami; upasaṅkamitvā bhagavatā saddhiṁ sammodi. Sammodanīyaṁ kathaṁ sāraṇīyaṁ vītisāretvā ekamantaṁ nisīdi. Ekamantaṁ nisinno kho rājā pasenadi kosalo bhagavantaṁ etadavoca: “bhavampi no gotamo anuttaraṁ sammāsambodhiṁ abhisambuddhoti paṭijānātī”ti?
3.1.e: Then King Pasenadi of Kosala went up to the Buddha, and exchanged greetings with him. When the greetings and polite conversation were over, he sat down to one side and said to the Buddha, “Does the worthy Gotama claim to have awakened to the supreme perfect awakening?”

3.1.s: “Yañhi taṁ, mahārāja, sammā vadamāno vadeyya ‘anuttaraṁ sammāsambodhiṁ abhisambuddho’ti, mameva taṁ sammā vadamāno vadeyya. Ahañhi, mahārāja, anuttaraṁ sammāsambodhiṁ abhisambuddho”ti.
3.1.e: “If anyone should rightly be said to have awakened to the supreme perfect awakening, it’s me. For, Great King, I have awakened to the supreme perfect awakening.”

3.1.s: “Yepi te, bho gotama, samaṇabrāhmaṇā saṅghino gaṇino gaṇācariyā ñātā yasassino titthakarā sādhusammatā bahujanassa, seyyathidaṁ— pūraṇo kassapo, makkhali gosālo, nigaṇṭho nāṭaputto, sañcayo belaṭṭhaputto, pakudho kaccāyano, ajito kesakambalo; tepi mayā ‘anuttaraṁ sammāsambodhiṁ abhisambuddhoti paṭijānāthā’ti puṭṭhā samānā anuttaraṁ sammāsambodhiṁ abhisambuddhoti na paṭijānanti. Kiṁ pana bhavaṁ gotamo daharo ceva jātiyā navo ca pabbajjāyā”ti?
3.1.e: “Well, there are those ascetics and brahmins who lead an order and a community, and tutor a community. They’re well-known and famous religious founders, deemed holy by many people. That is, Pūraṇa Kassapa, the bamboo-staffed ascetic Gosāla, the Jain ascetic of the Ñātika clan, Sañjaya Belaṭṭhiputta, Pakudha Kaccāyana, and Ajita of the hair blanket. I also asked them whether they claimed to have awakened to the supreme perfect awakening, but they made no such claim. So why do you, given that you’re so young in age and newly gone forth?”

3.1.s: “Cattāro kho me, mahārāja, daharāti na uññātabbā, daharāti na paribhotabbā. Katame cattāro? Khattiyo kho, mahārāja, daharoti na uññātabbo, daharoti na paribhotabbo. Urago kho, mahārāja, daharoti na uññātabbo, daharoti na paribhotabbo. Aggi kho, mahārāja, daharoti na uññātabbo, daharoti na paribhotabbo. Bhikkhu, kho, mahārāja, daharoti na uññātabbo, daharoti na paribhotabbo. Ime kho, mahārāja, cattāro daharāti na uññātabbā, daharāti na paribhotabbā”ti.
3.1.e: “Great king, these four things should not be looked down upon or disparaged because they are young. What four? An aristocrat, a serpent, a fire, and a mendicant. These four things should not be looked down upon or disparaged because they are young.”

3.1.s: Idamavoca bhagavā. Idaṁ vatvāna sugato athāparaṁ etadavoca satthā:
3.1.e: That is what the Buddha said. Then the Holy One, the Teacher, went on to say:

3.1.s:
“Khattiyaṁ jātisampannaṁ,
abhijātaṁ yasassinaṁ;
Daharoti nāvajāneyya,
na naṁ paribhave naro.
3.1.e:
“A man should not despise
an aristocrat of impeccable lineage,
high-born and famous,
just because they’re young.

For it’s possible that that lord of mankind,
as aristocrat, will gain the throne.
And in his anger he’ll execute a royal punishment,
and have you violently beaten.
Hence you should avoid him
for the sake of your own life.

3.1.s:
Gāme vā yadi vā raññe,
yattha passe bhujaṅgamaṁ;
Daharoti nāvajāneyya,
